reviews.author: Tom Mason
reviews.text:
My wife of 49 years is a current resident of a Sage Oak property, having moved in last November. I could not be more pleased with the quality and professionalism of the care she receives! There are only 8 residents in the home, and there are always 2 fully qualified caregivers on location 24/7. My wife suffered brain cancer in Jan 1998, and although the cancer has never returned, her physical and cognitive abilities have declined with aging. And for the last 2 years she has not been able to use her legs or Rt arm, and her speech and memory have deteriorated. She requires constant care and assistance with all daily living functions.

Sage Oak has provided incredibly good care of my wife. They get her out of bed daily for meals at the dining room table and social time in the den. The caregiving staff is attentive, friendly and helpful. They receive fresh food deliveries several times a week, and prepare nutritious hot meals 3 times a day. In addition to caring for the personal hygienic needs of my wife, they clean rooms, bedding and personal laundry on a regular weekly schedule. With our 6 children and 9 grands, and my work, church, exercise, high school support and college support activities, we are blessed to have the professional staff of Sage Oak to care for my wife! Thanks for providing the care that you do! --tm

reviews.author: John Kirk
reviews.text:
My mother is currently at Sage Oak and loves it. It’s a warm, nurturing home rather than a facility. I live in another state, but mom raves about the staff treating her like family, especially the house manager Alicia and the nursing director Juanita.

Mom has decided she wants to stay long-term versus moving back home. This was always my hope because Sage Oak does for mom what she can’t do for herself. I strongly believe mom will be around a lot longer because of the level of care provided - Sage Oak makes sure she goes to all her doctors’ appointments, eats healthy, and has human interactions.

9/19/24 Update
Mom has been at Sage Oak for almost three years! In April she moved to Michigan for two weeks, hated it (largely because she missed the food at Sage Oak Aberdeen & her caregivers :)), and promptly moved back to Sage Oak.

The owners were flexible and accommodating-moved her into Sage Mockingbird until a room was available at Aberdeen. I have had the benefit of comparing similarly priced retirement communities. The other communities are nice and clean too.

The main differences I have witnessed are much more human interaction/love/caring; almost zero wait time when mom needs help with something, and food (institutional vs home cooked/personalized nutrition).

I have access/timely response to/from the ownership (Seth), the head of nursing (Juanita), and the house manager (Candy).
I came in town last week for mom’s birthday and took her to North Park Mall and her caregivers had her all dressed with her hair, makeup, and nails done - see picture. She’s happy at Sage Oak and I can’t thank them enough for all they do.

reviews.author: Parks
reviews.text:
It's difficult to put into words how much this place means to me. My Dad has multiple conditions that make living alone at home untenable. He is a proud and strong man who has achieved a lot in his life and leaving the home he has known was difficult.

The change that has occurred in the 2 weeks since he came to the Landon has been like the dawning of a new day! Even in the context of "independent living" there is SO MUCH support here! Breakfast with the gang in the morning, supervised exercise and engaging classes in the early afternoon, field trips to wherever the consensus decides, cars available for reservation for errands, the quiet environment, capable security, chef prepared meals, on-site exam room for doctor visits, on-site salon, and the welcoming atmosphere for family and friends are just a few of the many features.

It is like Dad was "awakened" and is much more engaged in life, is happier, and spreads joy to to others! The support has turned back his clock by years!

If you have the means for this place, it will be a bargain to offer your loved one a space here. I look forward to my own eligibility for residence here!

reviews.author: Daniel Garner
reviews.text:
The NUMBER ONE criteria for a place for my mother to live - even more than first class tangibles (like The Forum has) — is the Heart of the Staff and the Staff’s Leader. Here, the Forum gets 10-Stars, not just 5.

My parents moved to the Forum in 2013. My Dad passed away in 2017. My mother has continued and continues to thrive and flourish - and enjoy life and living - at The Forum, now 9 later and almost 13 years since first moving there.

EVERY member of the The Forum’s Staff - the Executive Director, Sonia Nix, and the front office, the Receptionists, the Executive Chef, Paul Glassman (who is a world class chef and consistently provides top quality dinning) and the dinning room staff, the activities, lifestyle and well-being staff, the limousine drivers, house cleaning staff,Maintenance staff, Security staff, “Happy Hands” assistance staff, the Ageility physical therapists on site, the Salon on site, are Angels who do what they do as a Calling... THEY are the heart and soul and fabric of The Forum. They care personally about each resident. And they also care about and are welcoming and attentive to residents’ family members (and as a result, we know and love ‘em all).

A lady from another top institution of excellence once told me that before considering anyone for employment, she first talks to them by telephone. “If I can’t feel their smile over the phone, I tell them this isn’t the place for them”. And so it is especially as to Heart) for The Forum.

My experience is likewise for the other residents at The Forum. They are friendly, welcoming, genuine... no pretentiousness.

My mother has made many, many dear friends at The Forum, who - along with The Forum’s Staff - enrich her life daily.
My mother has always been wise. Never more so than when she selected The Forum.

reviews.author: Bailey C
reviews.text:
PLEASE READ WHEN CONSIDERING THE GROVE FOR YOURSELF OR LOVED ONE. I am not just a family members loved one but also in the medical field.

If I could give the grove a negative score for my mother's care, I would. If you or your loved one require assistance with mobility (especially getting in and out of bed), assistance in showering, assistance with medications I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS PLACE.

12 days after moving into this facility my mom, who was healthy and only needed assistance with getting out of bed, was admitted to the hospital for failure to thrive, a urinary tract infection (not shocking due to the amount of times we found her sitting in her own urine) and delirium from not taking her medications correctly. My family checked on my mom almost every single day and it was very common to find her sitting in her own urine each morning. We had a meeting with Shri shortly after my mom was admitted and expressed we felt she needed a higher care level since THE GROVE had originally chose level one FOR HER (by someone who isn't even medically trained and before even evaluating her) but we were told that higher level of care wouldn't be possible until a 30 day period of observation. My mom didn't even make it 30 days in this facility, she made it 12 days before her doctor at a routine appointment made her go to the emergency department where she was admitted for failure to thrive, a urinary tract infection and delirium (something I wanted the grove to help us out with but was met with resistance about waiting 30 days) I almost lost my mom because of those 12 days. Before she came to the grove she was getting out of bed on her own, dressing herself, showering herself and just 12 days later we have lost any progress she made in skilled nursing. I have regret that I allowed my mother to "live" in this place and fully believe they have significantly worsened her cancer treatment course and accelerated her physical and mental decline because of how weak she is now and the delirium we are still dealing with. And of course there was no negotiating any return on the $6000 we spent for them to watch our mom fall into failure to thrive, bacterial infections and delirium while she was there. It's almost as if they refused to let us pay more for a "higher level of care" so that this would happen, she would leave and they could keep the money without doing any of the work.

Also of note, her room didn't even a working fan in the second bedroom and they let her toilet sit with feces for 2 days before getting it fixed. They'll make you promises to get into this facility but once you are in they dont seem to hold up their end of the contact.

If you or your loved one really requires care and attention, DO NOT SEND THEM HERE.

reviews.author: emily laible
reviews.text: I’ve seen a real positive shift in my Mom’s daily life since joining The Grove. The staff are consistently warm, patient, and attentive, taking the time to get to know each resident and tailor care to individual needs. There’s a true sense of community—friendly neighbors, engaging activities, and nutritious, well-prepared meals that brighten every day. The living spaces are comfortable and clean, with thoughtful safety features that provide peace of mind to families. Most importantly, my mom feels respected, independent, and genuinely cared for, which brings our whole family relief and happiness. I’d highly recommend The Grove to anyone seeking compassionate support, dignity, and a vibrant, safe place to thrive.

reviews.author: Wendy Holden Carey
reviews.text:
First, I want to acknowledge the obvious: the grounds, décor, and overall facility are top notch. Everything visible is well maintained, modern, and beautifully designed. It truly is a stunning property that creates a welcoming environment for residents and families.

As for the staff, my father was in the skilled nursing facility (“health center”), and like many SNFs, they appeared understaffed for the number of patients they serve. Unfortunately, that seems to be common in healthcare facilities today. Despite that, the staff was generally personable, caring, and professional. They took very good care of my father, and he genuinely enjoyed both the food and the physical therapy services.

The only negative experience we had involved a staff member stealing my father’s leather duffle bag. It was reported, but nothing ultimately came of it, which was disappointing. Receiving his medication on time was a challenge but we did work that out.

Overall, while there were some concerns, my father received good care and had a positive experience during his stay.

reviews.author: Susanne Jefferson
reviews.text:
After spending the past eight weeks after getting a total knee replacement at The Villages of Lake Highlands, I can honestly say that my experience has been exceptional. I don’t usually write reviews, but the outstanding care and kindness I received from everyone on the staff deserve to be recognized.
From the day I arrived, every single person treated me with compassion, respect, and genuine concern for my well-being. During my entire stay, I never encountered a single employee with a bad attitude. That alone says a great deal about the culture of this facility.

There is a physician and a nurse practitioner who do rounds every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Both of them were never in a rush to listen to my concerns and issues with my recovery- and I had quite a few in the beginning. They even came to the PT area to make sure nobody was left out. That was truly amazing to me! The nursing staff provided excellent care and always made me feel safe and well looked after. Whenever I rang the bell in the painful stages of my recovery, someone showed up in a very timely fashion. Whenever they didn’t, I knew it was because they were busy taking care of someone else, not because they didn’t care. The physical therapy team was encouraging, knowledgeable, and truly invested in helping me recover and regain my strength. The housekeeping staff kept my private room spotless and comfortable, making it feel like a home rather than a medical facility.
The kitchen staff went above and beyond to make sure I had meals I enjoyed. They were always accommodating and often prepared something extra when I needed it. It was clear that they genuinely cared about making my stay as pleasant as possible.
I was also impressed by the administration and leadership. Whenever I needed something, they did everything they could to make it happen. Whether it was a special request or simply making sure I was comfortable, they always responded with kindness and professionalism.
What stands out most about The Villages of Lake Highlands is the people. Every department—from administration and nursing to therapy, housekeeping, dietary services, and everyone working behind the scenes—works together with one goal: providing the best possible care for their residents. Their compassion, patience, and genuine love for the people they serve are evident every single day.
Recovering away from home can be difficult, but the staff made me feel cared for, respected, and valued throughout my entire stay. They consistently went above and beyond to ensure I was comfortable and had everything I needed.
I am deeply grateful to everyone at Villages of Highland Park for their dedication, kindness, and exceptional care. I would wholeheartedly recommend this facility to anyone looking for a place where residents are treated with dignity, compassion, and genuine concern. Thank you all for making such a positive difference during my recovery.

reviews.author: Renardis Banks
reviews.text:
As a healthcare administrator in the Navy with over 30 years of experience in the medical field, I have a very high standard for clinical coordination and operational excellence. Moving a loved one between skilled nursing facilities is always a complex undertaking, but when you add the logistics of a 300-mile relocation and the critical requirement of dialysis chair coordination, the margin for error is zero.
The team at Villages of Lake Highlands rose to the occasion during a particularly demanding season of my life. While I was navigating a major career transition, they provided the steady hand I needed to ensure my father’s care remained seamless.
Several key staff members deserve individual recognition for their dedication:
• Cameron (Administrator): His leadership is evident in the facility’s culture. He went above and beyond by sharing his personal contact information, ensuring I had a direct line of communication during the move. This level of accessibility is rare and deeply appreciated.
• Cynthia (Business Office): She was instrumental in navigating the financial complexities of long-term care. She worked diligently to transition my father to a Medicaid bed, which eliminated the burden of private pay costs and provided our family with immense peace of mind.
• Yvette: Assisted with the daunting task of coordinating the 300+ mile transfer and the specific dialysis requirements.
• Tiffany: Her support throughout the process was invaluable, contributing to the overall sense of teamwork that defines this facility. She engaged every step of the way and ensured that every "i" was dotted and every "t" was crossed for his arrival in Kerrville. I’m forever grateful!
If you are looking for a facility in Dallas that understands the nuances of complex medical needs and treats families with genuine empathy, I highly recommend Villages of Lake Highlands. They don't just manage patients; they support families through difficult transitions.

reviews.author: Deborah Blocker
reviews.text: Meadowstone Place has a wonderful “crew”!! Jeremy is caring and a great administrator. “Z” is the best❣️❣️She spoils us all and is one of the most caring people I’ve ever met. She is a real jewel. Cathy goes out of her way to be helpful and kind and organized. reviews.author: Joy Denley
reviews.text:
My mom lived in Meadowstone Place for 13 years. For her first years, everything was really good; however, for quite a few years after that there were a number of changes in their staff. Sadly, we saw much of the property decline and they also lost much of their personal touch. In August 2026 they got a new Director, Jennifer Daniels, and she has brought it back to a 5 start retirement complex! Mom absolutely could not say enough great things about Jennifer and when I met her via a phone call I began to understand why! Jennifer not only is a great administrator but she also genuinely cares about the residents under her care!! In just a short time property improvements were being made, maintenance issues addressed in a timely manner, and even more importantly, she was forming relationships with the residents. "Community" is a powerful word and one that we all desire. I know Jennifer has to have a very full plate but from the first day mom met her she was so excited to call me and tell me how personal, friendly, and caring she was! Mom commented on how one of the first things she did was move her desk so she could always see what was going on in the lobby and her door was always open to visit. Mom was 95 when Jennifer arrived and she finally began to feel listened to and understood. Mom's sole desire was to never have to move away from Meadowstone! Jennifer brought mom a renewed hope in the physical facility, but even more importantly she gave mom a source of security and trust when mom needed it most! I live out of state and Mom began to not feel very good. On December 16th, mom text my sister and I, "Please call the office and ask Jennifer to come up here. I do not feel safe alone." Mom had several friends at Meadowstone and a granddaughter close by but she wanted Jennifer! The only two people that mom would receive advice from is her primary care physician and Jennifer! I made it to mom later that evening and took mom to the ER the next morning. Jennifer stayed in close contact with our family over the next few days and mom celebrated her first Christmas with Jesus! Jennifer was so tender and caring and even helped us navigate moving mom's things out and closing that 13 year chapter of her life.
There is another person at Meadowstone Place that is also one-of-a-kind! I do not know her formal title but Kathy in the office is priceless. She is so sweet, tender, and genuine and always had a way of making mom know that everything is going to be okay. Kathy was always readily available, and on top of all the moving parts at once, yet provided a calm atmosphere regardless of any chaos that may of been transpiring. Kathy was a gift and a huge blessing at Meadowstone Place during their many transitions that mom could always count on being there. Although I live out of state, Mom kept my sister and me well informed of everything going on and when we visited things were always exactly like she described to us.

Besides Jennifer and Kathy being so exceptional there were a few other things that made her never want to move away. She loved that she could see out her front and back windows/doors and see activity throughout the day. She loved that she wasn't inside one big building and that she was out and walking around outside safely at any time. She also joined others playing Bingo, Mexican Train, and other games almost every day! She enjoyed special events and group activities. She built friendships and never felt alone. She even got her greatest desire, to never have to move out of Meadowstone Place!

In March of 2026 my mom moved into her cute 1 bedroom apartment with all the support and care she needs.

From day one, I have only had wonderful and positive experiences with the PVN staff, options, facilities, resources, and services. I feel a sincere and strong connection with everyone on the campus and I know my mother is in loving and caring hands.

The Serenity Prayer teaches us accept the things we cannot change, courage to change the things we can and wisdom to know the difference. I feel so fortunate for the serenity, courage and wisdom we all had when we chose PVN as our mother’s new home. The PVN community will never replace our family, but I honestly feel we have just expanded our extended family to include PVN as we join efforts to support my mother and provide her with an excellent and comfortable quality of life.

Thank you PVN!
Dr. Michael Adams
Son of Nancy Adams

address: 10754 St Michaels Dr, Dallas, TX 75230, USA
description: Manchester Care Homes St. Michaels is a residential care home in Dallas, Texas. Operating in a residential neighborhood, it provides high-ratio caregiver care, specialized memory support, private rooms, and personalized dining services.
researchSummary: Verified location as a Manchester Care Homes residential care property.

reviews.author: Christian
reviews.text: Even though my dad was at Manchester for just a few months, we always felt like we were treated as family by Brian, Sandi and the entire staff. My dad received wonderful care, and I would recommend Manchester to anyone who is looking for a place for their loved one.

reviews.author: Cindy Wolken
reviews.text:
I had my mom at the St Michaels house for a little over a year – while there were some good moments, overall, it was a very frustrating and exhausting experience. In my opinion, the management/sales team promises a lot of things but really fail in the delivery.
1 – When we moved in the house it was full of residents – sometimes mom had to wait upwards of an hour for personal needs to be taken care of (she was bedbound) - I had to hire additional caregivers for my mom to ensure her basic needs were being met in a timely manner.
2 – Attention to detail lacking – many times mom would call me because she needed something and her call button was hanging beside the bed nowhere within her reach – so I had to call the house to go and take care of what she needed and to put her call button within reach. I found some staff to be reactive instead of proactive. Many times I would enter the house and find some caregivers sitting in living room on phone yet when I went to mom’s room she needed water or something else.
3 – Med problems –
A - there were several times mom got meds that were not part of the current approved list (discontinued, etc)
B – there were times mom didn’t get meds that were on her approved plan
C – There were times that meds would arrive from the pharmacy but not get entered into the system for a couple of days
D – when it came time to use items in the comfort kit they discovered it had expired - I believe that is something that should be routinely checked – we lost several days having to order a new kit and get it entered into the med system.
E - after my mom passed, the house failed to notify the pharmacy and accepted a med THREE days after my mom’s passing rather than rejecting the med when it showed up.
4 – shortly after moving in they told me mom could only wear gowns because the pajama pants were “too hard on the caregivers to change” - but even with wearing the gowns there were many times they left the gown bunched up around her waist making mom uncomfortable and causing red places on her skin.
5 – they ruined a piece of mom’s furniture – stripped the finish off by placing something on top of it – and said they could “buff it out” – the finish was gone.
6- the house itself was nice but the floors were filthy – when the youngest great grandkids would visit their clothes and shoes were black from the floor being so dirty. I requested carpet cleanings but it isn’t something they did regularly.
There are some incredibly nice and competent people working at the house and some people who don’t really care to be there. If you have a loved one who is very independent, truly needs very little help, and likes a quiet place this might be a good fit for you – but if you have a parent of loved one who needs extra care this house is definitely NOT the right fit in my opinion – even with hiring additional help.

name: The Tradition-Prestonwood Assisted Living & Memory Care
address: 5555 Arapaho Rd, Dallas, TX 75248, USA
description: The Tradition-Prestonwood Assisted Living & Memory Care is a high-end senior living community in Dallas, Texas. It offers personalized assisted living care, memory support, fine dining, physical fitness programs, and 24-hour staffing.
researchSummary: Verified Tradition Senior Living property location on Arapaho Road.

reviews.author: Anonymous Reviewer
reviews.text:
My father pays nearly $10,000 per month to live at The Tradition, and the quality of care and services has declined dramatically.

Over the past few years, many of the employees who genuinely cared about residents have left or been fired, and it shows. Seems like they are trying to push out the only sincere people they have left.

Residents are constantly being charged extra fees and nickel-and-dimed despite the enormous amount they already pay. For 10k a month I don't think my father should be charged a fee to have a subpar meal from the dining room delivered to his room when he's not feeling well. I mean come on!!!

One of the most frustrating examples is the condition of the facilities. For a community charging residents thousands of dollars every month, basic amenities like working laundry equipment should not be an issue.

I've also witnessed staff entering residents' rooms and handling personal belongings in ways that made families uncomfortable. Items have reportedly gone missing, and concerns raised by residents and families often seem to go unresolved.

The people living here are elderly and deserve dignity, respect, safety, and properly maintained facilities. Families trust this community with their loved ones and pay a premium price for that trust.

Before committing to this facility, I would strongly encourage families to spend time talking with current residents and their families about their experiences. What's advertised and what's actually being delivered can be very different. I will be looking at other options for my father but wanted to warn others before thinking about this place as an option for their loved ones.

reviews.author: Sharon VanderDrift
reviews.text:
My husband was on the Memory Care floor of the Tradition for 2 months. He decidedly did not want to be there. Two individuals in particular eased his troubled state while he was there....
Bernadette, a care partner, listened attentively to every concern he had and always responded in a helpful way. She is quiet and gentle and caring. She made being in Memory Care more bearable for my husband.
Judy, a nurse, was another presence on the 4th floor who eased my husband’s anxieties in his unsettled state. She was always cheerful, smiling, and laughed easily. She brightened every room she went into.
These two ladies impressed my family with their kindness, their appealing personalities, and their genuinely caring manner.

reviews.author: Angie Garcia
reviews.text: I came in to this unsupervised facility. The patients were running a muck. I am an Uber driver. I came to deliver a package that apparently was pain medication for a hospice patient. She was waiting in her wheelchair chair by the entrance. I could not get in the door. She signaled to me to push the door in. When I finally entered, she saw the package I had and it had her name on it. She said she had been waiting for a day and a half for this medication. She asked me to leave it with her and I just couldn’t. I asked if anyone was in charge and she said “ no one works on the weekends. And for the few here that are working are all at lunch” . A woman finally came up to me and explained my reason for being there and she said- everyone is at lunch. A gentleman came up to her with a trach tube, and asked her to adjust his tube. She said hold on- she was texting. People all over the place in their wheelchairs and staff eating while walking up and down the hallway. Just a horrible sight to see. I know no one will care. But these people are human. They deserve better. I know it’s hard to find people, good people to work here or any assisted living facility..... man, this just breaks my heart. I don’t know. Humanity has left the building!

reviews.author: SHINOJ MATHEW

researchSummary: Verified identity as Duncanville Senior Living in Duncanville.

reviews.author: Joan Spanne
reviews.text:
My loved one has been at this facility for some time, longer than any staff member there. As a whole, the facility staff do a great job on individual care. They also work well with hospice staff, coordinating when things need to change for an aide’s vacation and such, watching to see that routines are followed. Raven, the nurse supervisor (not sure of her exact title), has the care staff well coordinated and working effectively together. Rashidat, longest on staff, knows the residents’ habits, likes, dislikes, all of it, and gives top notch care, interacting with residents’ families to be sure the residents have what they need. Jennifer, another longer term staff on day shift, also provides excellent care. My loved one has a bond with them and great confidence in them, which matters a lot for peace of mind. Since I work 8-5, I interact more with afternoon-evening shift staff, seeing my loved one daily. Tyeisha and Chelsea, afternoon/evening med techs, are careful and caring. Julia, Jackie, Nisha, Whitney, Taliyah, (I am sure I am missing someone I should remember), each one I have full confidence in. Family events, such as the recent Thanksgiving party, bring out the best in fun interactions between caregivers and residents, and Margie, the chef, always shines (the best Italian creme cake!)
The building always smells clean when I walk in, and my loved one’s en suite bathroom is kept very clean. Common areas are kept clean and are seasonally cheerful but not overdone. Room temperature control is a problem during the heat of summer, though they made a change this summer that seemed to improve conditions. I might wish for the carpet to get cleaned more often, or dusting once in a blue moon, but in the things that really matter to my loved one’s well-being, they do their jobs well and with kindness and humor. With the current management and staff I have no hesitation recommending Duncanville Senior Living.

reviews.author: Cindy Langermann
reviews.text:
My housemate’s mother is in the Duncanville Senior Living Center and has been the resident who has lived there the longest (8 years plus). It has been a good facility for her over these years and is only a five minute drive from our house. She has received good care through the years by the facility both by management staff and the caregivers. Raven, the nurse, is responsive to the needs of the residents and jumps in to help staff if needed. Rashidat has been a faithful, personable, caring and efficient caregiver at the facility for a number of years. Jennifer also is a great caregiver on the team helping our loved one getting up in the morning and feeding her since she is bedridden. Tyeisha is careful as the Med Tech and jumps in to help in
hands in caring for the residents. Chelsea also does a great job in giving out medications to the residents. Neisha, Esther, Julia, Jackie, and Whitney, during the afternoon shift are cheerful and interact with the residents while also providing friendly assistance to each one of them. They care deeply for the residents and carefully provide what they need and treat them with dignity and respect. Margie, the cook, provides wonderful meals for the residents and takes into account dietary restrictions. She bakes wonderful desserts such as Italian cream cake for special occasions and has a great sense of humor, willing to work long hours when needed. With the current management and staff I have no hesitation recommending Duncanville Senior Living.

reviews.author: stacey nemanic
reviews.text:
The facilities at CC Young are very nice and clean, but staffing, documentation, and communication were significant concerns during my mother’s stay.

I researched rehabilitation facilities and chose CC Young for my mother while she recovered from pneumonia, with a major goal of strengthening her lungs. She did not receive an incentive spirometer until seven days after admission, when I asked during her care meeting whether she was using one and learned that it had not been provided.

During another update, the nurse practitioner told me my mother was doing well and did not need oxygen. When I asked for her oxygen levels during physical and occupational therapy, I was told they had not been documented. When I asked how they knew her levels had improved without documentation, I was told that staff said they had.

Getting information was extremely difficult. I sent multiple emails, made phone calls, and escalated my concerns without receiving responses. After my mother was discharged, her home-health provider never received the required orders from CC Young. We ultimately had to take her to her primary care physician to obtain new orders.

In hindsight, I would not have sent my mother here.

reviews.author: Victoria Rheams

reviews.author: Jennifer McFarlane
reviews.text: After almost two years of talking with the diector, mother's residence was less than 3 months. Mom was still recovering from shoulder surgery and was told she should not use or pull on the bad arm. Some caregivers continued. Near the end, when we began hospice/comfort care, she was to always have 2 people lift her. Mother's room would be left unlocked and other residents would enter her room from early morning to night.We kept requesting it be locked. It continued to be a problem. Then one evening, on camera, I witnessed mother being treated poorly, "man handled" and ignored, even as she screamed in pain. The caregiver was ultimately terminated and the community was told this was their last chance. By end of the next day, another resident entered her room alone, rifled through things at her dresser, with his pants down, showing his bare rear, before closing himself in her bathroom (see photo). Later that evening, she was once again lifted by one person, pulling her up by her bad arm. We promptly moved her. Sad thing is, I emailed all of the videos, to the corporate director, of the above mentioned and have heard nothing back. Yes, the facility is lovely and clean and there are a few amazing caregivers, but that is where it ended. For the price charged, I would never recommend this community. My best to anyone who experiences the stress of placing an aged parent into care.

reviews.author: Christina Jones
reviews.text:
Hope Springs Memory Care restored my faith , renewed my weary heart, and allowed me to finally trust someone else to help care for my sweet Dad. By the time I found it we had already been through another very large multi-care facility. Hope Springs is small enough to be focused on Memory Care, the staff is trained JUST for dementia patients. It made a HUGE difference for my Dad. The changes in him were apparent after only 2 days. Hope Springs is structured completely differently than any Memory Care facility in the DFW area, and I know because I looked at almost every one of them. They keep the rhythms of a person with dementia in mind the entire day & night. It has a secure outdoor back yard for sunshine. In fact the whole building is light filled, not a dimly lit corridor in the whole place! They have scheduled activities that they actually do, not just say they do like the previous one my Dad was in. The food is homemade & cooked in the kitchen onsite w/ fresh ingredients.
But THE MOST IMPORTANT thing is the staff. I have laughed with them, cried with them , and consider them each my family. Miraval, Elizabeth ,Zee, Beverly, Elayna , and the rest of my Dads caregivers made my Dad feel loved & comfortable. He smiled all the time. He was treated with respect & dignity. I could not be more grateful to each & everyone of them.

reviews.author: Misty Hoyt
reviews.text:
Though I was confident on every level that moving my dad to a memory care facility was the right decision, it was the worst day of my life. However, I was eventually comforted by knowing we selected the right home-away-from-home Dad deserved.

It started with the education. Whether we chose Hope Springs (Bader at the time) or elsewhere, the staff was a wealth of knowledge. From why carpeted floors are imperative to knowing what the staff-to-resident ratio should be to official programming empowered us to ask the right questions and ultimately choose the best care for our family's superhero.

Seeing the good in bad:
— Our Big John always thrived on interacting with people. Bam! New friends, who we now consider family. New faces for John to ask "How are you doing?" (really wanting to know), give a wink to, tell "I love you" "You're pretty," and even pull a prank on.

— Our family was able to share our husband/dad/grandpa with more people. The heart and soul of John's personality was obvious to the caregivers, staff, residents and other families at HS.

— Our family was treated with kindness, respect and patience, as we navigated unfamiliar territory (which was always changing).

— A team of people who understood him and what he was going through.

— A group of professionals who not only catered to his needs, but also loved him (I am 100% certain) like their own father. I mean, he is easy to love.

— He was treated with the grace and dignity he deserved.

— Through programming and intimate conversations, we were educated and guided through this process with knowledge, compassion, hand-holding, hugs and prayers.

Though Dad didn't really participate, our family and the other residents enjoyed stellar programming and activities.

There's just one thing I would change:

I would love to see a culture where the caregivers receive the same kindness, support, and compassion they extend to the residents.

reviews.author: Sheila Gilliam
reviews.text:
If you’re looking for a memory care community where compassion isn’t just a word but something you see every day, I cannot recommend Silvermark Memory Care in Plano enough. The level of service and care they provide consistently exceeds expectations.

Carrie, the Executive Director, leads with genuine kindness and compassion. She truly cares for each resident and pours her heart into supporting families through what can often be a difficult journey. Her dedication creates an environment where residents feel valued and families feel supported.

The caregivers and team members—including Amari, Bri, Jazmin, and Kyselene—are exceptional. They are always engaged with the residents and their families, bringing patience, warmth, and joy to every interaction. You never get the sense that they’re simply doing a job. Instead, they are committed to enhancing each resident’s quality of life with dignity, respect, and genuine affection.

I also believe this culture of excellence starts at the top. Owners Nik and Dee have created an organization where the promises made to families are truly honored. Their commitment to maintaining high standards is reflected in every member of the team and in the exceptional care their residents receive.

Silvermark is a place where families can have peace of mind knowing their loved ones are surrounded by people who truly care. That kind of heartfelt dedication is rare, and it deserves to be recognized.

reviews.author: Inez Westrom
reviews.text:
I previously had my husband at another facility, and unfortunately, he did not do well there. The residents were not closely monitored, and medications were not administered in a timely or structured manner.

I toured many places in Fort Worth, Colleyville, and Southlake before making a decision.

When I visited Grand Brook Memory Care, I immediately noticed how happy the residents seemed and how clean the facility was. It felt welcoming and well cared for, and there was none of the unpleasant odor you sometimes find in senior living communities.

The caregivers there are truly angels on earth. They are so kind and compassionate with both the residents and their families. My husband was younger than most of the residents, so at times he could be more active and a bit challenging, but they always knew how to handle him with patience and understanding.

At Grandbrook in Grapevine the staff and caregivers have been there for many years (5 + years) unlike other memory care facilities which shows stability.

Felicia, the cook, is incredibly caring, and her food is delicious. She has been there 20 years. Her partner, Aida, is just as wonderful. Nurse Grace is highly experienced and attentive, and the medical technicians are knowledgeable and compassionate. Precious, Tenisha, and Marian all have amazing attitudes and so much patience. Ruby is energetic and full of life. Every single one of them always knew exactly what to say when our family became emotional.

The staff and caregivers truly make all the difference in the world. I cannot say enough good things about Grandbrook!

reviews.author: Mark Haynes
reviews.text:
I had to place my wife into dementia care about 3 years ago. I thought that a large skilled nursing facility in Fort Worth would be best for her. I was very disappointed in the level of care they gave my wife and other residents. I decided to move my wife to a different memory care community and visited 15 different places. Grand Brook stood out as the best place for my wife.
I am so thankful that I was led to Grand Brook of Grapevine to care for my wife. It is a warm, safe and peaceful home-like environment that provides compassionate care and love for the residents. My wife was there almost two years, and I was thankful the entire time that the Grand Brook team was caring for her until her passing.
Everyone from the executive director, life-enrichment manager, culinary manager and team, nursing, med techs, maintenance, housekeeping and caregivers are dedicated to caring and providing for all of the residents. They are welcoming and care for the loved ones of the residents also. It is a small community, and I believe that is the main reason for their effective caregiving.
Their caregiver staffing level is sufficient to cover the needs of the residents, and they do not hire temporary caregivers from agencies to fill in. That allows the caregivers to really get to know each resident and their individual needs. A lot of the staff have been working there for many years. It indicates that it is a well-managed and caring place to work. It is family owned, so it is not subject to ownership changes that occur in many of the corporate owned facilities.
If you are looking for a peaceful and safe home-like environment that provides care and love for your loved one, visit Grand Brook at Grapevine.

reviews.author: Barbara Gentry-Schantz
reviews.text:
I am not surprised to see that they have removed my review. My Mom was at Brookdale in 2017, she had Alzheimer’s and the Doctors told me it was time to place her in a home for safety reasons. At first it seemed nice, I would notice things like they were not bathing her properly and cleaning her room well. I would say things and tried to give them a chance to correct this.

I saw a huge change in Mom after a few months, long story short when her medicin bill came this month they had changed her from 5 medications to 21 medications. I stayed home from work that day to look them all up and found they were mostly giving her anti psychotics!! This explained why such a change.

I met with the Director and Doctor and could not have been spoken to any worse than they did. To add insult to injury I found the doctor on the internet and she was under inditement with a local Hospice agency for over medicating the elderly. Once they do this you usually loose them within a few months. It was so awful we moved her that night to Twin Rivers. Twin Rivers tried so har to get my Mom back, they were fantastic however it was to late and we lost Mom 2 months later.

While talking to the Brookdale Director and Doctor they had the nerve to get nasty with me and say well you did not take good care of of your Mom, she had a kidney infection and pneumonia when you brought her here. Yes she had a kidney infection, I had taken her to the doctor twice to treat this and she was on her second round of medication. As far as pneumonia I had her at the hospital just before taking her to Brookdale and I was NOT told that she had pneumonia but it appeared they just wanted to sling mud and blame me??? Please beware of this, when has a nursing home been given permission to decide when someone dies. I will check this site once a year and continue to repost this review until I am no longer here. I love you Mom, Signed Barbara Gentry

reviews.author: Serena Hicks
reviews.text: It's heartbreaking when you realize your loved one requires Memory Care. I chose Brookdale after shopping many places. Brookdale was the obvious choice for me and my very loveable (and challenging because he's super smart but also now brain injured) Dad. I have no complains only praise for the entire staff at this facility. They worked quickly to get his room ready. They send me pics of him enjoying social activities and games with his friends. It's so hard to know he's not at his home of 45 years. It's SO comforting to know this home is a safe, social and caring place for him to enjoy the rest of his life.

reviews.author: Stephen White
reviews.text: A very close friend of mine that I have known for over 40 years was recently moved by her family caregiver from a senior living facility in the Mesquite area to the Cambridge Court Mesquite facility, memory care section. My first visit to this new facility was conducted a few days ago on her 92nd birthday. I found my friend very alert, responsive, and she stated that she loved this new home. I have never seen her this alert and talkative for the last several years. She was never like this in the old facility. In walking from the front desk to the memory section, the staff were very supportive to helping guide me. They were all very alert and involved with the residents that were outside their rooms having fun watching TV in the hallway. This was not like my visits to my friend in the other facility. Those hallways were usually empty with closed doors. Although the room is smaller than her prior facility room, she stated that she likes it much better. She sat up from the bed when I entered (never did that in the old facility) and we talked for over an hour. There is something in this facility that has made her happy. I was impressed.

reviews.author: Mylora Frazor
reviews.text: Cambridge Caregivers has been a blessing for my parents and myself. I was hesitant to bring caregivers into our lives, had an appointment to meet with Rachel, our coordinator, in April 2025, March 2025 our world fell apart, I contacted Rachel, she met with Dad and myself that day, the following day caregivers were in place along with contacts for hospice. I cannot express how much our caregivers have provided for our family. Our family started off with 12-hour daily shifts 7-days a week, contacted Rachel for night care, in 24 hours our 12-hours care moved to 24/7 care for mom then couples care in September 2025. Each caregiver has compassion. I did not fully understand the value of consistency caregiving until December 2025, when meeting with the Hospice Nurse, our caregiver was able to give more detailed information than I could provide, extremely valuable information for the Nurse and myself; I work fulltime, fill in the holes for my parents, I cannot be with them 24/7. My family’s journey is not unique, familiar for each caregiver. Our decision to inquire about caregiving, what it would look like for our family, was the best decision I made for Dad and again for both. There is comfort in knowing all their needs are taken care of daily, especially when I travel.

reviews.author: Michaele Vardy
reviews.text:
Our loved family member was a resident at Oak Ridge Alzheimer’s Special Care Center, and our experience raised serious concerns. Prescribed medication critical to managing his Alzheimer’s symptoms was reportedly not administered for approximately three weeks. During that time his condition worsened, and he suffered a fall requiring an emergency room visit and stitches. Further, the facility required us to hire private sitters at our own expense while they were “adjusting” the medication that they reportedly failed to administer.

Despite a physician’s order and repeated reminders, the facility failed to consistently provide a soft diet. I also frequently found him in wet bedding and soiled clothing.

I was informed he was left unclothed and shivering because he was “refusing” care. Our expectation of a memory care facility, specifically marketing themselves as an “Alzheimer’s Special Care Center,” would have staff who are trained and able to redirect and assist cognitively impaired residents, not leaving them vulnerable and suffering.

Families should carefully evaluate staffing, training, and medication management here.

reviews.author: Emily Deeb
reviews.text:
If you are looking for the worst dementia care in DFW you have found it.

First off, I am a retired medical doctor. This facility provided disgraceful care for my brother. From the director of the facility, down to the people who are “supposed” to do the laundry, to the people who dispense medication NO ONE CARES. He did not receive his most important medications to prevent hallucinations for 3 WEEKS and this resulted in him hurting another patient and then himself after a bad fall where he split his head open. During his stay here, we have found him in a urine soaked bed daily. We have arrived to poop and vomit in his bed. Several times we arrived to find him in one of the many hallways only dressed in a diaper and shivering on the floor with skinned knees and feet because he had been crawling in his diaper. How this facility is so uncaring is unthinkable. I couldn’t be more disappointed and could never recommend this place to anyone. Part of our decision to put him here was its wonderful reviews...how deceptive. Families beware

As a Senior Real Estate Specialist, I’ve had the opportunity to tour and partner with many senior living communities across North Texas and Long Creek in Sunnyvale continues to be one of the top recommendations I share with families in need of Assisted Living or Memory Care.
Unlike some larger communities, Long Creek is intentionally focused on Assisted Living and Memory Care, and they do both exceptionally well. This focused approach allows the staff to specialize, personalize, and truly serve residents with the kind of attention and compassion that makes all the difference.
What really stands out about Long Creek is the warm, family-like atmosphere. The team here is highly engaged, knows residents by name, and builds meaningful relationships with both seniors and their loved ones. I’ve seen firsthand how they support families through what can be a challenging time while providing clarity, comfort, and consistent communication throughout the transition process.
The community itself is well-kept, thoughtfully designed, and easy to navigate. Residents enjoy access to daily activities, shared dining, and purposeful engagement which is especially important in Memory Care, where structure and connection are key. It’s clear that the staff here are not just trained to care for individuals with dementia or Alzheimer’s, they are called to it.
If you’re looking for a senior care community in the Sunnyvale, Forney, Heath, Mesquite area where your loved one will be seen, known, and truly cared for, Long Creek is absolutely worth a visit. I have full confidence referring families here, and I know they’ll be met with both professionalism and heart.

reviews.text: Kristi was a Godsend. We knew nothing. Kristi was able to help us find the best place for my mom. My mom is very happy and just loves the home Kristi helped us find. If your looking for a place for your loved one, Kristi is your person for all your needs.

reviews.text:
At some point in time most of us are going to be faced with one of the most difficult decisions we will ever have to make in our life. What do we do when our parents or loved ones circumstances / health grow beyond our capabilities and capacity? While it may not be something that you want to plan or think about, if you are witnessing early signs of your parents or loved ones needing help in the future, I would strongly encourage you to lean into the discomfort and begin researching your options. The good thing is that you don't need to look any further for your source of truth!

Kristi and Dewayne Vance are the absolutely remarkable! In fact, they are the cream of the crop and have extensive experience and knowledge with Independent and Assisted Living, Memory Care, and Residential Care Homes all across the DFW area. They are intimate with the amenities, business practices and personnel at each facility and will act as your advocate to help you narrow your options and plan. They will listen to your needs and help arrange tours/visits to each facility. The best part is that you will not have to do it alone because they will be by your side every step of the way!

They have the certification and affiliation of the NPRA and treat each families situation as if it was there own.

I can't say enough about Kristi's Senior Solutions other than if you need assistance, you only need to make one call.

reviews.author: Saundra Finley
reviews.text:
Placing my mom into an assisted living facility was one of the hardest decisions I’ve ever had to make. I had promised her that I would always care for her, but it became clear toward the end that I could no longer provide her with the level of care she deserved. It was important to me to find the next best thing.

I knew immediately after touring A Caring Home with Friends that it would feel like an extension of our home for her. The facility is a wonderful residential care home with private bedrooms and areas that she shared with the other residents. I didn’t want her to get lost in a large nursing facility. The ratio of residents to caregivers is exceptional.

The administration was so helpful in helping us navigate the system of forms and hospice. Their knowledge was invaluable. Having never dealt with these things, it was overwhelming on top of all the other things our family was dealing with.

The staff were amazing with not only her physical care but her emotional well-being. They were upbeat and happy when they came into her room or worked with her. Every member of the staff is a long-term employee, and you can tell they enjoy working there and providing care to their residents. This isn't a job for them but a calling.

Our family was made to feel a part of her care with updates and lots of fun special family type events that made my mom feel special, like Thanksgiving. Christmas and birthdays.

My mom was there for over a year and as her illness progressed, they continued to provide her with exceptional care. They always treated her with dignity and love.

The final month of my mom’s life, she shared that she felt so lucky to have people who loved her and that she was very happy. I couldn't have asked for better.

reviews.author: Cyndi McCullough
reviews.text: After taking care of a neighbor for 5 years, I’ve seen the good and the very bad in places. This home was OUTSTANDING. I would put one of my parents or loved ones here without hesitation. The owners and staff are caring and competent individuals! Can’t recommend this place enough- you won’t find a better place with a low ratio of staff to residents, cleanliness and true compassion.

reviews.author: Maureen Tabor
reviews.text:
We chose River Oaks for my mom's first memory care experience. The sales team really lays it on thick, for sure. The facility itself is very nice and we have no complaints about that. Communication is an issue with them. For one of several examples, my mother fell and was taken to the emergency room. No one from River Oaks bothered to call me...I'm next door in Carrollton and they had my contact information and I was a frequent visitor. The ER is who called to notify me that they were treating my mother. She went to rehab directly from the hospital and it was weeks before anyone from River Oaks even inquired about my mother's health. She returned to River Oaks (I was very reluctant to let her go back there, but she'd already spent the $2500 community fee and had only spent about 2 weeks actually living there so it felt irresponsible to go spend even more money moving her) and she fell again shortly after her return. I do not blame them for her falls, although I do feel like they could have been more attentive to her than they were. She went back to rehab since this time she actually broke her hip. Also, she broke her hip on a Saturday and they didn't have her checked out until Sunday, which is when she was taken to the ER. At least they did communicate with me this time. She never returned to River Oaks after her hip repair.
Turnover is or at least was high last summer among the nursing staff and the people who sit with the residents in the TV room. I don't recommend River Oaks for anyone's loved one who has the slightest bit of mobility issues. They're not going to get enough attention from the staff. I understand that they don't have enough staff for one-on-one attention but with multiple falls in the short amount of time my mom was there, I feel like they could have done a little better by her.
Linda was the manager and ignored my multiple requests for a simple key to my mom's room. She was very difficult to get a hold of. I understand that she's no longer there, which is probably for the best. She was not a friendly or helpful person at all.
My sister is financial POA, and it took months to get the bills straightened out. My mom didn't even live there any longer and she was still trying to get the bill issue fixed.
Lots of good reviews on here....take mine with a grain of salt but I am a real person, not a bot.

reviews.author: Jennifer Gilbert Photography
reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Bethesda Gardens has been an incredible blessing for our family, and we are so thankful we found this community.

After multiple rehabs, hospital stays, and even in-home care for the last 6 months, my mother needed a positive place where she could truly heal, feel safe, and not be alone. This has been the perfect fit.
From the moment you walk in to the beautiful uplifting environment, you feel the warmth. Lexi, at the front desk is always cheerful with a welcoming smile. You'll see workers moving about who know these sweet people by name and genuinely seem to care about each one of them. It’s not uncommon to see staff loving on residents by stopping for hugs, holding hands and encouraging those who might have a struggle and need assistance.
The medical and caregiver teams seem to have endless patience and respect for this aging community.

We worked with Brandy from the start. She was so patient and compassionate as we worked through this emotional decision for us and our mom who wasn't looking forward to moving there. Kathy (Activities Director) connected with her immediately. She learned some details about my mom to help her find her place to fit in right away. She brings contagious enthusiasm that keeps residents active and engaged with new things to do and look forward to all the time.
Every member of the team we have met is incredible. Reyna fills the halls with joy through her housekeeping, and Izzy on the maintenance team always steps in with a helpful, can-do attitude.

Most importantly, my mother is happy! She’s surrounded by new friends, smiling again, and truly thriving. She looks forward to her daily activities which is so important for her mental health. Seeing her this content after such a difficult season of what seemed hopeless at times, has meant everything to our family.

We are deeply grateful for the love and care shown at Bethesda Gardens. They are an example of how it should be done. I don't know how they do it, but I wished this experience for anyone who is aging, in need of help with daily needs or alone and feeling a bit lost in their later years. I appreciate each and every one of these special people who work as a well oiled machine.

reviews.text:
Broadway Cityview has been a blessing from the first day my Mom moved into an independent living apartment in 2024. 18 mos later she's in assisted living and continues to tell me every time we talk how grateful she is that we found Broadway at Cityview when she decided to move halfway across the country to live closer to us.

There are a number of floor plans to choose from of independent living apts . She ended up in a ground floor 2 bedroom unit with an exterior door and a small, beautiful patio and yard. Her assisted living studio apt doesn't have the exterior entrance but has a very nice view, is large enough to comfortably fit her most important furniture and clothes while providing support that makes Mom feel safe and cared for.

There were a la carte assistance services available for the independent residents when she needed support. Marlee and her team provided 5 star service when she needed it. Joe and his team in assisted living continue the 5-star service with a higher level of care, assuring us that Mom is getting the support she needs and while making her feel looked after and safe.

There's one more element that Broadway at Cityview has created for its residents: Community. The options for gathering together with other residents vary widely and include potting plants, to building a birdhouse, happy hours with live entertainment, excursions to theatres or blue bonnet drives (they'll take them to doctor appts, as well), card games, exercise classes, and holiday celebrations. They have a community council made up of residents that meet monthly, beautiful dining rooms in both resident sections, an art room, library,and lovely green space to enjoy the fresh air and sunshine with a book or friends.

The Broadway Cityview team have provided a perfect balance of peace of mind for me that Mom is getting what she needs while maintaining some independence, safety, and privacy for her. I can't express my respect and appreciation for the facilities and the team at Broadway Cityview.

reviews.author: Sandy Green
reviews.text: My mother spent the last year of her life in an independent living apartment isolating at The Tradition before she passed. She was 88, with the onset of dementia and rarely left her apartment. She became very confused and angry. She was also diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer. I was her primary family care giver along with my sister as she became sicker and more confused by the day, eventually put under hospice care who prescribed morphine throughout the day and other drugs to manage her pain and symptoms. As adult children in our 60's, we expected the executive staff to listen and take seriously our input and concerns regarding her behavior with the dementia and being heavily medicated. They did not. My mom was not in her right mind especially at the end yet they allowed a gravely physically and mentally ill woman dictate no contact with family when she was finally taken to Hospice House to die. They also allowed a service person into her apartment without direct authorization from us after her death. They didnt bother to call personally to verify if it was ok to let a stranger in her apartment. When we finally found out she had been moved to Hospice House, all we got was one day before she died. I wouldn't recommend The Tradition if I were paid to.

reviews.text: Took a tour as looking to move my mom from KC here. What a beautiful, clean, secure, luxurious, friendly, and superb facility. Know mom will live it!

reviews.author: Cathy Graham
reviews.text:
My dad was at a large assisted living before he got worse and needed more care. Moving him was the last thing we wanted, but now he has a much higher level of care for not much more money since this is a residential group home.
Sparks is like your favorite mom and pop shop in your hometown. They know the residents very well. There is no nickle and diming them for every little service. There are not tons of policies, but they are flexible and open minded with the residents' best interest in mind.
The owner is very hands-on, so you get much better customer service. He is great with the elderly since he is patient and caring. He is not in this for the money. He is very generous with his time and resources. He returns calls and texts immediately. That is so unusual and refreshing.
He is a leader who takes initiative; you don't have to point out that your loved one needs a haircut, etc.
I just wish that he could work 24/7 since naturally his staff are not as awesome as the owner himself.
The house is very clean. I am even comfortable using the bathroom myself when I visit.
I hope always to have my elderly loved ones in caring, small group homes like Sparks.

reviews.author: Nancy Durham
reviews.text:
My husband has been at Sparks Assisted Living for three years. The staff is very good and it is comforting to know that the people responsible for caring for him truly care ABOUT him. I like that it is a small facility -- 11 residents -- with a cozy atmosphere, so the residents get more personalized attention than in a large facility. The staff is very good at taking care of any special dietary needs and my husband really enjoys the food.

Michael Sparks, the owner, is an RN and he is very proactive. He stays on top of any medical changes and keeps me informed. He is also very prompt answering phone calls and texts. He is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about his job and has a really good relationship with the residents. He understands what a difficult decision it is to move a loved one to assisted living and he makes the transition very easy. I highly recommend Sparks Assisted Living to anyone who is looking for a facility for their loved one.

reviews.text: Nicest place I ever been in, The residents are getting so much attention from the staff. We feel spoiled and don’t want to leave. We are. reviews.author: D Shannon
reviews.text:
I am writing this review to express my deepest gratitude to Christina, the wound care nurse. During a very difficult time for our family, Christina was truly amazing. She took exceptional care of my Dad and was, without a question, the best part of our entire experience at Ignite Medical Resort. Her dedication and compassion were a light during a very dark period, and we are so thankful she was there for him.

We also want to acknowledge the other nurses who cared for my Dad; their hard work did not go unnoticed. Additionally, the Rehab team appeared very skilled and professional, though unfortunately, we didn't have the opportunity to see the final results of the goals they were working toward with him.

However, I cannot recommend this facility due to significant systemic issues:

Administration: Dealing with the administration was a total nightmare. It was nearly impossible to get in touch with anyone, and the lack of communication made a stressful situation much worse.

Cleanliness: The facility was not clean. My Dad’s room was perhaps cleaned only once a week, which is unacceptable for a medical environment.

Dining Services: The food was consistently poor. Even when we pre-selected meals for my Dad, items were always missing, the food arrived cold, or it was simply unpalatable.

While Christina and the nursing staff are doing incredible work, the management and facility standards at Ignite fall far short of what patients and their families deserve.

reviews.author: Fred Soto
reviews.text: My 93 yr old Aunt required 2 weeks of 24 care and rehab after a bad fall. The Forth Worth Transitional Care Center took great care of her. She loved the rooms and the staff. They got her up and moving. Thank you so much for the great care you gave my Aunt.

reviews.author: Jennifer Ellis
reviews.text:
STAY FAR AWAY. My mom was admitted here after a long hospital stay from multiple strokes and needed attentive care. Our experience here was extremely concerning.

On her first day, her call light didn’t work, so she had no way to ask for help. This happened again the next day. Throughout her stay, it often took over 2 hours for anyone to respond. Despite being told she’d be checked and cleaned every 2 hours, there were frequent 4–5 hour gaps with no care.
We also found pills left in her bed because the staff didn’t stay to make sure she took them.

Catheter care was not done properly. I requested daily cleaning, but the unit manager, Ruth, refused and said it was "bad practice". She later developed a UTI due to this. We weren’t informed until she had already been on antibiotics for 2 days, only when I asked about her urine culture results. As her UTI condition worsened, staff (including Ruth & Director of Nursing, Fae) refused to adjust treatment, and we ultimately had to take her to the ER ourselves.

There were serious safety issues as well. She had a known blood clot in her arm, and despite clear instructions and signage, staff repeatedly tried and even used that arm for blood draws and blood pressure. It took multiple days to get her bed rails, even though she was a serious fall risk & could not walk.

The facility also had a roach issue in her room, and they "lost" over $400 worth of her clothing when washing them & refused to reimburse us.

We spent most of her stay advocating for basic care and safety. My mom mentioned often the staff was mean to her when we were not around. I would not reccomend anyone to ever go to this facility.

Their guiding motto, “Love at All Times,” shines through in every detail—the thoughtfully designed great rooms, garden room, library, and gourmet dining options all blend stunning aesthetics with practical accessibility.
The team I met was warm, professional, and genuinely passionate about creating a true home where residents can thrive, whether in assisted living or specialized memory care. It’s clear this isn’t just a facility; it’s a community built on compassion and high-quality, integrative wellness.
For anyone searching for a smaller, more intimate senior living option with top-tier care in a breathtaking location, Serenity View is going to be an absolute standout. reviews.author: Morris Family
reviews.text:
Regular nursing homes are too dangerous for dementia patients. Fortunately, there is James L West Center for Dementia Care. The care provided for our father was exceptional. Their patient to caregiver ratio is around 4-1 while your typical nursing home is going to be around 18-1 or even as high as 24-1. There’s no way a regular nurse by home can provide superior care for your loved one with such inadequate staffing.

Our stress level just about evaporated after our dad was admitted to JL West. What a relief it was to know that he was being closely monitored and so well cared for. My siblings and I visited him every day and became very fond of the staff. My best advice is to never trust the dementia care of your loved one to a regular nursing home (especially if it’s in North Richland Hills). When we moved dad to JL West (at the recommendation of our hospital case manager) we immediately noticed the superior care he was receiving. The staff was well engaged with him. Dad was happy with his surroundings and how nice everyone was to him. The staff doctor was always available to answer questions and to keep us updated on his treatment plan. JL West gave us peace of mind.

reviews.author: Shirley Martin
reviews.text: We moved my dad here after he spent time at 2 other dementia care centers. James L West has been a breath of fresh air! The physical facility is exceptional compared to most in the area. Most staff are great and the building contains caring and helpful support such as beauty shop and physical therapy.
The business office is unprofessional and poorly run. It took months to begin using the ACH information we provided before we moved in and I was getting non payment notices on his door. A "manager" had me sign a transfer form to memory care and told me there would not be an upcharge because we had given notice to leave but I did not get it in writing so of course they billed after we left. When I asked them to review the process and find the "manager" who told me we were paid and owed nothing more I got the feeling this was not an uncommon scam to get a signature. Someone from "corporate" called me and offered a discount if I just paid but that was apparently never notated either.
Takeaway is to get EVERYTHING in writing and be prepared to argue your case.
My 4 rating is for the staff who tried to make this a good experience for someone who had a hard time adjusting.
The business office overall would rate a 2.

James L West’s Home Care Program review:
Thanks to the Medicare Guide program, my husband is eligible for JLW Home Care He attends the JLW Day Program thanks to the VA. The Home Care has been a perfect adjunct to the day program. The Director placed a very capable, kind and eager to help young person with us for hours and days that flex according to our needs. Our helper is ready for anything from cleaning to shopping or transporting my husband with his walker to or from the day program. She’s honest and self-motivated. If I need to be gone, she knows to change linens, vacuum, mop, and she can set up pre-measured healthy cereal servings and dried fruit portions for the week. My husband and I greatly appreciate her consistency. She was our first and there’s been no change in caregiver. We’ve been blessed to have her help for months and will certainly continue. There’s a lot of comfort and assurance in having the same person that we can count on. She’s never late and never asks to leave early. She’s even going to help me prepare for his 75th birthday. The Home Care Program is the best thing to have entered our lives since the JLW Day Program. They say it takes a village to raise a child but it also takes a village to care for our seniors as we and they do their best to have quality in life with Alzheimer’s dementia. If you have a loved one and want help, we highly recommend that the JLW Home Care and Day Program be where you will find the best in DFW.

reviews.author: Mike Norgaard
reviews.text:
My mother had a wonderful experience at Brookdale Oak Hollow after moving up care levels from Brookdale Eden Estates a block away. At least once a week Mom would tell me how happy she was to be living there. The marketing director, Peter, got to know us and our needs and was always there for support or to answer questions and welcomed us to the community. He also helped maintain her plants and bird feeder outside her window in the beautiful courtyard.

The staff is very resident centric, and you can feel that day in and day out. She was genuinely loved and cared for by the staff. On the rare occasion where there was a concern, they were responsive and addressed and resolved issues quickly. I appreciate their dedication to what they do and those they serve.

The food quality was good and chef Tracie goes out of her way to make sure residents have food they love. My Mom lost the ability to swallow solid food in the end and they made her custom shakes daily with probiotic yogurt, ice cream and fruit and took the time to go shop individually for her culinary needs since it didn't fit into the standard bulk food orders.

I never worried about medication being given correctly and on time. The health services are top notch, and Mom had some challenging problems that needed extra attention.

Although my Mom didn't usually choose to participate, there are many activities and family opportunities to engage with the community which were always well planned and executed. Again, there was always that feeling of focus on and connection to the residents and families.

I saw 3 other memory care programs, and this was the only one that really felt like a community from the moment you walked in. The others felt more like hallways in a hospital and very institutional. Oak Hollow is the exact opposite of that and is a great choice for those with loved ones needing the level of care.

reviews.author: Julie seibert
reviews.text: Brookdale Oak Hollow is a wonderful facility all ways around. It is always tough when you have to make a decision to move a loved one to this level of care.
