reviews.author: Becky Sandefur
reviews.text:
Over the time my mother lived at Elk Creek Assisted Living & Memory Care, we experienced repeated concerns with her care, supervision, communication, and leadership. I was repeatedly assured that staff were being retrained and that improvements were being made, yet the same serious problems continued.

The most heartbreaking part was witnessing caregivers who were impatient, dismissive, and at times cruel toward vulnerable residents. I personally witnessed staff taunting my mother, speaking harshly to her, and failing to provide the attentive care and dignity every resident deserves. I also found prescribed medications in her bed that she should have taken, repeatedly had to advocate for her basic care, and watched situations where residents were not being adequately supervised, resulting in a serious injury to my mother and an ER visit for 5 staples in her head. During another visit, I witnessed what I believed to be a very concerning response to a fire alarm and visible smoke in the building. No one was evacuated and staff did not seem to know what they were supposed to do.

Instead of spending my visits simply enjoying time with my mom, I found myself constantly monitoring her care, documenting concerns, and advocating for her needs. Despite countless conversations, emails, phone calls, texts, letters, and meetings with leadership, lasting improvements never occurred.

Because I could no longer trust that my mother would consistently receive safe, compassionate care, our family made the difficult decision to move her to another memory care facility.

I sincerely hope Elk Creek makes meaningful changes. Families entrust them with the care of those who are unable to advocate for themselves, and that responsibility requires compassionate caregivers, strong leadership, adequate staffing, and consistent accountability.

reviews.author: Lily Bennet
reviews.text:
I would not recommend this facility to anyone looking for dementia or memory care for a loved one. Our family’s experience was deeply disappointing and heartbreaking.

My grandmother suffered a quite serious injury while in their care. Beyond the injury itself, we were extremely concerned by what we observed regarding the overall quality of care, communication, supervision, and attention to residents’ needs.

As a nurse practitioner myself, I have a solid understanding of the standard of care expected in long-term and dementia care settings. Based on what I personally witnessed, I believe this facility fell well below those expectations. Residents with dementia require vigilant supervision, compassion, and timely intervention, and our experience left us with significant concerns about whether those needs were consistently being met.

Families place enormous trust in facilities like this during one of the most vulnerable times in their loved one’s life. Unfortunately, our experience left us feeling that trust was not honored. I encourage anyone considering this facility to ask detailed questions, visit frequently, and carefully evaluate whether it is the right place for their loved one.

reviews.author: Alexandra Baldwin
reviews.text:
Our family entrusted this facility with the care of our mother, who has advanced young-onset Alzheimer’s disease, during one of the most difficult times of our lives. Unfortunately, our experience was deeply disappointing and, at times, alarming.

Despite accepting her as a resident and assuring us they could care for someone with her condition, it quickly became clear that they were not equipped to manage the realities of advanced dementia. Rather than working with us to identify the cause of changes in her behavior, we were repeatedly told she needed to be admitted to a psychiatric hospital.

What is most concerning is that her significant urinary tract infection was overlooked. Instead of recognizing that a serious UTI can dramatically worsen confusion, agitation, and behavior in someone with dementia, the focus remained on sending her to a psych ward.

After bringing our mother home, she received appropriate medical care and was started on the correct antibiotics. Within a short period of time, she returned to her baseline. It was heartbreaking to realize that an untreated infection—not simply a psychiatric crisis—had been contributing to the dramatic change in her condition.

The communication from the facility was poor, and we often felt that we had to fight to have our concerns taken seriously. Ultimately, rather than providing the specialized care they promised, they discharged our mother because they were unable to manage her needs.

Families deserve honesty about a facility’s capabilities and staff who look for underlying medical causes when a resident with dementia suddenly declines. We hope no other family has to experience the fear, stress, and disappointment that ours did.

We cannot recommend this facility for anyone with advanced dementia or complex medical needs.

reviews.author: Darla Sansbury
reviews.text: I want to share with everyone our family’s 3+ year experience with the Wyndham Court of Plano. We had to place my mother there in February 2023 due to a rare form of dementia. First off, the place is decorated very well, warm and inviting. It is CLEAN and WELL maintained. The food is delicious and nutritious with a variety of meals satisfy a variety of palettes. What is even more important is the care and how this facility is run. Let’s start with Shannon Garcia, the executive director. When we first arrived, she was in charge of nursing. Any medication change, care needs, or you wanted to ask questions, you were given her number and she was ALWAYS accessible. If you reached out to her, you got a call or text back that day. Now, she’s the director and nothing has changed. I can text or call her and I’ll get a response in short order. She knows every resident and is up to speed on each and every case. She staffs this facility with quality, experienced caregivers, maintenance workers, kitchen, the whole nine yards. They are patient and kind to every resident. Tony, the head of maintenance and housekeeping always goes down and turns on my mother’s tv now that she’s lost that capability, fixes every thing she may break or simply adjust her thermostat now that she’s lost those functions. We adore him. There’s not even pages to go into how precious of a man he is to my mother but to all of the residents. HE CARES. Next you have Addy. She’s head of Nursing now. She’ll call doctors to come in if she sees or is reported a problem with a resident. You can text or call her about anything related to your family members care and she’ll call you back if a phone call and conversation is the better option rather than a text. She'll text you back on any matter. Once again the point here, is these employees are accessible, will address all concerns, answer questions, or get answers for your family. Lauren, she’s simply precious. She’s kind, caring, patient, observant, and has to love what she does to care for the elderly the way she does. The dining staff help the residents who often don’t know what to do when a meal is placed in front of them. They’re patient and encouraging. The physical therapy folks are always on hand to keep these residents moving and help with any speech, mobility, and memory issues your family member needs help with. My mother is still a resident just now over 3 years. She is safe, gets her medicine on time, her blood pressure checked, assisted with daily grooming and while still maintaining her dignity and they encourage as much independence as a resident can possibly have. I’ve seen a couple of negative reviews and I’ll call them hogwash. We are a VERY involved family. We check EVERYTHING about a place to care for our mother. We are all in and out of there and we find great comfort in knowing The Wyndham Court of Plano is taking care of our cherished mom. I more than highly recommend this facility. (Call Amy if you or your family member (or parents, they offer couple living) has a need too... she is THE BEST.) All of us loved their newly renovated place and she decided to move in Dec/Jan 2020. She has found Cariad to be the perfect fit for her because actually prefers to “having her own space” and yet needed the extra assisted living support (may need memory care soon) and didn’t want us or a stranger to hover over her. She also values having a very clean room all the time, laundry services and her own kitchen for snacks or easy meals she can make in her apt. We are wwwwaaaaaayyyyy less worried about her that now that it is easy for her to enjoy regular nutritious (and tasty) meals, ensure she takes her medicine correctly (delivered to her daily with oversight from a full-time nurse on staff), and she now has plenty of interaction with other people (pre-COVID). She’s very social. Although Covid protocols have been difficult on everyone, most especially residents in assisted care of any kind, Cariad seems to have taken all the precautions necessary and I appreciate that they communicate regularly about their status. Fortunately, as of the time of this post, I’m not aware of any residents in their Plano or McKinney homes having contracted COVID. The new leadership/owners and all of their caregivers are all amazing ... making Cariad a very special place for a rather amazing price. We highly recommend that you interview with your family member/s and Amy to see if they would be a fit for you too (we would love to have more friends to join to for our Mom/Aunt to enjoy getting to know).

reviews.author: David Haack
reviews.text: The Team at The Lodge on Preston Ridge is the best in the Frisco market. Their commitment to excellence in Resident care is outstanding! Each the Team at The Lodge, goes that extra step to ensure that everyone who comes through the front door feels at home.

reviews.author: Jill Baty
reviews.text: The Lodge at Quail Park is a good senior living facility but not so good for assisted living. The food is great. The ambience on the main floor is great. Most of the staff are pleasant. And the entertainment is great! Unfortunately we were looking for an assisted living facility that would provide additional care for my father and mother. The Lodge said they would provide higher levels of care for the same locked in price as they became necessary, but I don't see this happening. My mom has minor memory issues and doesn't remember she is diabetic, incontinent, whether she has brushed her teeth, showered or washed her hair. The staff per her care plan is suppose to provide cues and assist her but if mom says she isn't incontinent because she can't remember, the staff rather than coaching her, considers this as an elderly person's right to refusal, and walks away. Texas is very different from other states when it comes to the health and wellbeing of their dementia people. My mom is incredibly easy, cheerful and if she is reminded that she needs to wear Depends or can't have 12 ounce of processed orange juice for breakfast because she's diabetic, she obediently obliges- but it's easier for the staff if she forgets. Also my dad tends to look out for his own interests rather than my mother''s, so there is no one looking out for my mom's rights. Evidently in Texas, the husband is still allowed to get his way. For example, my dad will tell the aids to leave his soiled Depends in the large open trash can for days at a time and the aids listen to my dad instead of emptying the trash daily like they are supposed to. The carpet is filthy from urine and the stench is unbearable. I don't think the shower, sinks or counters get scrubbed nor the furniture dusted. Also the facility doctor seems to over prescribe medicine. When a nurse was recently questioned about all the blood pressure meds my mom is taking, her response was, yes, your mom is taking a lot of BP meds and her BP is still not under control! It's not very logical. If the meds aren't working, it would be better to find the right meds, not give her three powerful meds that don't work. Same with her diabetes meds. Mom is always exhausted. Is it the meds? All in all it's a great place for elderly who need shelter, 3 meals a day, medicines delivered, and entertainment. Unfortunately often so much more is required...

reviews.author: Gwendolyn Peterson
reviews.text:
If I could them no stars i would. I would not recommend Prairie Estates in Frisco for respite care.

My mother is a bedridden hospice patient with stage 4 dementia, and I left very clear written instructions for her care, along with all of the supplies needed to properly maintain her hygiene, skin, and wound care. Those instructions were personally reiterated multiple times by me, my hospice social worker, and my nurse.

Despite this, staff failed to follow even the most basic care plan.

The incontinence pads I provided to protect her skin and wound were never used. Her wound care supplies were untouched. Her clothes were not changed appropriately throughout her stay, and when I picked her laundry up, she had feces all over the back of her clothing. This is unacceptable for any patient, especially one who is bedridden and unable to advocate for herself.

Her feeding instructions were ignored as well. She was not given her morning smoothie or snacks as instructed.

The condition of the facility itself was equally concerning. The hallways smelled strongly of urine, which immediately raised concern about the overall quality of care for all residents. There was visible filth, including feces on the sink and food left sitting in the common area without being cleaned.

When I arrived, my mother was sitting in a room at 64 degrees with minimal covering, no television on, and no stimulation—just isolated in a cold room with the door shut.

What makes this most concerning is that none of this was due to lack of communication. The staff was told repeatedly and acknowledged understanding her care plan. They simply did not follow it.

This was not a matter of preference. This was neglect.

I removed my mother from this facility early and will never use Prairie Estates again for future respite care. If your loved one is vulnerable, bedridden, or requires detailed care, I strongly advise looking elsewhere.

Overall so glad we chose this place.

reviews.author: Leonard Garron
reviews.text:
Was looking for that feeling of security and knowing your loved one is getting everything they need. Atria Carrollton provided that and much more. The staff is enthusiastic. The rooms are well-designed. The food is great. Plenty of activities to keep mom interested. Mom is happy and well cared for!

reviews.author: Karen Ferris
reviews.text:
The weekend and evening receptionist, Anesia, is wonderful. She always greets everyone with a smile and kind words. I enjoyed talking to her on my daily trips to Stonemere. She is perfect for the receptionist position. She is willing to help in anyway she can.

There were two CNA's that took outstanding care my husband. Tina and Victoria were excellent taking care of his needs. We need more people like these two ladies. A big thank you to both of them.

reviews.author: King Kells
reviews.text:
I'm giving two for the facility always being clean, one star for the care. Great care depends on if its after 5 pm when all managers are gone or if its the weekend those are the worst times at this place, Chris is good at making the staff step up and do the right thing problem is when he and the team are not there. Linda is good at what she does however her attitude will change if you inquire to much about your family member seems to aggravate her, BOA is a beautiful person. I will say that in the past year the food has went from great to mediocre at best. My mom was here before in 2024and my dad in 2025, and the highlight of their days was the food, the chef who was running the kitchen back then had the food on point and would make anything on the fly if your family wanted anything different. This time around it seems that the chef who was there then ( forgive me I forgot his name but he was great with a great personality) is not there anymore and now the guy running it now is maybe more of a cook, just from what my family members were telling me this time around
The food seems more of a cheaper quality either that or the people in the kitchen dont know what they are doing I was shocked when Dad main complaints was the food here but now I know why. Even the way the plates looked back then was 100 times better. Guess that's what happens when you spoil people with a real chef then replace them with a average cook. Seems alot of frozen foods at stonemere nowadays. However I would still recommend stonemere for the care and services, therapy is awesome!!! But be prepared to order door dash for your loved one or to bring them meals evey now and then. Sorry just being honest guys.

name: Tribute Senior Living - Assisted Living & Memory Care Facility
address: 190 N Preston Rd, Prosper, TX 75078, USA
description: Tribute Senior Living is an assisted living and memory care facility located on North Preston Road in Prosper. The community features evidence-based care design, specialized memory care programs, personal care services, daily dining, and organized social events.
researchSummary: Verified as an active senior living community in Prosper, Texas.

reviews.author: AC Cervantes
reviews.text:
I’m disappointed with the memory care experience here. The facility itself is beautiful and has a lot of potential, and it may be a good fit for senior living or for residents with very mild, docile Alzheimer’s symptoms. However, in my opinion, it is not equipped to function as a true memory care facility.

Memory care residents can have a wide range of needs, behaviors, and levels of decline, and this community does not seem to have the staffing, experience, or training necessary to handle that variety. Memory care takes patience, specialized training, and a deep understanding of all the different ways dementia can show up, and I did not feel that level of skill or support at the Tribute.

For families looking for comprehensive memory care support, I would strongly recommend asking very detailed questions about what types of behaviors and care needs they are actually prepared to manage. Their skill are definitely limited.

It’s honestly night and day between this location and where my father is now. In his new community, I finally see what real, skilled memory care looks like, and it breaks my heart that he didn’t have that here when he needed it most. For that reason, it feels wrong for them to present themselves as a true memory care facility. At best, they should be honest and describe themselves as a limited memory care setting, better suited for very simple, docile cases than for the real complexity that comes with this disease.

reviews.author: KarenConcern
reviews.text:
Senior Abuse can be a very Serious situation
This place isn't safe for your family members. The employees here will neglect situations and cover up negligent action and decisions made by doctors and care givers regardless of the Dangers to the Resident, whether it is assisted living or memory care. First hand witness, The House Doctors here allow Prescriptions to assist in Sedation and Control of Residents beyond safe therapeutic levels, causing residents to Decline, Fall, go into Hypotension and worse. The ambulance is always here for someone. It is obvious the lack of care exhibited when these type of problems aren't appropriately handled efficiently in these types of facilities. If only they cared. They will allow harm to your family without ever reporting it even after it has been verbally recognized by third parties. You can contact Adult Protective Services(APS) when you suspect BAD ACTORS such as these. Don't make this your story. If you care what happens to your loved one, think again before signing up to let these people have their way with you, or your family. This decision is yours.. ENTIRELY NOT RECOMMENDED!!
RUN THE OTHER WAY

reviews.text: My home in Ladera Little Elm is nearing completion, I’m very excited! reviews.author: Angie Baines
reviews.text: We've been working with Todd in Little Elm to help my in-laws purchasing a new house. The process has been super easy and Todd has been great! name: Stonefield Assisted Living and Memory Care
address: 2701 Alma Rd, McKinney, TX 75072, USA
description: Stonefield Assisted Living and Memory Care is located on Alma Road in McKinney. The community provides complete personal care assistance, medication monitoring, fine dining, specialized memory programs, and secure outdoor areas for residents.
researchSummary: Verified as an active assisted living and memory care facility in McKinney.

reviews.author: Wendy Galaska
reviews.text:
As a liaison for a hospice company, I’ve had the opportunity to visit many assisted living and memory care communities over the years, and I can confidently say that Stonefield Assisted Living and Memory Care truly stands apart.

From the front office staff to the med techs, nurses, aides, lifestyle director, and even their marketing team, everyone is consistently kind, attentive, and willing to help. The teamwork and family atmosphere are evident the moment you walk through the doors, and it’s clear how deeply they care for their residents.

One thing that especially stands out to me is the cleanliness of the community. Unlike many facilities, there is no overwhelming odor or heavy fragrances masking unpleasant smells. That speaks volumes about the level of care, housekeeping, and attention given to residents and the environment.

I also love seeing how engaged and active the residents are each time I visit. Whether in Assisted Living or Memory Care, residents are participating in games, crafts, exercises, group activities, and meaningful social interaction. The community does an excellent job promoting dignity, involvement, and quality of life.

In short, Stonefield is a community I would confidently recommend to my own family. Their compassion, professionalism, cleanliness, and resident-centered care truly make them exceptional.

reviews.author: Maria Carmen Tellez Friedli
reviews.text:
I’ve had the opportunity to work closely with this assisted living and memory care community, and I continue to be impressed by the level of care, professionalism, and compassion shown by the entire team. Emily and the staff is dedicated to creating a safe, welcoming, and supportive environment for residents and their families.

This community itself is clean, well-maintained, and filled with caring individuals who truly make a difference every day.
I would confidently recommend this community to anyone looking for exceptional senior living and memory care services.

reviews.text: I moved here a short time ago and have found that each day is better living here. The complex itself is beautiful, clean and the amenities are designed for the active senior. reviews.author: Donna
reviews.text: Just wanted to say how much my grandmother loved living here for the past few years. Would highly recommend if you are helping an elder loved one find a new home.

reviews.author: Evelyn Bailey
reviews.text: I moved my mother out of Brookdale Senior Living in early Dec. She lived there for 10 months. It was a recurring financial nightmare for me. They wanted to raise the cost of her care about every 2 months. Most of the time they backed down when I pushed back. The last three months I received outragious invoices from them. Each month Derald Powell, the director, said it was an error & he would take care of it. Mom has been moved out for a month & it's still not resolved. They auto drafted my mother's bank acct today for monies not owed. I contacted my bank & stopped the pymt. My mom was also left in her room & was only taken out for her meals. Many of the staff didn't know how to pronounce mom's name correctly after 10 months. There is also a lot of staff turnover. She's much happier at her new assisted living & spends her days in the common area visiting with other residents. I strongly advise you to avoid Brookdale!

reviews.author: Sue Baker
reviews.text: This is a wonderful community that truly cares for their residents. The residents dressed in their team colors and watched a football game. Let me know if you need more information.

reviews.author: Amber Henderson
reviews.text:
I recently toured this facility for potential relocation of my grandmother from out of state. Before scheduling the onsite tour, I spoke extensively with Lisa who was very informative and answered every question I had. Unfortunately, Lisa was out of office on the day that I had available, but the facility still accommodated me with a tour with Breanna.

I never would have known that Breanna was filling in had they not told me. She was very kind and knowledgeable. My grandmother had given me a laundry list of questions, and Breanna was very patient and informative. Each staff member or resident who I came into contact with was very welcoming and had nothing but good things to say.

Upon returning to office, I received a thoughtful follow up from Lisa to ensure everything went ok and offer any additional clarifications that I may need. During the entire process, I never felt pressured for a decision. Both Lisa and Breanna were very understanding for my unique situation and offered comfort throughout the process. My grandmother is still trying to finalize her decision and future travel arrangements, but I am very thankful for both of these ladies who made this experience easier than could be expected.

reviews.author: Victoria Hansen
reviews.text:
The staff are very good about being part of a team with my family regarding my mother’s care. The location is clean with many extra touches to make you feel at home.

It is such a difficult time for families and love ones to need any type of care..and the people at Willow Bend, Denton, do their best at resolving the changing needs for my mom in this part of her journey.

reviews.author: Craig Lindsey

I highly recommend Liberty Senior Residential Care Homes to anyone looking for exceptional care for their loved one. My mom was a resident at the Glencarin house for over two years before she recently passed away, and I will always be grateful for the love and care she received there.

I am especially thankful for Rusinder and her team. The caregivers are incredibly kind and truly treat the residents like family. They always kept me informed about what was going on with my mom and were very attentive to any changes in her condition, which brought great comfort to me and my family.

They did everything they could to keep my mom happy and comfortable. She was loved, respected, and very well cared for by an amazing staff. Her room and the entire house were always clean and well maintained.

Knowing she was in such caring hands meant the world to our family. I will forever be grateful for the compassion and dedication they showed my mom during her time there.

reviews.author: Kim Barnes
reviews.text: Finding a small group home where you know your loved one will be cared for and loved is an emotional and sometimes daunting task. Upon meeting Rusinder Baines, I appreciated her observations and insights. She invited me to tour Summertime Home and I met two incredibly giving and genuine people, Noline and Betty. The staff at Summertime Home under Noline's leadership was kind, compassionate, silly when they needed to be, communicative, and truly loving. I knew my husband was in the best possible hands. My gratitude to Rusinder, Stephanie, and all the Summertime Home caregivers.

reviews.author: Marlen
reviews.text:
Christine was incredibly rude and unprofessional throughout the entire process. I was shocked when she told me she couldn't provide even basic pricing information unless I first disclosed detailed information about my parents' financial situation. That immediately made me uncomfortable, and I wasn't willing to share sensitive financial details just to learn what the community charges.
To make matters worse, after asking for all of that personal information, Christine stopped responding altogether. The whole experience felt frustrating, unprofessional, and left me questioning the transparency of this community's sales process. Families looking for independent living deserve straightforward pricing and respectful communication—not pressure to disclose private financial information before they can even determine whether a community is affordable. Based on my experience, I would look elsewhere.

reviews.author: Cynthia Durrance
reviews.text: Pioneer Ridge Gracious Living living is redefining independent living. This beautiful community stands out with spacious residence, impeccably maintained amenities and the talented chef who delivers decadent meals. Stop by and ask for the incredibly amazing Lonnie Channing Sales Director. Lonnie will treat you to an executive style tour that just might have you ready to call Pioneer Ridge home.

I cannot thank my caregiver Diane Richards enough for her reliable and professional service care she provided me over the few months on the weekend.
She has officially made it to my “Favorite People” list.

I always looked forward to her visits. She walks into my home with a happy smile, a halo over her head, lights up a room and brings hope to me in need. She brought immense warmth, patience and genuine compassion.

Her communication is her strength (can she talk) and a contagious laugh. I’m pretty sure Diane is secretly an Angel and must possess magical laughing powers.

Her physical strength is her weakness, but she makes up with wisdom, and experience from taking care of her own parents. She always took the time to listen to my stories and kept my spirits high, even on my difficult days. A big heart and emotional support with a positive attitude.

If you’re looking for a trustworthy, skilled, and kind caregiver, look no further. I highly recommend her to anyone looking for an outstanding caregiver services.

“Kindness can transform someone’s dark moment with a blaze of light. You’ll never know how much your caring matters”

I would highly recommend First Light Homecare of Frisco for anyone that wants to enter the medical field or would like to build a rewarding career caring for the aging population. reviews.author: Stephanie Kolb
reviews.text: Can’t say enough good things about Eagle Ridge, they truly have the most caring staff and what really sets them apart is the incredible activity program lead by Carla who is the very best! Every day is filled with engaging, meaningful activities that keep the residents active, smiling, and connected which is so wonderful to see

reviews.author: Katie Green
reviews.text:
Eagle Ridge Alzheimer's Special Care CenterCare Facility, 2505 Brinker Road, Denton, TX My husband has been a resident here at Eagle Ridge for 2 years. In the beginning all the caretakers were like 1 big happy, caring family. I have gone every day to be with my husband and have watched the change. Morale is low, if you try to do the correct thing of giving a 2 week notice to transfer to one of Sinceri other facilities, the Executive Director will fire you right on the spot, which eliminates your chance to transfer to another Sinceri property. Of course all the other caretakers are watching, so they won’t be giving any notice. Another very disturbing and scary thing is we have not had a nurse at the facility for over 2 weeks. The last one survived 4 days and quit because she couldn’t work with the Executive Director. Again, I know this because I am here every day. Resident family members that only visit once a week or so, have no idea that there is no nurse for the facility. There have been many calls to corporate to make them aware of the concerns, but nothing has been done. Only thing being done is Eagle Ridge is losing more and more caretakers, the real backbone of the place. The ones who really love and care for our residents. It is sad how Sinceri has let 1 person take this place apart. I am sad and have tried to not make a knee-jerk reaction and move my husband because the caretakers here really care about the residents.

Please share this if you have time and care about this happening to our most vulnerable residents.

reviews.author: Virginia Saunders
reviews.text: My husband was a patient with Visiting Angels for over two years. During this time we had several different caregivers coming to our home with Visiting Angels. They were all good. But there was one visiting angel that stood out above the rest. Her name is Judy Moya. Judy exceeded all of my and my husband’s expectations. She was always prompt, courteous, sympathetic, kind, professional, and she genuinely cared for my husband and also for me. Judy provided knowledge ,comfort, and love to my husband and our whole family. Her attention to every detail was excellent and gave our family confidence that we were receiving the best care possible. Judy was patient, encouraging and dedicated to helping our entire family through this process. I highly recommend Visiting Angels, Judy Moya, to anyone seeking Home Health services

reviews.author: julie travis
reviews.text:
Visiting Angels helped provide care for my father-in-law in his final days. We had one caregiver (Harrison) who was absolutely wonderful. Harrison was very compassionate and caring, he went the extra 2 miles ensuring my father- in-law was clean and comfortable ( he was completely bed-ridden), and he sat by his side and held his hand even when family were not in the room. I am an RN and was very impressed with our “ Visiting Angel”. The only criticism I have is that when the charges were discussed, I was not informed that additional fees for mileage would be added to the hourly fee.
Overall we were very pleased with the service provided, and would definitely use their services if a need arises in the future.

reviews.author: Carmen Vielma
reviews.text:
Oxford Grand truly feels like home. I had the opportunity to tour the community, and I was genuinely impressed by the love and care they pour into their residents each day. From the engaging activities to the thoughtfully prepared meals—you can tell the chef puts heart and intention into everything he creates. This community is truly centered on caring for and honoring seniors.

Myesha Williams, the Director of Sales, made the experience even more special. She was incredibly patient, kind, and attentive, answering all of my questions and providing the peace of mind we all hope for when exploring care options for a loved one. Her compassion and knowledge truly stand out.

If you’re searching for a community where your loved one will be cared for with dignity, warmth, and respect, I highly recommend visiting Myesha at Oxford Grand McKinney.

reviews.author: Jeff K
reviews.text:
The Oxford Grand has literally been life changing for my mom. Living on her own was becoming difficult for her, and her health was deteriorating fast. We knew we had to make a change. We visited several assisted living facilities in the area, and the Oxford Grand was an easy choice for us. From the attentive and friendly staff to the meticulously-maintained facilities to the amazing number of activities they offer, no where else compared to what Oxford had to offer.
After just a few months at being at the Oxford Grand, she was moving much better, and she was happier than she's been in a long time. She was originally a little reluctant to move to assisted living, but now she wishes she had done it sooner.
When I asked if she's made any new friends, she rattled off at least 30 names from memory. She couldn't be happier.

name: Discovery Village Castle Hills
address: 2500 Windhaven Pkwy, Lewisville, TX 75056, USA
description: Discovery Village Castle Hills is a senior living community located on Windhaven Parkway in Lewisville. The property offers independent living, assisted living, and specialized memory care with full-service dining, fitness activities, housekeeping, and health management.
researchSummary: Verified as an active multi-level senior living community in Lewisville.

reviews.author: Rhonda O
reviews.text: My mom was a loyal tenant for almost 3 years. She passed away on April 29, 2026. We informed them on April 24th she was sick. We cleaned out the apartment totally and turned the keys in on May 5th. When we talked to Brook on April 30 she expressed her condolences and said out of the goodness of her heart she would wave the May rent since she passed at the end of the month. On May 9th I see that they have deducted $2,100 from moms account. When we called Brook to ask about it she said you have to give a 30 day notice. I explained that mother passed and there is no way a person can give a 30 day notice when someone passes. She said what she meant by explaining she would comp us “out of the goodness of her heart” meant she would comp all mom’s meals, not rent. She never once said anything about meals! I think it’s terriable business to do what they did and I will tell everyone I know to don’t even consider this place. In addition to this mom moved in Aug of 2023 and by April of 2026 they had raised the rent $500 a month, which equates to $6,000 a year. I understand leases being raised but this is a little ridiculous!

reviews.author: Laura Hubbell
reviews.text:
My father was a resident at both the independent living and assisted living buildings. While he was still active, he enjoyed independent living with it’s dining options and delicious food choices. They have in-house physical therapy with a gym and workout equipment. Housekeeping is always visible keeping the place clean and smelling good. There are a lot of activities to choose from and nice green spaces to walk around outside.
I am very grateful for the staff at the Assisted Living. The front desk, administration, food service, maintenance, and caregivers were so friendly, caring and concerned about my dad. The caregivers especially were attentive and respectful to my dad at the end of his life.
The building is new and beautifully decorated with a nice dining room and places to sit and relax which is nice, but I would highly recommend Discovery village because of the friendly and caring staff.

name: Oxford Glen Carrollton
address: 2221 Marsh Ln, Carrollton, TX 75006, USA
description: Oxford Glen Carrollton is a specialized memory care community located on Marsh Lane. Designed specifically for individuals dealing with Alzheimer's and dementia, it offers home-style pod layouts, secure outdoor areas, 24/7 care staffing, and personalized memory activities.
researchSummary: Verified as a specialized memory care community in Carrollton, Texas.

reviews.author: charles smith
reviews.text:
My MIL has resided at Oxford Glen for three years and my wife is very pleased with her care. Many of the staff have been there for a long time and feel like family. Special thanks to William, Cristina, Keisha,
Edith, Judy, Tyler, and Andreyah.

reviews.author: Priya Joshi
reviews.text: We have been blessed to find Sonoma house for mom. She has been in assisted living for almost a year and we are happy with her care. reviews.author: Scott McClenaghan
reviews.text:
My parents have been residents of Sonoma House since November 2022. While my mother was not in need of memory care, my father was so they made the decision to both reside in one of the memory care centers. The moved from Wisconsin and were both well into their 90s. While the transition was difficult, the leadership at Sonoma helped us overcome every single obstacle.
In June of 2023, my mother passed away and Sonoma was able to manage all of her end of life. They helped us select a hospice when it was time, and she was able to be in her own bed by her husband’s side, as she had been for the last 74 years. The staff in house 1 was so caring and helpful to us that our entire family now has a tight bond and considers them part of the family.
As you can imagine, after 74 years of marriage the transition for my father was more than difficult. His condition complicates the situation, but Sonoma House continues to support him and us.
Sonoma has provided us with support by helping us get involved in support groups, keeping us up to date on my father’s day-to-day activities and challenges and comforts him during the challenging times.
Moving your loved one to an elder-care facility is always a challenge. The challenges are unique for each family and they change on a daily basis. Finding a team of leaders that will put your needs and desires ahead of their own and has the experience to navigate these challenges is key. I fully endorse Sonoma House and can assure you that their leaders will work through all the challenges you face.

reviews.author: Robert Rardin
reviews.text:
I wanted to leave what is probably an unusual review.

My daughter and I toured Touchmark at Emerald Lake while searching for a new home for my mother. After visiting SEVERAL other communities, the decision became easy the moment we walked through the doors at Emerald Lake. It wasn't even close. We immediately knew we were done looking.

The community itself is beautiful. It honestly feels more like a five-star hotel more than a senior living community. But what impressed us even more was something you can't manufacture, the genuine kindness of the staff. Everywhere we went, employees greeted residents by name, stopped to talk with them, and treated them with remarkable warmth and respect. We hadn't experienced that as this level anywhere else we toured.

We were excited to put down a deposit to reserve a place for my mother and when I showed my mother the photos in her rehab facility she was just as excited to move there. What makes this an unusual review is that unfortunately, before she was able to move in, her health rapidly declined, and she passed away. She never got to experience what I have no doubt would have been an incredible home for her filled with new friendships.

All this said, I especially want to recognize Rochelle Humphrey, the Retirement Counselor at Emerald Lake. Throughout this entire process, as my mother's condition became more complicated, Rochelle showed a level of compassion that I will never forget.

Each time I updated her, she responded with genuine concern and kindness. Although I know availability at Emerald Lake is limited, not once did Rochelle pressure us for a decision or ask how my mother's declining health might affect her residency. Instead, she repeatedly asked what she could do to help our family and make our lives easier.

When I told her my mother had been admitted to the hospital, Rochelle didn't ask about paperwork or timelines. She simply literally asked if she could bring lunch to my family so we wouldn't have to worry about finding something to eat while we stayed with my mom.

That moment has stayed with me. Acts of kindness like that are incredibly rare in any industry, and Rochelle deserves to be recognized for the exceptional care and humanity she showed our family during one of the most difficult times of our lives.

Although my mother never had the chance to live at Touchmark at Emerald Lake, I can recommend it without hesitation. The kindness you experience during your tour is genuine. It isn't something put on to earn your business, it's simply who they are.

Thank you to Rochelle and everyone at Touchmark at Emerald Lake for treating my family with such compassion and kindness. We will never forget it.

reviews.author: Deborah Malinowski
reviews.text:
We had an exceptional experience working with James Weinman with iNavigate Senior Living Solutions during a very emotional and complex time for our family. We needed to find both a memory care community for my dad and an independent senior living option for my mom, and he guided us through every step with expertise and genuine compassion.

His knowledge of the different types of senior housing and local options was incredibly helpful, and he took the time to truly understand our parents’ needs. What stood out most was his sensitivity to the emotions involved, especially my mom’s feelings about making these decisions and facing two major life transitions at once.

He was also extremely attentive and collaborative, working closely with me and my siblings to ensure we were all informed and aligned while helping support my mom in making the best choices for herself and my dad. We never felt rushed or pressured, only supported.

I would highly recommend this service to any family navigating senior living decisions. It made a difficult process feel manageable, and we are so grateful for the care and professionalism he showed throughout.

reviews.author: Kathy Cummings
reviews.text: Thank you to James for helping me find a place for my mom to live!! James was very personable and listened to our needs in detail. He helped us look at different options and we found the perfect place for her. She had lived in another place for 3 years prior in assisted living and memory care at one facility. It was NOT ideal and he helped us get to a much better place and we couldn't be more happy! The whole process with James was so easy and he was very caring and nice! Highly recommend!!

researchSummary: Verified as a skilled nursing facility in McKinney, Texas.

reviews.author: Dawn McLean
reviews.text: OT and PT is excellent! Elise, Assistant Administrator, is amazing! She went above and beyond to make sure my mom’s room was just right and family could visit often. Natasha, the Social Worker, was amazing! She’s so knowledgeable and helpful! Jennie, the Speech Pathologist, was also excellent. She does so much and is very knowledgeable about the facility/services, etc. Jessie, Issy, and Marylyn were outstanding nurses! James, Faciliities Manager, was so warm and encouraging to the patients. All of the staff is extremely friendly!!

reviews.author: Jeannette Grand
reviews.text:
My loved one was transferred here from the hospital after back surgery, and I wouldn't wish this place upon my worst enemy.

Was supposed to be for skilled nursing, but "skilled" must be a loose term. Food was awful (first night was chicken nuggets and tater tots, dessert on night was mushed mandarin oranges with mini marshmallows thrown on top...what are they, toddlers?), and ringing the call button 'might' get you attention...eventually. Pain meds rarely delivered on time. Other asks go ignored or told they "have to wait for doctor orders"; finally got an enema 4 days after initial request. Diapers so heavy when finally changed, they could hardly lift them. And every complaint met with excuses. The one staff member I met that actually worked seemed incredibly overworked while others sitting/standing around chatting amongst themselves. Was supposed to be getting PT, (place we transferred to is 3x/day) but in 5 days, only got 1 full session.

Was actually told by Sam the admin that care on the weekends was much different than during the week, while my loved one was there 24/7.

Stay far, far away from Baybrooke Village! If I could give 0 stars, I would.

reviews.author: Marti Power
reviews.text: I have lived here a little over a month....I was strongly opposed to apartment living. I don’t think I can properly describe how absolutely incredible Mera Craig Ranch is. Everything I was told by the staff when I came to tour the apartments, was NOT a sales pitch. It was 100% truth. The facility itself is gorgeous. The apartments are beautiful. The staff is always there for you. The residents are friendly. I won’t elaborate anymore. HOWEVER, if you are 55+ and want an amazing place to live, come pay a visit. Guaranteed ~ you will not be disappointed! Promise🤩

reviews.author: Terry Myers
reviews.text: First I want to say how wonderful the staff was to me when I came for a tour. Helpful, attentive and so sympathetic to my needs. Just to name a few were Jordan Nash, Tanya, Tracilynn, and Christina. They all made me feel comfortable and relaxed. The grounds, the rooms and the staff at Mera Craig Ranch are excellent. I highly recommend anyone 55 and older looking for a lovely, safe and comfortable place to live, Mera Craig Ranch is definitely the one.

name: Belterra Health & Rehabilitation Center
address: 2170 N Lake Forest Dr, McKinney, TX 75071, USA

researchSummary: Verified as a post-acute skilled nursing facility in McKinney.

reviews.author: Yosheme Al
reviews.text:
My great aunt was there for 2 weeks. Here’s my honest review. It is our responsibility as loving, caring family members to visit our loved ones in these facilities as much as possible. Most of them/us don’t have the financial situation to make sure they are experiencing a more luxurious stay. The staff at Belterra did what they were paid to do. Some did better than others, that’s life. It is a basic facility to help your loved ones get the help they need to move on to the next step of their recovery. The staff is very busy. So at night time/middle of the night, your loved one may not get the immediate help that they need to get to the toilet. At the end of the day, I don’t have any real complaints. Tip: Make sure you/loved one asks the name of every staff member who enters their room. And remember you have to do your part to make sure your family is safe here or anywhere else.
I do want to give a shoutout to Jennifer! Thank you!

reviews.author: Raeshawn Wallace
reviews.text:
I had a great experience with this health and rehabilitation center. From the moment we walked in, the staff was professional, compassionate, and truly cared about the patients. The nurses and therapists took their time, explained everything clearly, and made sure my mom was comfortable every step of the way.

The rehab team was knowledgeable and encouraging, helping build confidence and real progress.

The facility itself was clean, well-maintained, and organized, which gave us peace of mind. Communication was also strong, and we were kept informed about care plans and improvements.

I’m grateful for the support and care my mom received here and would definitely recommend this center to anyone looking for quality rehabilitation and compassionate service.

reviews.text:
Del Webb’s new model park in Trinity Falls is beautifully designed and showcases eight floor plans across three elegant series — Scenic, Distinctive, and Echelon. From the cozy Alpine to the spacious Renown, there’s something for every lifestyle and stage of life.

Each home reflects Del Webb’s signature attention to detail — open layouts, designer kitchens, energy-efficient features, and optional sunrooms or extended gathering spaces. The Echelon Series models truly stand out for those wanting premium finishes and larger square footage.

The grand opening event was warm and welcoming, with model tours, food, and golden-hour photo ops. The community itself offers resort-style living, peaceful trails, and easy access to McKinney’s best amenities.

Whether you’re planning your next chapter or just exploring 55+ active adult living, Del Webb at Trinity Falls is absolutely worth a visit.

— Chelysia Young, REALTOR®

reviews.author: Melissa Hendrick
reviews.text: I was so excited to visit. Made an appointment online. Only to arrive and they didn't have record of the appointment I made online a week before. BUT...they had my info in their database (was already getting spam emails). I met with Mark (the sales guy). As soon as I shared that I would prefer to buy an already built home vs building, I was dismissed, told to find a realtor and he had an appointment waiting. Then he instructed me how to do the self-guided home model tour. Didn't give me his business card. Didn't tell me anything about the amenities or where I could go look (a map would have been nice). As a salesperson, Mark should have approached my reply to buy an existing home, with .... while that may be an option, we at Dell Webb make building the home of your choice easy. Let me show you our design studio and you can see for yourself how easy we make selecting your build out easy. It was beyond a disappointing experience and I had heard Del Webb was the best from friends who toured other locations. Of note (and surprising) there are no wood fenced homes, you are literally on top of your neighbors, less than 1/2 a football field. Would have explored this community further if the salesperson had told me if there were any lots where the back is on a greenbelt and not right across from neighbor (now that is what I would buy). Corporate if you are reading this, and there is land at this location w/o being directly behind your neighbor, please have a salesperson contact me (not Mark though). Landera and Robson Ranch next steps on my quest for a 55plus community.

reviews.author: mobile mobilebb3
reviews.text: Met Bee, the leasing agent, at Bell Tower Reserve. She has been so accommodating in showing us every apartment we wanted to look at and has answered all our questions with a smile. She even went in and took photos of an apartment for us when we couldn’t be there. We couldn’t have asked for more. She goes the extra mile. We are really looking forward to our next new home!

reviews.author: Amy Roller
reviews.text:
My mother was a resident here for three years. When she passed away, management was notified, yet no one contacted our family to explain the procedure for terminating her lease. I eventually had to ask the front desk, where I was finally told what steps were required. We followed those instructions and completed everything by the end of the month.
Despite this, we were still charged for the following month’s rent. This is where my one-star review comes in. I called, emailed, and followed up repeatedly, but could not reach the property manager. I left numerous messages and had to visit the property twice before finally speaking with her in person. At that time, I was told a refund was “in the works.”
That conversation was three months ago, and I have yet to receive anything. Since then, I have continued to email, text, and call with no resolution. It now appears I will have to make another in-person visit.
Dealing with the loss of a parent is difficult enough. The lack of professionalism, communication, and follow-through from the management at Bell Tower Reserve only added to an already painful experience. If you plan to live here, be sure to immediately close any accounts tied to the property, or be prepared for significant frustration when trying to resolve issues.

researchSummary: Verified as an independent senior apartment complex in McKinney.

reviews.author: Suzan Wright
reviews.text: I have been a resident here for a few years now, and I am happy with the actual apartment, the mgmt (Carol), & the maintenance (Oscar, in particular). Of course, I would like the rent to not be as high as it is, and the annual increases far exceed most of our ability to pay. I actually don't know what I am going to do if the rent continues to increase at the current rate. That is my biggest concern, but as far as the amenities, the floorplans, etc., are concerned, I have no real complaints.

reviews.author: Tamera Bliss
reviews.text:
Im only giving one star because they wont allow me to do zero! If you are a loved one are considering moving here, I would suggest doing your own research. Visit the property on different occansions, when unexpected. I have been coming here for over 2 years, at least 3 days a week caring for my Grandma. She pays over a $1000 in rent and anytime she needs anything fixed the lady at the front office does not like to be bothered and will take her time plus her tone is always so rude. (I'm not referring to Cheryl either) Whenever maintenance actually comes, they only partially fix the problem. They will spray paint over mold, from water leaks to cover it up, instead of replacing the wood. Because it's so good for the elderly to be breathing in mold. They have wasp nest that we've asked to have removed multiple times and I've had to personally remove them as they were never removed.

Each resident was given a notice about upcoming inspections they just had. The notices stated the residents had a certain amount of time to report any damages inside the apartments so they could have them fixed before inspections. This wouldn't be necessary, if they fixed said problem months before when they were originally reported to the office. It seems this place only cares about your money and not your family. They also have wheelchair bound residents on second and third floors, to which I asked grandma what do you do incase of a fire since you can't use the elevators? She is wheelchair bound, can't walk on her own and surely can't use the stairs, her response, "I guess I'm BBQ because they've never gone over a fire evacuation plan". They do have the fire department come test the smoke detectors, but again a smoke detector cant get my grandma down the stairs. Please do your research. We're praying this past inspection brings good updates as we'd hate to have to move her again at her age.

I feel very confident in having my loved ones residing in the care of this residence.

reviews.author: Stephanie Getreu
reviews.text: I toured Waterford on Cooper to find a memory care facility for my mother. It is hard to know from a tour how the staff will take care of your loved one. If Stockton Berrymore, Sales Director is an indication, she will be treat with the most excellent care and consideration. Stockton went above and beyond to help me.

reviews.author: Alex Hall
reviews.text: I am very impressed with how welcoming the team at Bethesda Gardens Arlington is. Denisse does a great job explaining everything that is involved with making your loved one a resident at the community. She is very helpful and thorough in making sure everything comes together when you feel ready to choose the community as home for your loved one. Barbara is very accommodating with matters related to medication management. I would definitely recommend this community for those seeking a great assisted living community!

reviews.author: roxanne nazir
reviews.text:
Most facilities only know your loved one by what’s written in their chart, and many don’t take the time to truly connect during the move-in process. It’s rare to find nurses who go above and beyond—who genuinely get to know each resident, interact with them, and treat them as individuals.

Choosing the right place for your parent isn’t easy, but when you find the right one, it’s truly a blessing. Nurse Barbara is one of those blessings. She consistently goes the extra mile, showing patience, compassion, and genuine love for the residents. Her dedication and hard work never go unnoticed.

name: Woodside Place Assisted Living
address: 2705 Woodside Dr, Arlington, TX 76016, USA
description: Woodside Place Assisted Living operates as a small residential assisted care home on Woodside Drive in Arlington. The micro-community delivers personalized daily living support, meal preparation, medication tracking, and home-like atmosphere.
researchSummary: Verified as a licensed small residential care home in Arlington.

reviews.author: Alvin Bowser
reviews.text:
Our family is incredibly grateful to the staff at Woodside Place Assisted Living for the exceptional care they provided to our dad. During the final five years of his life, he lived in several care settings, and I can honestly say that the time he spent at Woodside Place was the only period when we did not worry about his safety or the quality of his care.

The staff consistently treated our dad with dignity, respect, patience, and genuine compassion. They didn’t just meet his physical needs—they celebrated him as a person. Whether it was recognizing special occasions, spending meaningful time with him, or simply showing kindness in their daily interactions, they made him feel valued and loved.

As I recently prepared a slideshow in memory of my dad, I came across so many photos and videos of him with the caregivers. Seeing the smiles, laughter, and the tenderness with which they cared for him brought tears to my eyes. Those moments confirmed what we experienced every day—that he was truly cared for by people with servant hearts.

We especially want to thank Toyin for the extraordinary love and compassion she showed our dad. Her kindness reflected the type of Godly love and compassion the Bible speaks of. We regularly witnessed her advocate for our dad and for other residents, always ensuring they were treated with dignity, respect, and genuine care. Our family will never forget the difference she made in his life and in ours.

Choosing an assisted living facility for someone you love is one of the hardest decisions a family can make. Woodside Place gave us peace of mind during a difficult season, and that is a gift we can never repay. We will always be thankful for the care, dignity, and love they showed our dad.

If we could change one thing, it would simply be that we had found Woodside Place sooner.

reviews.author: Jennifer Crosthwaite
reviews.text: I work in the healthcare industry and I happily give Toyin and Woodside Place a 5 star review. From the immaculately clean and decorated home to the fabulous outdoor space, and safe neighborhood. Not to mention the excellent care you will receive form Toyin and her incredible staff. Searching for a place for a loved one can be overwhelming and difficult to navigate, not to mention draining on the pocket book. Woodside place is a great option for senior living that is affordable, and will give you the peace of mind that your loved one is being taken care of. Toyin can walk you through it every step of the way. Her compassion, and drive to help anyone she can is nothing short of spectacular! I highly recommend Toyin and Woodside place!!

reviews.author: Penny Stevens
reviews.text:
My mother has had nothing but problems!
1. Bedbugs! She is constantly getting bed bugs because they don’t exterminate them properly. Also residents won’t say they have bedbugs because they don’t want to be quarantined in their apartments so they continue walking around spreading them!
2. House keepers are MOT cleaning the apartments good enough plus they can’t speak English so they are unable to communicate with the residents, one even gave out my mother’s land line number and people have called on my mother’s phone! She changed my mother’s radio station to a Spanish radio station even after my mother told her not too.
3. The hallway floors still have carpet so guess what people who have bed bugs are carrying throughout the apartment complex.
4. Roaches! Like bedbugs aren’t enough?!?!
My mother never had any bugs before she moved here very very disappointed. Due to the bedbugs infestation we had had to put my mother up in a hotel, and constantly buy linen, and clothes and I will be damn if we are going to buy new furniture to be infested with bedbugs.
Do Not let your loved one move here!

reviews.text: We had a nice visit today with my former neighbor of 42 yrs. Her little apt.was very nice & all the staff members were friendly & accommodating. The entire place was spotless & all the tenants seemed to be enjoying themselves.

Karina the sales representative has been very supportive and continues to oversee her welfare long after the initial move in. She helped my loved one to see that she could fit in and be happy. Overall, the quality of care from the front desk, caregivers, and administration is top notch. I highly recommend this facility as an option for your loved one's assisted living needs.

reviews.text: I can not rave enough about Karina, Crystal and the rest of the staff here as they have all been amazing. I recently put my dad in memory care here after not working out at another facility and I am very impressed and how well they all worked together and made things happen that were probably not normal. Professional yet friendly and they definitely put the residents first. Thank yall for everything you have done so far as I know my father is in the right place.

reviews.author: Judy
reviews.text: There’s nothing like having peace of mind and confidence in the people who care for your loved one. My sister and I are so thankful we have Mom at ExcelCare. She has been in this home for two years. Prior to that, we tried two corporate assisted living facilities and a different residential home. The assisted living facilities were beautiful, but when Mom no longer could do things for herself the assistance was not readily available. Sadly, corporate facilities do not staff appropriately. We then tried a residential home. Shockingly, the owner of this home was not providing meals for the residents but was charging a fee for them. Thankfully, we were led to ExcelCare. The past two years have been wonderful. The loving care Mom receives from Alice and all the caregivers is beyond excellent! The caregivers know each residents likes and dislikes. They are treated with love, respect, and dignity. It is obvious Alice and Toyin truly love their residents. The home is always clean, food nutritious and delicious, communication easy, care is consistent and quickly available, and the mood is always positive. Our family is able to have peace knowing our Mom is in a loving environment and receives great care.

reviews.author: Andrew
reviews.text:
Angels and legends! How fortunate we are that people like Toyin, Alice, and the other caretakers at these homes exist.

My mom has been with them for about a year now after spending four years at a different group home. While her previous home was good, the improvement when she moved to ExcelCare was obvious and everywhere.

Better food. Nicer house. Better caretaker to patient ratio. Nicer bed.

But it all comes down to the people, and Alice deserves a special shout out for the HARD work she does, day and night (and sometimes middle of the night) for these residents. She does it all with a smile, a positive attitude, and an authentic love for the people she serves. We’re all lucky that the world has Alices in it.

Similarly, Toyin (the owner) is an incredible person. She’s incredibly intelligent and accomplished. She could do anything for her career but she’s chosen to dedicate herself to helping the most vulnerable old folks live lives of comfort and dignity. (And fun! She works hard to ensure there are little touches of delight in the homes.)

She’s communicative and thoughtful. And she’s made the whole process clear and trustworthy. I can’t say enough good things.

The cost isn’t cheap, but it’s also not the most expensive I’ve seen (even in the same part of town). But the cost is also extremely fair, and it’s worth every penny. Because Toyin, Alice, and the entire staff at ExcelCare genuinely offer families peace of mind. I know that my beloved mom is receiving top-quality attention all day every day.

♥️♥️♥️

reviews.author: David Dowd
reviews.text: Over the last 9 years, our hospice team has had several patients who were residents at Abiding Joy Care Home, and we’ve consistently been impressed by the wonderful care they provide. The owners, Dave & Karen, live in the home and truly treat each resident like family. It’s also incredibly rare, and such a gift, to have an RN owner like Karen living in the home and available 24/7 to provide nursing care. They create a peaceful, loving environment, and I highly recommend Abiding Joy Care Home to anyone looking for compassionate, family-style care.

reviews.author: Karla Hill
reviews.text:
On a Friday afternoon at the hospital, we were surprisingly told that we needed to place my father into a hospice care center and that we needed to find a place by Monday. But sometimes in life you get lucky, and we definitely did when a residency at the Abiding Joy Senior Care Home opened up that same weekend.

We had a great experience at “The Joy House” (our nickname for the place) and with the owners/caregivers Karen and Dave (who my Dad jokingly referred to as “Boss”). My dad was happy in his last weeks. Karen and Dave had the most accommodating visitor policy we could have imagined, allowing us to arrive whenever we wanted and stay as long as we cared to. Even better, we were given access to their swimming pool, so the grandkids and great grandkids were able to come over and swim while my dad watched. (Who has ever heard of this perk at a hospice care center?!)

The personal attention he received was exemplary since he needed a higher level of care than most (an Alzheimer’s patient that required personal feeding of soft foods). We frequently got update calls from Karen informing us of his good days, his bad days, changes in his condition, and foreshadowing what the future held, to the best of her knowledge. This allowed family that was out of town to plan trips to see my dad and spend time with him at the end of his life, while he was still in a state where he could interact with them and enjoy the visit. His time at “The Joy House” was a blessing to our family! Karen and Dave treated my dad like family, with round-the-clock medical care, but also with friendship and emotional support.

We can’t recommend the Abiding Joy Senior Care Home highly enough. They deserve the highest rating, the most stars, and - as awkward as it may sound when talking about a hospice care center - they are the first place we will call in the future should another family member require this level of care. Karen and Dave are simply the best!

reviews.author: Dahlia Walker
reviews.text:
Our family trusted New Era Assisted Living to care for my uncle for about a year and a half. Unfortunately, our experience during the final months of his life was extremely disappointing and heartbreaking.

As his health declined, he was moved to another home because we were told he would receive more one-on-one care. Despite those assurances, his condition continued to worsen. When I became concerned and insisted he be sent to the hospital, doctors discovered he was severely dehydrated, malnourished, and had multiple stage 4 pressure sores. Our family had never been informed that his condition had deteriorated to this extent.

When I asked Lillian why these serious issues had not been communicated to us, she simply replied, “I didn’t know.” That response was devastating and unacceptable.

My uncle passed away just two weeks later. While I understand that not every illness or death can be prevented, families deserve timely communication and compassionate, attentive care. We were denied both.

Based on our experience, I cannot recommend this facility for anyone whose loved one requires a higher level of care at any point. I hope our family’s experience encourages improvements so that no one else has to endure what we did.

I had a great experience with Interlochen Health and Rehabilitation Center. The staff was incredibly caring, attentive, and professional from the moment we arrived. They took the time to make sure all questions were answered and made both patients and family members feel comfortable and supported.

The facility itself was clean, well-maintained, and had a welcoming environment. The nurses and caregivers showed genuine compassion and patience, which made a big difference during recovery. Communication was clear, and I always felt informed about the care being provided.

reviews.author: Maricela Trevino
reviews.text:
I would strongly warn families to think very carefully before placing a loved one at this facility.
During my mother’s stay, there were repeated problems with transportation that caused missed medical appointments and referrals. Important follow-ups simply were not completed. Communication with staff was extremely poor, and getting clear information about her care was often difficult.
The most serious incident happened when my mother began showing symptoms consistent with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), a life-threatening condition. Instead of responding with urgency, the staff dismissed our concerns and refused to assist because we were already transferring her to another facility. We were told she “looked fine” and would be okay.
When we arrived at the new facility, the staff immediately recognized how serious her condition was. They were unable to admit her because of her medical state and quickly called 911. She has now been admitted to the hospital and is currently in the ICU.
Had we not already been transferring her that day, I am honestly afraid to think about what could have happened.
Families trust facilities like this to protect and care for vulnerable people. Based on our experience, the lack of urgency, poor communication, missed medical follow-ups, and disregard for obvious symptoms made us feel that our mother’s safety was not a priority.
Please do your research and ask hard questions before trusting this facility with the care of someone you love.

reviews.author: dennis redwine
reviews.text:
Mom went to Arbrook to recover from surgery and an extended hospital stay that left her too weak to come home.
Arbrook staff were very caring and the whole place was full of positivity and helpfulness.
The leadership was very supportive of patients, family and staff.
Folks like Eric, the admissions director, Paulette, just one of the very attentive and kind nurses made me feel very confident and comfortable about my mom’s care.
Mom got PT, OT and ST a couple of times a week and started walking to lunch and dinner which helped her recover even more and faster.
All that said, nursing and rehab facilities have a very hard job and with so many ailments, injuries and conditions not everything is perfect to every patient’s liking.
For example, mom shared a room with a stroke victim who was quite vocal as she struggled with terrible hallucinations.
I brought mom headphones to watch TV in peace and earplugs for sleeping.
Full disclosure, I went to see her most days for 6 hours a day.
So I saw a lot and I think it was a very well run, responsible, attentive and happy place.

reviews.text: My sister was in this facility and I definitely would NOT recommend it to anyone! She ended up staying there because of surgery after a fall and was completely bedridden. I would stay in the room with her for at least 5 hours at every visit and no nurses/aids came in to check on her the entire time I was there except to bring her meals. She also acted like she was afraid to be there. She is now deceased and my heart is broken. Just wanted people to know if you have a loved one that goes into Hospice care at Arbrook, check on them often. The other people that left 1 as a rating on their reviews were all correct. I would give them a zero if I could. I do have to say that there were probably 2 aids/nurses that seemed kind, but most didn't act like they cared about any of the patients. I don't know who governs these facilities but they need to check them more often for the patients sake.

reviews.author: Dian Darr
reviews.text:
Update added April 1, 2026

An update to my previous review- I recently read the review of Wendy B and was so surprised to read such a vitriolic review of the place my husband thinks of as home where he has found nothing but comfort and security during the almost two years he has been there. I can’t imagine that Wendy B was describing the same place. The staff is the most dedicated, caring group I have ever seen. My husband is on over 20 pills per day and would have seizures if they were not administered properly. Țhe only problem with meds I have ever seen happened a few evenings ago when I was there. A resident was screaming at the attendant that she wanted her meds immediately. He calmly explained that he had to do them in order and would be to her soon. She just kept screaming at him.This brings up an important point- if we as family members are told our resident is acting out, screaming, going in other’s rooms, etc. we need to take responsibility for these actions and either get meds adjusted or move them to a higher care/memory care unit. This facility is Assisted Living and they go way beyond what they have to do to make the residents happy and safe.
Another attack that Wendy B made was against our nurse who is the hardest working, kindest person I have met. I have seen her working hours and hours on paperwork, medications, vaccination clinics, and attending to her many residents who love her. The unkind remark about her being on social media was laughable, I am there several times a week and always stop in for a visit with the nurse. I can’t imagine her being on social media- maybe Wendy B saw this during the nurse’s lunch or her break. I really wonder how she even knew this about the nurse especially enough to comment that her social media was “immature.” One time when we were late getting transferred back to Brookdale from Rehab, the nurse stayed with us several hours that evening to complete all the intake and to make sure his meds were all transferred. Brookdale’s management amazes me. The Director is hard-working, kind, and caring. The new Activity Director has added such joy and enthusiasm to the group. I am thankful everyday that my husband has the privilege of being at home at Brookdale Richland Hills. When you are making the decision about placement of a loved one, go visit the facility several times and see the residents. At Brookdale you will see happy, comfortable, safe residents.

My original review:

Making the decision to place a loved one in a care facility is one of the hardest decisions one can face. I visited nine facilities until I entered Brookdale, Richland Hills, and felt immediately at home. As we made this transition, every question or challenge we had was answered by the staff with kindness and a solution. The one thing I never considered was how much my husband would improve. He has now been here for a year, and has such good friends who look after each other. The happiness and friendships he has developed at Brookdale have enhanced his life so much. The staff is so kind and caring. I do not know what we would do without them.

reviews.author: Shaneque Armstrong
reviews.text:
Our family’s experience with Oxford Glen was unacceptable and deeply disappointing.
Our loved one passed away on 11/27/25, yet his account was still drafted on December 1st, after his death. During this time, our family was grieving and managing funeral arrangements out of state. The funeral took place on December 6th, and the remaining personal belongings were retrieved on December 10th.
Despite these circumstances, we were informed that only a partial refund would be issued because items remained in the room for a short period following his passing. The director justified this decision by referencing a policy signed prior to move‐in, showing little consideration for the realities of loss, travel, and funeral planning.
Accounting later advised that refunds can take up to 90 days. We are now 93 days past that timeframe, and no refund has been issued. We were recently told we must continue waiting for checks to be cut, possibly not until the end of the month. This ongoing delay is unreasonable and unacceptable.
Most concerning is the complete lack of compassion, urgency, or accountability shown throughout this process. This was not merely a billing issue — it was a failure to treat a grieving family with basic dignity and respect.
Oxford Glen should seriously reevaluate how it handles end‐of‐life situations and financial matters involving deceased residents.
