reviews.author: SHAWN COOK
reviews.text:
Not long ago, VIP Living Center in Irving TX was for our family a safe haven in a storm. Having suffered inadequate care at other facilities brought about an intense focus on our part to find a satisfactory provider for mom during her recovery from multiple health issues. Bing and his staff truly exhibit what is described in detail on their website. The explanation of services and attitudes are entirely accurate with no exaggeration. Many older people are set in their ways and may find any change to their lives unsettling, but this care home masterfully covers all the critical issues with first kindness and then a complete and genuine regard for comfort and cleanliness. Safety and a pleasant atmosphere are not lacking in any regard. Professional respect for the staff by management is evident and allows each member to be at their best when interacting with resident patients. We were more than comforted to experience the large windows of access for visitation and never felt as we were not welcome or that anything was being hidden from us regarding the true level of care provided regularly. Mom recovered in part I believe due to the high quality of care provided at VIP Living Center and she was able to return home. Should another incident occur or when we reach that final season of life when a care facility is necessary, we only hope that Bing and his staff will be available to receive us with the same diligent and loving methods we experienced for many months. Last but not least is that we found Bing himself to be a hands on manager and therefore fully aware of the true nature of care being provided. He chooses to be available and introduces pleasant gestures of kindness as a an unexpected surprise to the staff and residents which always brought about good cheer to people doing their best to deal with life and hardships.
My sincere thanks and gratitude to Bing and staff.

First the people that run this place really do try their best for the residents. They do have rules in place for the safety of all. The grounds are well kept and the amenities from the fishing / turtle feeding pier, to the pool, to the game room and music room are first class. There are events for the residents nearly every week and right now there is a non-denominational Sunday service held in the "Big Room." The residents can add some personal touches as well to the hallways and exterior patio's.

This is a fine place for active seniors or even those a bit more senior, that still want to live their life their way!!

As of this review July 3, 2018, the construction going on around the Chateau is very disturbing. At this point the impact is dust and dirt everywhere. Still that isn't the fault of the Chateau. I guess that is just progress for this part of Irving, TX.

reviews.text: Everyone was so kind and patient with me during my stay. Felicia and all the nurse aides were there for me when I needed assistance with anything including small things like a cup of ice or extra pillows and blankets making my stay more comfortable. Physical therapy had me feeling stronger each day and really cool machines to help with the recovery including a virtual tours spanning from U.S. cities to overseas and European cities. My favorite was pedaling in San Francisco along pier 39 in the Fisherman’s Wharf with Alcatraz island and the Golden Gate Bridge in the background. They have a great team of occupational, voice and physical therapists. Housekeeping came daily to sweep, mop and emptying trash receptacles. The meals were always hot, delicious and different every day. I didn’t eat fish before my stay here and have since then changed my opinion about it. I know how silly it may sound but they always used real plates and silverware and everyone knocked before entering the room and those things make a difference in my opinion. I can’t elaborate how much they have invested in your experience here, it is not just a place where you are placed in a room and forgotten. Thank you Noel and Angela you have a wonderful staff and facility dedicated to helping people. The doctors and nurses made sure I didn’t miss any medication and worked with social services to complete my employer’s required documentation allowing me to focus on my recovery. I personally want to thank Donna and Erika from social services for helping make sure my employer got all the paperwork they needed during my recovery. I would recommend Villages on MacArthur to my friends and family members and to you should you need it. Susan the front desk receptionist brightens up everyone’s day with her smile as she greets you when you pass by and a sweetheart in activities will come to play card games like uno with you in your room during your stay. No one wants to see their parent have to go into a long term facility, but my mother has been there for about 5 months now and I really could not be more pleased with the facility and the care she has received. The nursing staff and aids have been really good with my mom. Overall everyone there has been very friendly and very attentive to my mom's needs. She has had very good physical therapist that have worked with her and they have a done a really good job with her. I would also love to give a shout out to the activities director and all the staff that help arrange activities for the residents. It's very important for these residents to have something to do and keep them busy. These love one's lives have changed so much after entering a long term facility and having daily activities to look forward to and keep them busy makes such a big difference. They just put on a prom party a few weeks ago that was a big success. The residents got to dress up and enjoy a live band and refreshments. It was really moving to see the smiles on their faces! The staff really put in a lot of hard work and time to pull off such a nice party. It meant a lot to all these residents and their families and I want to say thank you!! We really appreciate all the extra work you guys do to take care of and our love ones. I must also point out all the hard work the kitchen and dining employees do daily to keep everyone fed. They really do a good job keeping this many people fed 3 times a day 7 days a week. I am there a lot and they are always friendly and don't hesitate to change a dish if my mom's does not like it or want's something different.
So in closing, I really am pretty happy and satisfied with where mom is, even if i would rather have here home with me. It is very important to feel comfortable and feel that my mom is at a place where I know she is safe, happy and being taken care of.
One last thing! The place is very clean. They are always cleaning and mopping the hall ways. I have never walked in and noticed a bad smell. That is a big deal with me!!

reviews.text: had a wonderful experience with Toni at Avir Irving. From the moment I spoke with her, she was incredibly patient, knowledgeable, and compassionate. reviews.author: JENNIFER COX
reviews.text:
I would not recommend Avir Irving Nursing Home to anyone who cares about their loved one. My aunt was transferred there after major surgery for a 21-day stay for physical therapy, and the level of care she received was unacceptable.

She was not given physical therapy daily as ordered by her doctor, yet staff documented in the system that she was receiving it every day, which is simply not true. She developed a severe rash from being left in soiled diapers for long periods. When the call button was pressed, it often took hours for anyone to respond. The only time staff seemed attentive was when family members were present and actively complaining.

The professionalism of the staff was extremely poor. One tech aide was openly rude and spoke to me with a bad attitude, even telling me to move multiple times. Director Katrice Lee was informed of our concerns several times and repeatedly said she would follow up, but never once did.

The social worker, Mariam, was also unhelpful and misleading. She told us my aunt’s oxygen would be ready upon discharge, but when my cousin arrived to pick her up at 6:30 p.m., he was told he had to arrange it himself. Mariam insisted my aunt had to leave due to insurance, even without oxygen, saying she would be fine. Meanwhile, the nurse on duty stated they could not safely release her without it.

We also raised concerns with a man who said he was in charge of the facility. He promised to follow up with my uncle, but never did.

Basic care was neglected. My aunt went two weeks without a bath—her hair became matted and smelled so bad that I had to wash it myself in her bed. Only after my uncle complained at the front desk did aides finally give her a bath. Additionally, a night shift nurse was overheard speaking negatively about my uncle to staff, unaware he was sitting nearby.

The facility itself was also concerning. We saw roaches in the restroom, and it was common to hear other residents crying for help with no response from staff.

The only positive experiences we had were with a few male RNs and one male medication tech. Aside from them, the care was consistently poor, unprofessional, and neglectful. It felt like once insurance coverage became an issue, the priority shifted to pushing patients out rather than ensuring safe and proper care.

I strongly urge others to look elsewhere when choosing a facility for their loved ones.

reviews.text: Such a pleasure to meet Harriet the new activity director . She planned an amazing mother’s day event for the guest , The flower wall was beautiful and the resident really enjoyed it

reviews.author: Bradley and Anne White
reviews.text:
Perspective residents beware! Read the contract always! There’s been a recent change in ownership, and there are changes they aren’t being forthcoming about. My mom and I worked with Angela in marketing to move into a cottage for well over a year and a half. We even had a cottage finished out, and my mom was ready to sign the dotted line. We finally received the contract less than ONE week before move in, and there were several differences from what Angela told us vs the actual contract. We were told that the standard yearly rate increase was 3-5%, which is industry standard. Between the last time my mom looked at the property in Jan 2026 and her proposed move in April 2026, the monthly fees increased 15%! I’m sure this increase came with the new management company. The new contract states that they can increase the monthly fees at any time and any amount with a 30 day notice. No cap. They had also told us that she would immediately receive 80% back of her buy-in when she moved from the cottages, but in the contract it stated that her buy-in would be returned when the cottage was sold, not immediately. We were also wined and dined with some of the amenities like free internet, 30 meals included per month, and trips to the doctor on their shuttle within an XX mile radius. The actual contract verbiage stated that internet was extra, only 20 meals included per month, and limited doctor visits if it was on their route. Also the buy-in for the cottages increased from when we initially looked at the property in 2025 from $250k to over $336k.

We also had a horrible time getting Angela to ever call my mom back. My mom would call, wait a week or two, then call Angela again. Every time, she would tell my mom, “I was just about to call you.” Yeah, right. Fees like this should come with red carpet treatment. I shouldn’t have to hunt you down to spend hundreds of thousands of dollars.

We so wanted this to work for my mom, but at what expense? This management company is so new, there is no proven track record. It is a nice facility and the existing residents seem happy. We were afraid after less than a year after a 15% rate increase and being at the top of the monthly fees of their competitors, this place will be priced out of the market, and she would never get her money returned. We gave them many chances to be up front and honest. I’m glad our gut told us to go elsewhere.

reviews.text: I moved into Lewisville Estates approx. one month ago and it turned out to be one of the best decisions I've made in the past several years. My quality of life has improved significantly, my physical health is better, I've met a number of new friends, and as a USMC Viet Nam Veteran, I appreciate Lewisville Estates' commitment to and recognition of my service. reviews.text:
Morada Assisted Living Cedar Hill TX ZERO STARS
I moved my Mother into this facility on 6 June 2024 and moved her out on 2 July 2024. Here’s why:
1. Most of the care-takers my mother encountered were down right rude and unfriendly. I also experienced the rudeness first hand. Ginger is the best med-tech in the facility.
2. I reached out to the acting director, Bradley Buschow via text to introduce myself and to let him know my Mother had moved in 2 days prior. I also inquired about the broken handicap accessible remote door that was not working when we visited the facility in April and still was not working. This is a facility with elderly using walkers. Two days passed and I still had not received a response. I text back to confirm I had the correct telephone number and still no response. I finally asked the Marketing director if the number was correct and she confirmed that it was. I told her I reached out and did not get a response. She quickly said he was probably tied up (excuses) and she would reach out to him. Brad finally returned called and was anything but welcoming. He claimed that was his personal number and he doesn’t carry his personal phone during the day... reminder...I sent text days ago. He then began to tell me he was unaware the door was broken. I told him it was at a minimum not working since April. He then proceeded to tell me the process of submitting a work request. Hmmm, is it the family of residents responsibility to submit work request for the facility? The next day, I submitted our 30 day notice that we were moving from the facility. Once again, no response. He finally reached back out to tell me the door was fixed and if there was anything he could do to improve our experience at Morada....TOO Late Brad!!
3. I reached out to the Business Manager Barbara, 4 days ago regarding final rent payment. Still awaiting response and we moved out today,
4. The Management team has no urgency in matters, lack common business relationship acumen and do not know their residents. Leadership starts at the top and flows down. This is probably why they have so many caregivers that act like they don’t want to be there.
5. Morada corporate, this facility needs an overhaul....or maybe you are aware of the poor leadership team and just don’t care about the care of our elderly. Do Better!
6. PLEASE do not move your loved one into this facility!
SYSTEM WOULD NOT ALLOW ME TO POST UNLESS I ENTERED A STAR....ZERO STARS

reviews.author: Vincent Wee
reviews.text:
I’ve been coming to Discovery Village of Twin Creeks since May, and it has truly been a wonderful experience. I’ve worked as a therapist serving senior communities for over 20 years, and I can honestly say this place is different. There’s a real sense of closeness among the residents and a calm, peaceful environment that you don’t often find in typical senior communities.

The staff treats the residents like family, and it shows in the way they interact every day. The facilities are always clean and well maintained, and the entire community feels safe and welcoming. There are plenty of trees, the grounds are beautiful, and it’s a secured gated community.

One of the things I love most is the option to live in the cottages, which allows residents to enjoy privacy while still being part of the community. The units are spacious, there’s a dog park and a walking trail just steps away, and the location is extremely convenient.

Discovery Village of Twin Creeks truly feels like a special place, and I’m grateful to be a part of this community.

reviews.author: Michael Tafoya
reviews.text:
The staff is very courteous and professional when they work with you but it seems like the team work is not there. There are times in the first shift, I will switch my call light on and I'll be waiting an hour plus for help. If I was to have fallen noone would have reacted right away and I could have been seriously injured. I did fall once and Rachel overnight CNA was there right away and did great. The CNA's I have had Victoria, Kosha, Shiwa, Rachel, and there is one more I forgot her name are awesome and are 5star, and are busy bees, they run around with a lot on their plate. The nurses, aside from Nurse Rose I feel only really pass out meds and change wound dressings, they don't jump in to help their CNA's when they are helping other patients with patient care to make the process run more smoothly. Nurse Rose always makes it a point for me to have what I need and is very consistent and stays on top of her work, and I applaud that. The weekend male nurse for 200 hall on the other hand kinda seems like he's irritated a lot when he has to work, and likes to push everything on the CNA, like one time he brought me meds and he didn't have water so I could take my meds so he pushed the call button and said "the Aide will be here" rudely and walked away. Also, I needed to be changed on my first weekend and he would not help to make sure I was dry. He was more concerned with trying to find a CNA to do it although hours had passed on multiple occasions.
This place is not perfect and some of the staff definitely need to be better trained to work with people, as I would hope they would take care of us like they take care of their own family, but overall my experience has been good.
Physical therapy staff, I have had Linda alot and she is awesome. She is very knowledgeable and I can see how she cares for me as well as the other patients. I'm bad with some other names but all the others are really great too, but Linda is mainly who I have worked with.

reviews.author: Christine Owens
reviews.text:
My 84 year old mother has been here since mid December, and is recovering from spinal fusion surgery. She also has Parkinson’s.
I would like to give a shoutout to Kosha and Net, who take really good care of her. Kosha works so hard and goes above and beyond and we appreciate it. She really cares about the residents. Kosha gets 5 stars!
The room is kept clean by housekeeping. The therapy department is wonderful.
Trina, who runs the front desk is so sweet and always has a smile on her face and a warm greeting. We are also thankful for Abraham who does a wonderful job with transportation to and from outside medical appointments.
The reason for the 3 star rating is there is a problem with the overnight changing of her diaper. She isn’t able to get herself to the toilet so unless someone helps her, she has to use the diaper. Almost EVERY morning she and her bedding are soaking wet. There have also been several times while I’m there during the day where the CNA is busy and I’ve had to change her myself, even though other employees are capable and trained to help when necessary, they make no effort. This is not acceptable. There are a lot of wonderful employees there, but some are not helpful at all and make you feel like you are bothering them. They are receiving payment for her care from Medicare and we have to pay $217 per day on top of whatever they are receiving from insurance. That’s $6,700 per month out of pocket. Many improvements need to be made and I have been talking to anyone who will listen since December but it doesn’t really get better. The weekends are the worst, as they are usually understaffed.

It is clear that their staff values collaboration, communication, and a holistic approach to meeting residents’ needs. Facilities like this set a strong example of quality in senior care, and we look forward to opportunities for partnership in supporting patients and families together.

reviews.author: Eric Ulfsparre
reviews.text:
My wife and I have no great expectations for high quality care at most senior living residences, but our perception was quickly and convincingly changed for the better in so many ways on our first visit to Joyful. We volunteer at our church in a ministry specific for visiting homebound parishioners. We have visited people who live at other senior assisted living residential facilities prior to ever knowing of Joyful Assisted Living.

Even before our first visit to their Rolling Hills Drive, Allen location, I had telephoned the management office to learn about protocols for visiting. They were most helpful, immediately knew about the person we planned to visit, and their needs – they were even aware that our parishioner was expecting us. This was quite different from the normal need to explain ourselves and the purpose of the visit every time we arrived at other senior living residence facilities.

The grounds are well maintained, and the interior is fresh, clean, and up to date. We visit weekly and seem to arrive just ahead of whatever smells so delicious, being prepared for lunch. Everyone is always in good spirits with one another and in quite good care with the very personable aid staff. We always hear good and positive things about living there from the residents and we are able to even see and feel it for ourselves.

reviews.author: High Tolerance
reviews.text:
HELL-MORE AT PARK CITIES

If you love your family member, don’t take them here. On the other hand, if you need to wipe your hands clean, drop off that individual, and throw away the key, this is the right place.

My mother was admitted on November 13th, and honestly I did not feel at ease with her being there. The first day the CNA OB put my mother in a WWE wrestling move to transfer her from her wheelchair to the bed. Mind you this was done after being given specific instructions in said cases.

I asked the CNA what he was doing, and he looked at me like a deer in headlights. I’m even more furious as he flings my mother’s shoes across the room. I told him, “I don’t throw my mother’s shoes around, and why do you think it’s OK” ? Let him tell the story, he did nothing wrong.

It was all bad over the course of those 5 days. From the poop smeared on the seat after being told my mother was unable to go to the toilet, given regular food up to the last day after being told she’s on a mechanical soft diet, poor communication, waiting until the day of discharge to implement a “care plan”.

The tipping point was Fatmata, the rehab director, conducting a swallow eval by giving my mother hot water instead of room temp. How she had no clue the water was hot is beyond her comprehension. In that moment the incompetence was running at an all-time high.

The evening my mother was discharged, it didn’t help no one assisted the transport driver nor myself, in transitioning my mother from her bed to the gurney.

There are some true demons on that staff. Lord knows what may have taken place behind the scenes. They view you as being a problem when things brought to their attention are evidently wrong and need to be corrected.

Octavia the social worker was dismissive and framed having discussions over issues and concerns as “arguing” or me being confrontational. Crystal the assistant DON was standoffish and along with Octavia, the least bit professional.

Once I had the opportunity to speak with Tracie, the DON, she genuinely expressed concerns and empathized over what transpired over the course of those 5 days. She was proactive, along with the administrator, Marquita. Both were apologetic and did their due diligence in righting the wrong. Unfortunately by that time, it was way too late.

SOME staff members showed they were passionate about what they do, but the same can’t be said for others. People’s lives are at stake, and if you don’t have the heart to work in the medical field, find something else to do. In conclusion, save yourself the trouble and time and avoid this place AT ALL COSTS.

I want to thank ALL of the staff/volunteers/residents for taking great care of our Mother! She’s taken care of and her room is always clean, bed made and her “dementia doll” in tow😄 BTW, I’ve made several friends there myself and it always smells clean💙 Ty LV!!!

Five Stars! A Wonderful Experience!

I cannot express enough how thrilled I am with the exceptional care and services offered at Morada Meadow Lakes. From the moment I walked in, it was clear that this facility is dedicated to providing the highest level of care for its residents. The staff’s attention to individual care needs is truly remarkable. They take the time to understand each resident’s preferences and make sure they feel heard and valued. It’s not just a resident for them. They have become a family and when you can’t always be there you want to have some family around and for me. This has been a blessing as this day and age it is extremely hard to trust people to take care of family members or to help with their care or even just keep an eye on them.

What really stands out, though, is the diverse array of activities and outings available. Whether it’s a scenic group trip, a themed event, or even specialized workshops, there’s always something exciting to participate in. It’s so heartwarming to see the residents engage in these activities, creating lasting memories while maintaining a vibrant social life.

I also have to praise the meticulously planned and executed menu. The meals are not only delicious but also thoughtfully designed to meet the nutritional needs of seniors. My father is a diabetic and has been on insulin since 1992 through their help and menu planning. My father has been insulin free for over six months now a lot of work on his part but without being able to Bank on the dietitian and nutrition help, I’m not sure this would’ve been a possibility. There’s a wide variety of options, and the dining experience feels just like home—comforting, nutritious, and enjoyable.

Overall, the attention to detail, the variety of activities, and the focus on care at morada Meadow Lakes in North Richland Hills, Texas have made this an incredibly positive experience. It’s a true gem, and I’m confident any family would feel at ease knowing their loved ones are in such good hands. Highly recommend!

reviews.text:
At first glance this would seem to be a Heavenly place. Don't fall for the hype. The place basically looks like the pics but it has grown old and faded. But hey, who cares if the place safe, clean and care is good? The safety and security are pretty tight, but look at my pics. My best friend was taken to this home on a Friday afternoon, following hip replacement surgery. The surgery went great, but here were a few medical issues afterwards that I won't go into because of HEPA. They weren't ready at the home, and were still cleaning up the room after a former patient. After waiting the room still was not clean. There was left over food items in the little fridge, and you can see the fecal matter on the front of the commode, a used tissue on the floor. This was still the situation on Sat. afternoon when I visited again. The cold water on the kitchen hand sink didn't work at all.
But worst, they claimed to have received no orders for meds. My friend did not receive her first ordered medication until Sat. evening. This include not only pain meds, but her regular blood pressure etc. Her daughter brought her meds from home.
The medical issues that arose in the hospital required her to have assistance to get up and walk, such as bathroom. The first three times she used her call light nothing happened. Her daughter and I had to run down an attendant. It seems there is a light right outside her door, but this does not go to the nurses desk. We never could find out if this was everyone or just her room. So, you're dependent on a nurse seeing the light. The problem there was a low number of workers visible, and one very over worked nurse. On Sat. the nurse says, "You know she can make it to the bathroom and I said, "Oh no, she cannot, she has to have help. And the nurse relates that, she has no such orders and I mention, you don't seem to have any orders at all. But she was willing to risk it.
On Sat. when I showed up they were changing her bed. seems the plastic food storage bag with ice they'd place on her hips had leaked all over the bed. After this they were able to find a real icepack. When i asked about a water pitcher i was told they couldn't find any and must be out. If they don't have basic supplies that's scary all by itself.
I wouldn't put my dog in that place. Luckily my friend got better quickly and is out. I would not put in a review while they still had her in their clutches. Don't let the pictures fool you.

reviews.author: Becky Thimm
reviews.text: I was away from my apartment for 92 days with two hospitalizations. The care I received was exceptional. Savannah, who oversaw the food and dietary, cared about my likes and dislikes and made sure I received what I needed. She also is an excellent cook. I had the very best of care by the nurses and the CNAs. To have caregivers to put on compression socks that I have to have correctly without bruising or hurting me was a blessing. All of the staff was kind and courteous to me at all times. When it was time for me to leave and go back to my apartment, I cried. I had received so much support and good care that I didn’t want to leave. I got back to my apartment and decided that I wanted to be closer to the new friends I had made at Harrison at Heritage so 8 days later I moved a mile away. I can go over there and feel the warmth and kindness and hugs that I received at Harrison at Heritage. The physical therapists, housekeepers, maintenance man, cnas, nurses, doctor, PA, everyone made me feel like I could get better and enjoy my future. I send my deepest love to all that I met and cared for me. If I should ever need help again, this would be the only place I would go. The Harrison at Heritage earns so much. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

My loved one resides at this facility, and our experience has been mixed overall.

In our experience, the level of care and responsiveness seems to improve when family members are frequently present and actively involved. We have found that concerns are often addressed more effectively when escalated through the facility’s compliance reporting channels. I encourage families to stay informed, document concerns, and advocate for their loved ones when needed.

reviews.author: Tamara Haskins
reviews.text:
On Tuesday, January 20, I visited my mother and asked a CNA named Tiffany to help me get mom back into bed after she had been sitting for hours on a stage 3 wound. The CNA said she needed to finish dinner orders first. When I explained the urgency of relieving pressure from the wound, the CNA became hostile and started a loud confrontation with me. The facility director overheard and instructed the CNA to report to his office.

I filed a complaint with corporate and the same day. The next day, I spoke with the Regional Vice President, who assured me the issue was handled and that this CNA would no longer be assigned to my mother. However, later that same day, I went to see mom and I saw the same CNA on my mother’s hall, socializing with other CNAs. When Tiffany saw me, she rolled her eyes at me again, showing there were no real consequences.

Out of concern for retaliation and my mother’s safety, I immediately removed mom from the facility.

On another visit, a CNA told me my mom had no wound dressing on all day because it had come off during changing her. I asked why didn't you notify the nurse? The CNA said the wound care nurse will be here later today. I went to nurse station and alerted the nurse myself and requested a wound dressing be put on immediately. I also requested a culture be done on mom's wound, which later confirmed bacterial growth.

If you value professionalism, compassion and proper medical care, I strongly recommend avoiding this facility.

reviews.author: Kim Holcomb
reviews.text:
My husband and I took a tour of Richland Hills Rehab on Friday July 10th, 2026. I would NOT let my worst enemy stay at this facility!

This is an older facility and is undergoing renovations, so there was clutter everywhere, which was understandable due to the renovations. The front reception area is outdated, dusty and smelled musty. Not very inviting on a first appearance. However that is not the problem with this facility.

I believe the lady's name was Kristi that gave us the tour. She took a lot of notes beforehand on a small note pad and she kept wanting to sit down in the reception area or lean up against the wall to chit chat and we just wanted a tour. When we finally started the tour, she introduced us to every head staff member and went over her notes with them, which was very odd to us. She kept saying hippa, but we never saw her notes so not sure if anything else was on her notes other than what we shared with her. We were there only for a tour and not to be introduced to all the staff and for her to include them in the information we had given her.

On our tour she took us to the back of the facility where the patient rooms were. As we were going down each hall it reeked with Strong Urine Smell that was Very Old and Nasty! I mentioned it to Kristi several times during our tour and she acted surprised and just said sorry. She should have immediately told the CNA's about this problem, as the nurses station was crowded with nurses sitting around doing nothing. The staff work in this smell everyday so I guess they have adapted to the smell. It was SO nasty! Not a clean environment at all! Also the pics of the patient rooms on Google Do Not look like any of the rooms we saw or the room we were shown. All the rooms were all, nasty, outdated and tiny!

It was very sad to my husband and I as we walked by each room seeing these residents in their beds in fetal positions and potentially lying in soiled urine and fecal matter. It was obvious they were not getting the attention they needed or deserved. The patient rooms are very tiny and should really only accommodate one bed, as they really have no room to move around with two beds in those rooms, especially if there is a true emergency.

This facility has a lot of staff and we witnessed them either sitting around talking to each other or they were on their phones and not working. It seems they are just there collecting a paycheck, because this facility is nasty, dirty and horrible in our opinion.
Please Do Not take your loved ones to this facility, we highly recommend you finding another facility for them.

For those who are not aware, the Wellington offers "Respite Care" - temporary stays in their assisted living wing, for those who may need help on a temporary basis.

She lives alone in another city, and keeping her with me became difficult, because I could not be around all day to help her get to the bathroom, bathe, etc. We were very stressed about how to get her through her recovery in a way that felt comfortable and dignified.

reviews.author: Sharon Richardson
reviews.text: My father, who had Alzheimer’s, lived in The Plaza for almost a full year, until he passed away (at 90 years and ten months old) in June/2025. The staff were so very kind and caring toward him. The physical therapists were great at keeping him active. The nurses and CNA’s were helpful anytime they were called upon, tending to everything from baths, getting him dressed, cleaning his room, changing bedding, etc. The admissions staff were also very courteous and helpful in getting him settled in. We were thankful that, after his first week at The Plaza, during which he lived in a room in their Memory Ward, it was determined that he would be able to move out of the Memory Care wing and into a room on their main floor. The only reason for four stars instead of five is that, in the beginning, we had some concerns about the laundry and bathing schedule. But, it seems that was because of a staff turnover. After the first six weeks or so, all the issues had been addressed. The staff made sure he had a wonderful, compatible roommate, was well fed and cared for, and received attentive medical care. We appreciated very much how quickly the nurses would alert us of any medicine changes, or any behavioral or health concerns they had for my dad. He was very well loved and cared for at The Plaza.

reviews.author: Samantha Calnan
reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

From the nurses and aides to the therapy team, everyone goes above and beyond to make sure patients feel comfortable and supported. The facility itself is clean, welcoming, and well-maintained, which gave me so much peace of mind. Communication has always been clear and responsive, and I really appreciate the personal attention given to each resident. I can’t thank them enough for the excellent care provided — I highly recommend The Plaza at Richardson to anyone looking for a skilled nursing facility!

reviews.text: I had such a fear of skilled nursing facilities when my sister had cancer and her husband has Parkinson’s. My sister passed away and when her husband needed skilled nursing, I panicked! reviews.author: Sarah LaDoux
reviews.text:
My grandmother lives here, and unfortunately the management has been very disappointing. Her front door will not latch properly, so I contacted the office to request maintenance assistance to ensure that her door would stay shut. However, the maintenance technician who responded was extremely disrespectful.

In addition, the front gates have been broken for several years, allowing anyone to enter and exit the property freely, which raises serious safety concerns.

To make matters worse, the wheelchair ramp in front of her building was removed and replaced with a parking space and curb. This change has made it difficult, if not impossible, for residents who rely on wheelchairs to access their units safely.

Considering this is a senior living facility, it is extremely concerning that the residents do not appear to be properly cared for. The ongoing maintenance issues, lack of accessibility, and disregard for residents’ safety and well-being are unacceptable. I hope these issues are addressed promptly, as they significantly impact the quality of life for the people who live here.

reviews.author: Fran
reviews.text: I cannot say enough about Lakeside Manor Apartments. The apartments are newly renovated and they look beautiful. It is a 62 and over community and it is quiet and peaceful. Our office staff goes above and beyond to help all residents. April and Mike will do all they can to resolve a problem. April deals more with the residents. We are blessed to have such a caring person. She is Professional, Courteous and Kind. I have been here for a little over 4 years and anything that is donated goes straight to the residents. She cares about us and often buys things for the clubhouse. She is a very giving person with a heart of gold. I’m not sure why we would have a negative review when the office staff is the best I have ever seen. I rented from other places that were a nightmare. You didn’t even see the staff and good luck getting something fixed. Here at Lakeside Manor we have a very good maintenance team. Clara and Bud are knowledgeable, competent people that always get the job done in a timely manner. I have found a home here and I am not looking to go anywhere else. So please if you are looking to settle down come visit and see for yourself the great people that you will be dealing with.

reviews.author: Kelly Singer
reviews.text:
First impressions are important to prospective future tenants. While I’m not a tenant , the following occurrence helped make my decision to not consider this place.
I entered the office to obtain rental information. There were 3 other people present and a women behind the counter. A tenant entered asking about a parking spot assignment. The employee told him she was by herself and would not be able to take care of the request at that time. The tenant then stated he requested it 3 days ago. The employee told the tenant that she informed him the other day she would contact him when she had the parking info. The tenant replied back to the employee that she is always by herself and it was ridiculous to have to wait this long. He was not happy. I left, as this is a very negative experience for prospective tenants.

reviews.author: Ellen Edwards
reviews.text:
I moved in to Mariposa at Harris Road November 2023. There are many things that led me to only give 2 stars. First, the laundry didn’t work from what I was told it was because of an account that was not yet set up. Now, there are only 3/5 washers and 2/6 dryers working. That was reported to the office last week and when I asked the property manager about them today she pulled up the request to still be initiated starting the request today.
Another ongoing area of concern is the gates. Initially we had trouble getting them to open when they should and now stay open when they shouldn’t. This is a safety concern. Another area of concern is the ‘gym’. It has equipment that is damaged and can’t be used. Case in point is the treadmill that has a tear in the track.
Continuing on is the lack of direction for what to do when the community fire alarm goes off. We had this happen when it was still very very cold and people had no idea what they were supposed to do. When I inquired about the fire plan and possibly an educational fire drill I was assured that this would be scheduled. Well it’s been over 100 degrees for some time and no fire drill or any information has happened.
Still continuing another area is the pool. A crack was found and reported in June. It was fairly quickly closed down and has been closed for 8 weeks! Several of the residents were engaging in water exercise because they were unable to do more conventional exercises due to various conditions. The pool could have been repaired within a short time per a pool professional using water putty to close the crack allowing for continued use. And it sure would have been nice to have the pool available with the extreme heat that we have been having.
The final area is the assignment of parking in the carports. In February we were told to have our preference(s) submitted to the manager by I believe was the 23rd of February with the implied completion of assignments by the end of February. We are still waiting for the assignment. This is impacting me directly especially with this heat when not having a closer parking spot and now having breathing issues. I have spoken with the property manager, sent an email to the regional manager about a week ago and have not received anything back from them to date.
I would certainly appreciate any assistance possible as all of these areas are not new or something that the management is unaware of.

reviews.text: I would like to take the time out to brag about a person that not only helped me and my sibling’s get our mother the care she needed, she was a key player in making sure all the boxes were checked off to make it possible for my mother get accepted into Matlock Place. reviews.author: Gregory Brunken
reviews.text:
A few years ago, we put my mom in that home facility because she was only three blocks from me. Her first night there the Night Shift nurses did not give her her medication when she needed it and when she asked for it, they said get back in your room and stop begging.

That didn’t sit well to me. I went up there the next night To share my concerns with diplomacy. I told him what was said and the nurses that were involved and I told him that they need to treat their elderly people much better than what they do because one day you might be here. And I said I really don’t want to get any more bad news on this because it won’t be good now please treat my mother as well as other people right. I said it right in front of the administrator and the next day I got a good report for my mom. But needless to say after about three days, she moved back to her previous place and not too long after that she passed away. From reading the negative reviews that appears at this place has not changed a bit.

reviews.author: Cindy Brooks-Smart
reviews.text:
My brother has been a resident at Glenview Wellness and Rehabilitation Center for over three years, and I cannot speak highly enough of the care he receives. The staff is consistently friendly, attentive, and genuinely committed to the well‐being of their residents. Every month, I meet with his counselor and nurse to review his care plan, and they always take the time to ask if there is anything I feel needs extra attention. I truly appreciate how open they are to communication and how seriously they take family input.
In all the time my brother has lived there, he has never filed a grievance about his care or living conditions. The facility is always clean and well‐maintained, and there are many activities available for residents who choose to participate. It gives me great peace of mind knowing he is in a place where he feels safe, comfortable, and supported.
After three years, the fact that he has not once complained—and that I have never encountered an issue with the services provided—speaks volumes about the quality of care at Glenview. I am grateful for everything the staff does and would highly recommend this facility to other families seeking compassionate and reliable long‐term care.

reviews.author: Tiffany McMurray
reviews.text:
I do not recommend the long term nursing side of the facility. If you want your loved one to be happy and cared for, don’t put them in the nursing facility. My mom was in the rehab part three times and they took really good care of her, not to mention the relationships I had with the staff.. I do recommend the Rehabilitation Center there.

Then my mom went into the long term side. The first words out of the nurses tech when I walked in was “make yourself present so that your LO is taken care of”.. I am there several times a week. My mom would be in her wheelchair with the oxygen tank empty or even off when she is supposed to be in oxygen 24/7. She would ring her call button and no one would come,. There were at least three times that I couldn’t even find the call button.. it was all the way behind the bed. I had to pull the wire like a rope hand over hand and pull it out. What if there was an emergency, and my mom couldn’t find the button?? Everyday I was with my mom I had no idea what I was walking into. Did she fall and I wasn’t contacted, yes. I feel as though my mom was being neglected. There is so much more I could write but I’m saving it for another time.

Please, find another place to put your loved one!.. it is not safe and the majority of the people who work there are lazy and don’t care. As a matter of fact. Yesterday my mom asked if her nurses tech could help her to the restroom. She was told, “you have a diaper on, use it”, We actually have pull ups as she doesn’t need a diaper. There was a case of underpants in her room and they flat refused to put them on her. Mom was in the nursing facility from November 2025 till today, March 3, 2026.

I feel relieved that we got her out of there safely and we are no longer under their care.

reviews.author: Bryon Chesser
reviews.text:
Avoid Westpark Rehabilitation and Living. Our experience with this facility was unacceptable on every level.

The building is run down—peeling paint, holes in the walls, missing electrical faceplates, loose outlets, and damaged furniture. It looked neglected and unsafe.

The staff was not attentive to our loved one’s needs. One night he waited an hour for help to use the restroom. No one at the facility would answer the phone when we tried to call. I only reached someone because I had the Executive Director’s cell number.

Communication is almost nonexistent. They do not answer calls, rarely respond to emails, and repeatedly failed to provide basic information we requested. Even the external hospice staff caring for him was ignored.

We also have serious concerns about the quality of medical care he received. While he was there, he had an ulcer on his foot that the staff repeatedly told us was “getting better.” He is now in the hospital with a bone infection (Osteomyelitis) that required surgery. The surgeon told us there was a great chance he could lose his foot, but fortunately they were able to save it. This raises real questions about how closely the medical staff at Westpark were monitoring him—or if they were monitoring him at all.

This facility failed our family, and I would never recommend it to anyone.

reviews.text: The facility has much to do to provide commendable support to residents for sure. And it is evident that it doesn’t have a full complement of employees. reviews.author: Teresa Raney
reviews.text:
My mother was transferred to Sandy Lake Rehab after a 5-day hospitalization. She has dementia and Parkinson's disease. Before arriving at the facility, she was able to stand with assistance and walk with supervision to the restroom. During her time at Sandy Lake Rehab, however, she has experienced repeated neglect that appears directly related to severe understaffing.
The CNAs and nursing staff who are present have been compassionate and hardworking, and I am grateful for their efforts. However, they are clearly overworked and being asked to meet unrealistic demands, which is jeopardizing patient care and safety.
As a result, my mother has been having accidents daily, even though this only happened occasionally before she came to Sandy Lake. She is aware when she needs to use the restroom, but when it takes over 30 minutes for staff to respond, accidents become unavoidable. On one occasion, she sat for two hours after an accident before someone was available to change her, despite using the call button. The call button itself has also been unreliable.
There have been multiple instances where family members have had to step in because help did not arrive. One day, my sister and I assisted my mother to the restroom ourselves after waiting more than 30 minutes with no response. On another day, my 85-year-old father transferred her from the bed to the wheelchair and then to the bathroom because she was miserable waiting for assistance. This should never be the responsibility of family members, especially when it creates additional safety risks for both the patient and loved ones.
I have also come in on many days to find that my mother had no water. I began bringing water bottles from home just to make sure she had something to drink. This level of neglect has caused humiliation, discomfort, and unnecessary suffering for my mother.
Most concerning is that instead of improving through rehabilitation, my mother has declined over the past 10 days. Rather than receiving consistent care and meaningful physical therapy, she has been left waiting for basic assistance with toileting, transfers, and hydration. I am deeply concerned about what condition she would be in if my sister, my father, and I had not been present every day for 12 hours to help care for her ourselves.
Ever patient has different needs and requirements, so please do thorough research before placing your loved one in a facility.

After we reported that they dressed the golf size soars. We bought her 3 new cotton nighties and those were taken from her room. We bought a padding for her bed and that was gone too. reviews.author: Carl Tapia
reviews.text:
I had a very concerning experience with Heritage Garden Rehab & Healthcare. Despite having valid Power of Attorney in place, the facility failed to honor it and allowed my loved one to make independent decisions while clearly mentally incompetent.

As a result, she was put in real danger. After being allowed to leave, she fell twice and her actions led to police involvement and a report being filed. These were preventable situations that should never have been allowed to happen under proper supervision.

There was a lack of accountability from both staff and administration when these concerns were raised. Communication was poor, and there was little to no effort made to work with me to ensure proper care, supervision, or safety planning.

For a facility responsible for vulnerable individuals, this level of disregard is extremely troubling. I would strongly caution others to think carefully before trusting this facility with the care of a loved one.

What meant so much to us was that many of the original staff members from day one were still there when she passed, and they remained tender, compassionate, and attentive to her from start to finish.

They came to know our father and our whole family because we were there so often. Through all of my father’s medical ups and downs, they cared for him as well. When he stayed there for respite care so he could be close to her while I traveled, they were amazing with him too.

In the final days, after our mother was moved to comfort care, our father suffered a stroke the very next day. The staff helped us keep them together at the end, and their compassion during that heartbreaking time meant more than words can express. We truly could not imagine going through it anywhere else.

reviews.author: Keokuk Domingo
reviews.text:
My name is Keokuk Domingo, and after reading so many glowing reviews about this company, I felt compelled to share a very different experience.

While I was still in the hospital recovering from surgery, I received a call requesting my credit card information—even though I have PPO insurance that covers my care. I was initially told the cost would be $1,100, which was later changed to a $250 “hold.” The inconsistent information regarding payment was concerning, especially while I was in a vulnerable situation following major surgery.

I was discharged on March 5th after undergoing a full hip replacement. My surgeon referred this company for my home health services, trusting they would provide the necessary follow-up care. Unfortunately, that has not been my experience.

Since my discharge, I have not seen a physical therapist at all, which is extremely troubling given the importance of physical therapy after a hip replacement. A nurse has visited twice, but physical therapy—one of the most critical parts of recovery—has yet to begin.

I have made multiple calls trying to get answers, yet I still have not been given a definitive date for when physical therapy will start. At this point, I am left waiting while my recovery is delayed. Because of how referrals and insurance timing work, it is now extremely difficult to switch providers.

For a company with so many positive reviews, I expected a much higher level of communication, coordination, and care. When someone is recovering from major surgery, delays in treatment are not just frustrating—they can impact recovery and overall health.

Patients should not have to repeatedly call to receive basic follow-up care. I sincerely hope this company improves its processes so other patients do not experience the same situation. Not sure why we’re here.

reviews.text:
They set this facility up with the appeal of getting your business by greeting people with the most friendliest front staff to convince you to leave your loved ones. They show you all the amenities and weekly activities. But the staff who takes care of your loved ones are rude and do the bare minimum. Any questions asked are not answered. They are annoyed when you ask for assistance or help. The nursing staff is horrible and so are the hallway assistants. They spend most of their time sitting in the hallways and if you ask for help most of the time they tell you it’s not their job or they say okay and do not come back into the room. if you are looking for a facility to ONLY give your family member their meds and dropping off their food. Then this is the place for you. Don’t let the appearance of this place and its front staff fool you. Get to meet the actually people who will care for your loved ones. They keep them in the back for a reason. They are rude and do the bare minimum.

***Additional comment- My mom was there for wound care. When we asked the helper what cream she was applying she took out a tube of toothpaste. She had been applying toothpaste! When she was told it was toothpaste she said she didn’t know because the main nurse didn’t show her where the cream was she just assumed it was that tube. Another incident was my mom’s bed deflated on a Saturday, the nursing staff told us there was no maintenance done on the weekends. She was to sleep on it until Monday. Do not recommend this place. Looks are deceiving. Also my mom was denied services a couple of days after this post. They started the process of denying her appeals. At the discharge meeting we were given a binder and basically told figure it out.

reviews.author: Anita Woolsey
reviews.text:
I am the contact for my friend who was admitted here about 6 days ago, but I live out-of-state. I left a msg about 24 hours after admission for her nurse to ask about the plan, schedule, timeline or any care outline about her, but the nurse didn't call back. I have left 4 voice mail messages for the social worker who I am told is the person responsible for such things... 4 messages with no response. I called for the administrator, and the main number was answered at the nurses' station. I asked for the administrator, and the person said she would transfer me. I reached a no-name voice mail and left yet another message.

When my friend has called and begged me to get her out of this place, there was such wailing and crying in the background that I couldn't hear my friend talk.

When she had visitors on the 4th day of her stay, she had no pants and no shoes and no one from the facility had let me know. I guess I have to give at least one star for Google to accept my review.

reviews.text: Catherine the Sales Manager was very kind & courteous. She answered all questions. I am relaying our visit findings to the patient's nurse and caregiver. Units are a nice size & laid out well. So many amenities. Thank you Catherine!

reviews.author: joann olsovsky
reviews.text: Words cannot begin to express the gratitude I have for the Volante team. Starting with Sandy Rasberry who toured us and found the perfect apartment for my handicapped sister. She is simply incredible. Michael Masci visited my sister in the hospital and was a refreshing source of expertise and advice as we were contemplating her care needs. Lastly Mr Little the executive director talked us through the details of a resident’s stay. He is just amazing. Our family is so grateful for Volante. They even greeted my sister with a real red carpet and a celebration as she walked through the door. She felt so welcome. In fact it was lunchtime and we had our first meal together there. They said the food was amazing and they weren’t kidding. It is delicious!! My sister felt so at home. As a family member, it is a relief to know that my sister is in such wonderful hands.

name: HarborChase of Southlake
address: 700 E State Hwy 114, Southlake, TX 76092, USA

reviews.author: Kimberly Dobbs
reviews.text:
Working with Elizabeth at HarborChase of Southlake has been such a wonderful experience. She is incredibly kind, knowledgeable, patient, and truly cares about the residents and families she serves.

She goes above and beyond to make people feel comfortable, informed, and supported during what can often be an emotional transition. Her warmth, professionalism, and genuine compassion are evident in every interaction.

HarborChase itself is absolutely beautiful and truly one of the top senior living communities available in Southlake. The attention to detail, level of care, and overall environment are exceptional.

HarborChase is fortunate to have someone like Elizabeth on their team, and I would absolutely recommend working with her.

reviews.author: Kay McNabb
reviews.text:
I have been living at Harbor Chase Assisted Living in Southlake since May of 2025 following a serious illness and hospital stay. My daughter and son-in law who lived in the area picked Harbor Chase after visiting at least 6 other places. If you come for a visit, you will find Harbor Chase inviting.

The excellent therapy I received here made me stronger. The caregivers have been attentive to my needs. Diana in housekeeping, has kept my apartment clean. The Life Enrichment Director, Sarai has provided meaningful activities to socialize and has also given me the opportunity to lead residents in craft projects.

The Executive Chef, Bradley is available for any suggestions related to dining preferences. There are many food options to choose from and the meals are delicious. The community holds regular town hall meetings to get input from residents. The Executive Director Byron, has been accessible to me.

I am very comfortable and content at Harbor Chase when initially I had reservations about coming to an assisted living community. The staff here at Harbor Chase has been great and I am pleased to consider many staff and residents my friends.

Fairly soon, I will need to say goodbye to all my friends as my family and I are relocating to Florida. I hope that the experiences that I have there are as positive as what Harbor Chase has provided me in the last year. I would highly recommend Harbor Chase to anyone who needs an assisted living community!

reviews.author: Tanesia Coleman
reviews.text:
I had a wonderful experience at this facility. Everything was very clean, well-maintained, and comfortable. The view was absolutely beautiful and made the atmosphere feel peaceful and relaxing.
What really made everything even more beautiful was Nurse Momma J. She went above and beyond to make sure I was comfortable and welcomed. She was kind, attentive, and treated me like family. You can tell she truly loves what she does, and her positive attitude made a big difference in my experience.
I highly recommend this facility to anyone looking for a clean environment, beautiful surroundings, and exceptional care. Thank you, Momma J, for being so amazing! ❤️ The best nurse there is!!

reviews.author: Lindsay Antoniello
reviews.text: Want to share my recent move-in experience at Discovery Village Southlake. We moved mom to DV last week and so far the entire transition has been wonderful. The DV team has been incredibly caring and attentive to mom and to the family. Everyone from the sales staff, the nursing staff, the dining staff, the maintenance staff and the activity staff have been helpful, supportive and patient. Everyone is easy to reach and incredibly responsive. Hollie even helped me build some furniture for mom’s apartment and helped me manage cable set up with Frontier. And on top of it all, the community of residents on my mom’s floor are so kind and welcoming!

reviews.author: Vivienne Linder
reviews.text: The Oaks is a wonderful community! The Director of Entertainment and Programs (Kalista) goes above and beyond to create fun meaningful activities and experiences for the residents. She is very involved with both the residents and their families and truly cares about making everyone feel included and valued. Her energy and dedication make such a positive impact! Kalista puts so much heart into what she does and genuinely cares about everyone she comes into contact with.

reviews.author: shanzi wamboi
reviews.text:
Oaks is a good facility, and the services offered are excellent. The caregivers provide great care to the residents. I would especially like to recognize Nurse Sarita for the outstanding care she gives. She is respectful, attentive, and always willing to help. She explains things clearly and ensures that residents’ needs are met. Her calm and positive attitude makes everyone feel comfortable, valued, and well cared for.
JKiarie

reviews.author: Chloe Zeller
reviews.text: My grandpa has been at Avanti for the past six months, and we couldn't be more grateful for the exceptional care he's received. The staff has been kind, compassionate, and attentive every step of the way. We highly recommend Avanti to anyone looking for a caring place for a loved one. A special thank you to Tiffani, who went above and beyond by organizing a beautiful anniversary celebration for my grandparents. It meant so much to our family. Thank you, Avanti, for all that you do!

reviews.author: Joan Perkins
reviews.text: Avanti has done a wonderful job taking care of my dad. The staff cultivates a fun and caring atmosphere. Tiffani engages the residents in fun games, she gets the residents to laugh and participate with her high energy and sense of humor. Ken is very kind and so patient, always helpful. I also want to mention how wonderful Lisa, Jae, Erica, Josh, Nico and Kaveon are. They provide such a fun atmosphere and great communication with my family.

The property features secure interior spaces, structured cognitive therapies, sensory gardens, and specialized 24-hour caregiver support.
researchSummary: Verified standalone memory care facility in Flower Mound via official domain.

reviews.author: kat johnson
reviews.text:
If my mom had full memory functionality, she would have loved choosing this place for herself. After extensive review, we are incredibly grateful to have found Pam and Magnolia in Flower Mound. Safety, security, cleanliness, and personal attention were our top priorities. Director Pamela Ervin went above and beyond, helping us every step of the way and continues to help us navigate challenges as mom changes phases in her journey dealing with dementia.

We appreciate the home-like feeling, perfect size facility, no unpleasant odors, the Chefs always working so hard to meet mom's specific needs, and the looping corridor around the inner courtyard allow mom independence in safety. The entire staff share their smiles, friendships, and care to help mom find comfort and joy every day to the best of her current ability. Mom has been a resident for over 17 months now and continues to improve in areas that were exceptionally difficult dealing with at home.
Thank you for your kindness and compassion.

reviews.author: Jocie Means
reviews.text: The care and attention at this assisted living home truly brings peace of mind. The staff is compassionate, professional, and always willing to go the extra mile to make residents feel comfortable and valued. The environment is clean, welcoming, and feels like a real community. We’re so grateful to the staff for always showing such great love.

reviews.author: T J Hill-Harper
reviews.text: Found this property while searching for a quiet, senior community. Josie gave me a tour and I was so pleased I called my husband to come and see it. Josie's warm welcome was followed by Joyce's professional, courteous support when we applied to move in. Look forward to being a part of this neighborhood.

reviews.author: Christine Enslin
reviews.text:
First this location is under new ownership as of March 2025. We toured the facility at the end of March. The new owner has smaller residential homes and is known for superior caring caregivers. We moved my mom in at the end of March and had our own room. We furnished our room and Rusinder was very helpful with the process. While moving in we got to see new flooring going in, painting and decorations being updated.
The owner checks in on my mom daily. She cares about each of her residents. When my mom needed to go the hospital I was immediately notified and she kept in touch asking how she was doing. I am thankful that Margo Brooks senior care living coordinator found us the perfect place for my mom.

reviews.author: Christine Acker
reviews.text:
A BLESSING TO OUR MOTHER AND OUR FAMILY

For the past six months, our mother has been a resident at Beehive. Having considered many options to help our mother, we chose Beehive, and we are delighted with our decision.

A family-run organization, Beehive manages the home in a caring and nurturing environment. Cleanliness is consistently superb, the home-cooked meals are outstanding, and residents are encouraged to come out of the rooms each day for activities that are tailored to their interests and capabilities. The staff is nurturing – they treat our mother as their own with lovingkindness and attention in each moment of the day.

The owners, Chip and Lisa are fully engaged at the home as owner/managers, and they make themselves part of the caregiving team. From the chefs in the kitchen to the activities director to the management of the medications, the entire staff treats the home residents as family. House manager and nurse, Jackie, is an attentive, helpful and gracious leader.

We could not be happier with our decision and our mother is receiving excellent assisted living care.

Beehive: highly recommended without reservation – a wonderful, assisted living facility in a nurturing environment.

reviews.author: Richard Simmons
reviews.text: Sage Senior Support was a godsend! Professional in every way but especially kind, considerate and sensitive in resolving a very difficult situation. I can unequivocally recommend Logan and his team!

reviews.author: Linda Squyres
reviews.text: My husband and I sold our house “as is” to Logan at Sage Senior Support. Logan and Jules came to do a walk thru of our house and they both were so very nice and so very supportive of our move. We couldn’t have asked for a smoother experience. Both Logan and Jules promptly answered all our questions and our closing with a notary, who came to us, went perfectly. I truly recommend Logan and Jules to anyone selling their home. They were both so friendly and so understanding of our particular situation. I highly recommend them!!

reviews.author: sandy rockwerk
reviews.text:
My mom has been a resident at the Heritage for a number of years. This past weekend was her 106th birthday . The facility arranged a celebration for her and it was awesome.. All the arrangements.... were terrific.

Attendance.... standing room only . Entertainment... a professional singer was spot on.The Decor, the cake, the staff, Etc.... where all too wonderful to put into words.

A gift to my Mom that cannot be topped.

Truly a day to remember for us all.

reviews.author: John Willson
reviews.text: What makes this facility so incredible are the people. They have developed a culture of thoughtful and caring support that is simply extraordinary. Don't get me wrong, the facility is amazing and the food is great. The people are the difference.

reviews.author: YVBOA HOME DESIGN
reviews.text: I first came to know about Watermere through a friend whose mother was in residence. My parents were living in California and during a Christmas holiday I took them by to see Watermere. They were previously adamant about not moving to Texas, but after seeing the grounds, the amenities, the community and the golf, they made the move to Watermere. Watermere was is a first class community and what makes it so special is all the people. Even while my father was getting medical care at Discovery Village, we stayed at his residence in Watermere and had the full support from not only the staff at Watermere, but the amazing community of residents. It was the best of the best for my parents. Thank you Watermere!!

reviews.author: Brian Amrhein
reviews.text: This is a review for the Skilled Nursing Rehab floor, my mother spent a few weeks there, over 2 visits. This was a few years ago, around 2017-2018, but it was terrible place to leave a loved one. The facility is beautiful, but the aides are not caring people, and they do not want to do their job. I found one sleeping in the hallway one night while my mom was left with a nebulizer mask on for 45 minutes (should be a five minute treatment). They don't answer the call buzzer of the patients, and they don't answer the phone when you call. The doctor back then was bad as well. My mother told them she was slapped by an aide during a disagreement, and the doctor tried to talk me out of reporting it because "no one would believe her, because of all of the medications we are giving her"... check the Medicare ratings, do not be fooled by the pretty building.

reviews.author: Michelle Rankine
reviews.text: As a healthcare professional, I highly recommend The Carlyle Rehabilitation. Diana made the entire process seamless with her professionalism, excellent communication, and compassionate approach. She truly goes above and beyond to ensure patients and families have a great experience.

reviews.author: Kim Carlysle
reviews.text: My father spent almost a month here. Very good experience overall from the administration and reception, healthcare professionals, to the maintenance people! Highlights to his care came from Nurse Brenda, and the wound care nurse, Yolanda. Yolanda worked miracles on my father’s skin tears and open sores. She is a healing ANGEL!! The physical therapists and speech therapist are top notch too. He also needed to gain weight, so LC and her team in the kitchen made sure he had plenty of nutritious meals and snacks! He continues to improve at home now because of the care he received here. At 88 years old, he has a great outlook on life! Attitude matters! 💗

reviews.author: Sheila Fabrize
reviews.text: The staff is great. Many staff go personally out of their way to help. For example Bill went to retrive my Bible in another city and brought it to me. The nurses acted quickly to get me to the hospital to help avoid complications with a heart issue. Highly recommend for rehab or long term care.

reviews.author: Shannon McCurdy
reviews.text: We switched from another local skilled nursing who almost killed my mom. Everyone on staff went above and beyond to welcome us and give my mom the utmost care. Communication was excellent. We never had an issue reaching anyone and Linda worked hard getting my mom released with all the equipment and care she needed! We were fortunate to find Cross Timbers!

reviews.author: Krystal Alvarado
reviews.text: What a wonderful Mother’s Day experience Sage Oak of Denton gave their residents. This is an example of how their residents are recognized, pampered and cared for. Denton is lucky to have a top tier “boutique feel” Assisted Living right in our backyard.

reviews.author: Denise LaManna
reviews.text:
We are incredibly thankful for Sage Oak of Denton. From day one, the caregivers have treated my dad like family, showing genuine kindness, patience, and compassion, and extending that same care to our family as well. The caretakers and staff are attentive to individual needs, intentional with personal care, and very responsive. Every visit, we are greeted with warm smiles, and the residents are happy, engaged, and clearly well cared for.

A special thank you to Dee, who has been such a blessing. She took the time to truly get to know my dad, and the way she connects with him has made a noticeable difference in how he responds and engages. We are also grateful for the Director of Nursing, Kristina, who is proactive, responsive, and consistently goes above and beyond by answering questions, sending updates, and supporting my dad’s well being.

The community truly feels like home. The house is clean, warm, and thoughtfully designed to foster connection among residents. Rooms are always well kept, the chef-prepared meals are excellent, and the daily activities are purposeful and engaging. The heart, teamwork, and dedication at Sage Oak of Denton have brought our family great peace of mind. Thank you!!

reviews.author: Carolyn Stew
reviews.text:
We moved my friend to memory care at Village on the Park Denton about two months ago, and I just want to share how grateful I am that we made this decision and chose Village on the Park.

Karla has been an incredible advocate throughout this entire process. She helped bring us peace of mind and made what could have been a difficult transition feel much easier. My friend is truly thriving, and we couldn’t be happier with the care and support she has received.

Village on the Park has such a unique program that it doesn’t feel like traditional memory care. The staff is warm, welcoming, and genuinely loves serving the residents. They have become like family to us.

I am so grateful for the kind hearts and dedication of everyone who serves this community. God bless you all.

reviews.author: Nancy C
reviews.text:
We’ve been searching for the right place for my aunt, and after calling so many communities, Village in the Park Denton truly stood out. Karla has been extremely helpful and very knowledgeable throughout the entire process. While some places never even responded or took days to get back to us, Karla was on top of everything from the very beginning. She made us feel comfortable and supported every step of the way, and the whole experience felt easy and reassuring.

The community itself is beautiful, and everyone we met was genuinely happy — from the residents to every staff member we encountered. You can really feel the positive atmosphere as soon as you walk in. If you’re looking for a trustworthy assisted living or memory care community, I would absolutely recommend checking out Village in the Park Denton.

name: Fairhaven Denton Assisted Living
address: 2400 N Bell Ave, Denton, TX 76209, USA
description: Fairhaven Denton Assisted Living offers personalized senior care services in Denton, Texas. Residents receive individual assistance with daily tasks, medication supervision, nutritious meals, and social engagement opportunities within a supportive environment.
researchSummary: Verified Fairhaven Denton official site for assisted senior living care.

reviews.author: Damon Darkwalker
reviews.text: I cannot say enough about the entire staff at Fairhaven (Georgina, Brittney, all of them). They did such a wonderful job taking care of my mom. They treated her like family, and no matter how difficult Mom could be, they were always kind and patient with her. I felt so much more at ease knowing that she was somewhere safe, and somewhere where she could get the kind of care she needed. The facility itself is large, clean, open, and full of ambient light. My Mom had vision problems so it was important that she be somewhere bright and not gloomy--like so many facilities out there. The food was also excellent, and they have activities, and van trips for the residents to go shopping. Mom enjoyed playing bingo in the dining room as well--and she loved getting ice cream! Do your loved-one a favor and take them to Fairhaven first. It truly is a great place to live out your golden years.

reviews.author: Lynn Herod
reviews.text: I absolutely love this community and the staff! The building is so clean and beautiful inside. It offers a history like no other community and a step back in time. I love the way Fairhaven feels inside and outside. Robyn, Georgina, and Brittany truly care for the residents and their families. All of the staff members are happy and greet everyone with a smile. They are very involved with the residents. If you are looking for an assisted living community, please visit Fairhaven and let Robyn show you how amazing it is.
