researchSummary: Verified residential assisted living facility in Denton via official website.

reviews.author: Chelsea McCurdy
reviews.text:
We are so incredibly grateful for the care and compassion shown by the staff at this assisted living community, especially Amanda. She truly went above and beyond for our family member.

Amanda treated her with so much dignity, gentleness, and kindness. She was attentive, patient, and always made sure she was as comfortable as possible and had everything she needed. You can tell this isn’t just a job for her, she genuinely cares, and that meant everything to our family.

She also took the time to communicate with us, reassure us, and help us understand what was happening, and brought us so much peace. We will never forget the compassion she showed.

The entire staff was wonderful, and the facility itself was clean, calm, and welcoming. We are forever thankful for the love and care our family member got here.

I would wholeheartedly recommend this community to anyone looking for a place where their loved one will be treated like family.

reviews.author: Allison Maurine
reviews.text: Joyful Journey was such an amazing home for my grandmother. Amanda is so on top of everything and works so hard to keep every aspect of her resident’s day-to-day needs met and their lives in perfect harmony. The staff is unmatched and take their caregiving duties very seriously and with so much pride and grace. We are so fortunate to have had so much love around my grandmother and I will be forever grateful for the dignity, comfort and peace they provided to her and to our family as she transitioned from this world.

name: Bellaire Residential Assisted Living and Memory Care

reviews.author: Martha Frantz
reviews.text: We had the pleasure of being a part of the Bellaire family for two years. It was a great experience. They took excellent care of our loved one. The place is clean, staff is caring and friendly and they always make sure the residents have fun and feel at home. I highly recommend checking them out.

reviews.author: Yvonne George DFW Realtor
reviews.text:
As we age, most of us fear loosing our independence and leaving the comforts of home and what that will look like. If we have aging parents we worry about what type of care they will receive and will they be attended to properly.

I had the pleasure of touring both of the Residential Assisted Living and Memory Care Homes with the owner Kimberly Traux and let me tell you, I have never been so thoroughly impressed!

If you or a family member are being faced with making some tough decisions and unsure of what the future holds do not hesitate to tour here! You will be pleasantly surprised and your search will be over!

Just a few of the highlights are:
✅ Licensed nurse on -site 7 days a week
✅ 1:4 caregiver/resident ratio
✅ Home Cooking daily
✅ Daily activities & wellness
(you can even have a relaxing massage)
✅ Round the clock CNA’s and Caregivers
✅ Spiritual Support

So thankful that these homes exist for our loved ones!

name: Brookdale Denton South
address: 2525 Lillian Miller Pkwy, Denton, TX 76210, USA

researchSummary: Verified Brookdale Denton South official page offering assisted living and memory care.

reviews.author: Pam VanZandt
reviews.text: My Mom at first went to Brookdale Denton North then moved to Brookdale Denton South. I cannot say enough about how great my experience has been and my Mom is very happy there other than wanting to return home. Any questions I’ve had rather I msg a Director, Kathy or Michelle, or the nurses, Heidi or Jana or Serena the girl you first met me and gave me a tour, all of them always answered back promptly which was so convenient and thoughtful! I had so many questions! I never realized how much they all have to do with not only the resident but with their family also! Any time I called or walked in the staff would say something comforting about how Mom was adjusting. Great experience and truly hope my Mom stays on.

reviews.author: Penny Parker Klostermann
reviews.text:
My dad lived in Brookdale the last weeks of his life. We moved him thinking he had more time. Unfortunately, his dementia spiraled down quickly. We were doing our best to get him on a medication to help his anxiety. The staff recognized the quick decline and were very supportive, hoping we could find the right medication. One evening his breathing became very labored and the nurse contacted Hospice immediately. Her quick action comforted us. Her kindness and caring calmed us. Hospice came and he passed peacefully late the next afternoon. It took time and work to move him for a short 3-week stay. We could look back and wish we hadn’t have moved him. Instead, we feel the timing was perfect. The staff was amazing through this time and showed true concern for our dad. We feel thankful and blessed that our dad spent his last days at Brookdale.
If Dad were writing this, he would give the food 5 stars. We give Brookdale 5 stars - all the way!!

reviews.author: Linda Woita
reviews.text: Although I don't live here myself, I have visited several times and have always been impressed. The staff is consistently kind, welcoming, and genuinely helpful. The community is bright, cheerful, and beautifully maintained, with updated décor that creates a warm and inviting atmosphere.

reviews.author: anna blalock
reviews.text: I lived here for a year now and so far the help has been wonderful! They are willing to help as much as they can. The food is very good and tasty! It looks very appetizing! The room are kept very clean. Lety and Monkia have done a wonderful job in keeping my room clean! We also have good entertaining which keeps everyone busy!

reviews.text: We had a wonderful mens breakfast. It was a special time to get better acquainted with the guys. The culinary staff prepared a great breakfast. reviews.author: E Caston
reviews.text:
I recently had the opportunity to visit Lake Forest and was very impressed with the community. The environment was welcoming, clean, and thoughtfully designed for residents' comfort and well-being.

What stood out most was the amazing staff. Everyone I met was friendly, professional, and genuinely passionate about providing quality care and support to the residents. Their dedication and compassion were evident in every interaction.

A special thank you to Sandy Raspberry for the invitation and warm hospitality during my visit. She made me feel welcome and took the time to share what makes this community so special.

If you are looking for a senior living community in the Denton area, Lake Forest is definitely worth considering. It was a pleasure to visit and learn more about the wonderful work they are doing.

reviews.author: Jim Travell, Sr.
reviews.text: My sister moved from Robson Ranch to the independent living at Denton Village and was there for a few years then transferred to Assisted living for a more detailed environment. From the moment we scheduled a tour with Maria Bundock the Assisted Living Manager we knew this was the right choice. Maria treated us as Family and assured us that everyone of my sister's needs would be handled as if my sister was her sister. Every time I visit I feel as if I am in a peaceful place. Each staff member greets you as you walk down the hallway making inquiry as to whether they can be of any value to my visit. The Nurse Loli is exceptionally engaging regarding any medications my sister might need. All in all we have found Denton Village to be a great place for my sister to call home with a Special acknowledgement to Maria and her staff at the Assisted Living environment.

reviews.author: Cheryl LaRose
reviews.text: My father and stepmother have lived in Denton Village a little over 2 years and I have had many opportunities to visit them there. I have found it a very welcoming place with a multitude of activities offered. The staff is friendly and seems to care greatly for the residents. I have heard from my family that the food there is really good and that they have a great chef. I hope I can find a facility near me with such a sense of community if and when I need one.

reviews.text: Carriage House has been a mainstay here in Denton providing quality care. Not only do they take care of their residents, they also support the community. They just donated a wonderful door prize for the TWU social work graduation banquet. Thank you!

reviews.author: Michelle Rudek
reviews.text: This place is a hidden gem! My Mom loves her apartment, it’s spacious and clean. The staff is very friendly, professional and take excellent care of my Mother. Most importantly, the food is AMAZING! Highly recommend.

reviews.author: David L
reviews.text:
My Mother had a stroke that caused Dementia. The first place we went after the stroke was horrific. This is a level B assisted living facility. My mother had many problems when moving in both with memory and anxiety. The staff have been good about taking her specific issues into account and working to help her be her best self.
After the previous facility she had trust issues and was easily scared. In less than a year they have helped her to feel safe and comfortable. Her language skills and anxiety have massively improved.
Management has been incredibly responsive to questions and concerns that are brought up. The staff are friendly and seem to really care about helping.
This place has been a God send for both me and my Mother. She feels safe, and I feel like she's safe.
We both sleep better at night knowing that she's in good hands.

reviews.author: C A.D
reviews.text:
Went to do a tour of the facility 9/6/25 with family and my mom (the client) and just walking to the entrance we did not have a good feeling about the facility. Front porch entrance decor was thrown on ground and pillows all over. Ac and windows were old and rusted. The intercom was "on" from the outside and we could hear loud static, banging and talking coming from inside the building. We rang the doorbell 4x and no answer. We had to knock loudly 3x and then a frazzled young woman came to the door finally.
We sat and discussed our main top requirements and she was the new sales manager.. of Both North and South facilities. She did not have much info at all. Kept saying "Im not sure of that but I can ask someone" (Is she the one to ask?!? :/ ) Other workers interrupted her during our meeting also not knowing where things were. The staff all seems to do 2 or 3 different jobs which is not a good look. Transportation and outings for residents are only 1 day a week and ONLY if someone is available to drive. ?!? For $4500 a month, the amenities are verryy bad in our opinion compared to other Denton facilities and we will keep searching for better well managed, friendly and clean facility. We felt uncomfortable and didn't even take the tour and left. Visit at your own risk. Would Not recommend.

reviews.author: Karen Santilli
reviews.text: My husband and I have lived here for 5 years. We moved from Carrrollton TX. We truly enjoy living here due to it feeling like we live in a home. No one living above or beneath you and this is a very quiet and peaceful property. We have such good neighbors here. Everyone is friendly and speaks to you and waves as you drive or walk by. We also look out for each other and help each other when needed.. We do have a good management and maintenace team now. If you are looking for a nice senior active community. You will enjoy living here.

reviews.author: Eveda S.
reviews.text: Just recently celebrated my 5 year anniversary here at Sunstone. Before I even moved to this community, I prayed that I would be surrounded by friendly, kind and caring neighbors. i must admit that I haven't been disappointed in the least. As a neighbor and Tai Chi participant here at the clubhouse recently admitted to me 'We're a family here at Sunstone', and I can't deny that he's right. We do look out for each other and question each others absence whenever we come together at the clubhouse for various activities each week. To boot, I've never felt more cared for by any management team than I have with our current staff. Thus far during their one year+ with us they have strived to resolve any issues that have befallen us as speedily as possible. Our wonderful Receptionist and Assist Manager, Linn, is a true God send. There isn't anything she wouldn't do to help us . She's always cheery and upbeat whenever we meet, whether in the clubhouse or on the grounds. This team has been so inspiring that late last year in 2025 a staff appreciation party planned and paid for by the residents, was held in their honor. i look forward to having them here with us for many years to come. When I sit on my patio with my little furry friend, the neighbors and staff passing by whether on foot or driving, wave hello. The cottage feel and grounds here. is to me, a great alternative when downsizing from a private residence. Thus far, I've no regrets but wish I'd chosen this place 10 years ago after my early retirement.

reviews.author: KJ
reviews.text: Welcoming community with many activities and clubs. Very clean and well kept community. Before considering to build, be aware of the dangerous and overwhelming amount of traffic to get to the community-traffic that is only going to get worse as more development takes place along Robson Ranch Road. Very disappointing that the County and State has allowed the development to occur without addressing traffic issues. Would not recommend living here, until the traffic issues are addressed.

reviews.text: This is haves down the best 55+ active community around. The stunning grounds, friendly atmosphere, and state of the art facilities are quite impressive. The amenities, staff, and the ability to “try before you buy” is very appealing. We had the pleasure of taking a tour and dinning at their country club.

Serious Concerns Regarding Fraudulent Activity by Staff Member

I had an alarming experience with Mr. Stephen Temidayo Olowoyeye , a staff member at Denton State Supported Living (Project Management Specialist).

I believe I was scammed by him regarding a financial transaction, in which he took the money I paid him and failed to deliver the packages, and stopped picking my calls.

This has caused significant distress, and I feel it is important for the management to be made aware of the situation.

I’ve tried to resolve the matter directly, but I am deeply concerned that the issue may be more widespread or not fully addressed. It is critical for the safety and trust of those involved with this facility that these types of incidents are investigated promptly.

I hope management will take swift action to investigate this matter thoroughly and address it accordingly as it is critical to ensure the integrity of the workers employed.

Please take this review seriously as it reflects a deeply troubling experience that I hope can be resolved for the well-being of everyone involved.

reviews.author: Belinda Rudinger
reviews.text: My mother and I were so blessed to find Autumn Oaks! She had a beautiful year there before her passing. After two hospitalizations and two stays in physical rehabilitation facilities, Autumn Oaks was a breath of fresh air. Mom was always happy there, and always told me how nice everyone always was to her. She even sent me pictures of her pancakes with a smiley face! They were truly like a family to her, and to me. It's hard to capture all the details that made it feel like home. The welcoming foyer was always decorated for the season, with relaxing and nostalgic music playing. The small number of residents meant that they truly individualized her care, recognizing her unique mobility needs and adapting as needed. The leadership and caregivers were consistent, with very little turnover. People were promoted from within, so everyone knew the residents well. I visited twice a week, and always felt a sense of peace and tranquility there. I had worked as a caregiver in an assisted living facility in college, and had a bad experience, which had made me very nervous about trusting people with my mom. I'm so glad we took a chance on Autumn Oaks, and that they showed me how amazing assisted living can truly be. I still miss driving by the beautiful duck pond and dropping in for a visit. I will forever be grateful to their staff for the care and memories.

reviews.author: TJ S.
reviews.text: Julie and the staff at Autumn Oaks are great people who have a heart for caring for seniors. If you’re looking for a quiet community with some great, affordable options for both assisted and independent living, this is the place.

reviews.author: s wotipka
reviews.text:
Placing my father into a residential care facility was a tough decision for our family. However, within minutes of my father arriving at Selah Ridge, I knew we had made the perfect choice. We wholeheartedly recommend Selah Ridge to anyone seeking an exceptionally well run and caring facility for their loved ones.

We visited frequently and Selah Ridge provided a welcoming, extremely clean and well run environment. Rhonda and her staff focused on the things that matter, big and small. If my father wanted to watch a baseball game on tv, they made sure the tv was set to the proper channel. Because Dad could be a picky eater, they made sure he could choose items that he wanted to eat and that made him happy. They made sure he was always comfortable, mentally and physically.

Many thanks to Rhonda and her staff for the exceptional care they provided to my father before his passing. we will be eternally grateful to them.

Don

reviews.author: Bonnie Solomon
reviews.text: I had a good friend that was lucky enough to live out her last few years at this wonderful place. Every time I visited (I dropped in unannounced semi-regularly) she was clean, happy, content and obviously very well taken care of and loved. I cannot recommend this establishment enough. Ronda (R.N.) was a loving, involved, conscientious caregiver to my friend and I will always appreciate it. Also, that whole house is kept spotless and odorless, as are the residents. I can only hope to end up in this situation if I live long enough.

reviews.author: Donna Stewart
reviews.text: Living Well Senior Care has been providing health care services for my elderly cousins for the past 3 years or so, including 24 hour care for about a 2 1/2 month period. This took so much effort on their part and we never had a time without care. They continue to do a tremendous job of providing such good care for both of them. The specific caregiver we have had for most of this time is an absolute jewel and we all just love her. They are very comfortable with her and she provides them with companionship as well. I would highly recommend Living Well to anyone in need of their services. The management staff is great to work with and are always available to assist you with any questions or needs that you may have.

reviews.author: Amy Holmes
reviews.text: I hired Living Well Senior Care to help my elderly step-father who is in hospice at home. I can't say enough positive things about Living Well Senior Care. The management was extremely responsive to my initial request, and they really worked with me to identify needs and level of service initially for my step-father, and now for my mother as well. The Caregivers are very skilled, pleasant, and they really care and take pride in the services they provide. They provide a "family portal" website where I can login and see the caregiver's notes. This ensures transparency and good communication. I'm also impressed with the prompt and accurate billing. I highly recommend Living Well Senior Care!

reviews.author: Kay Peddy
reviews.text: The staff at Denton Rehab were very professional and kind. Irene (head nurse), in particular, was very knowledgeable and friendly in all our encounters. Beautiful facility, but the practical use of space for rehabilitation was not very well executed in my humble opinion. The only caveat to a glowing (5-star) review is the fact that it was extremely difficult to get through on the phone to talk with staff concerning admitted loved one.

reviews.author: P Pfaff-Duca
reviews.text:
My family’s experience with Denton Rehab was very disappointing overall. While the Director of Nursing was helpful, many other aspects of the stay fell far below expectations.

From day one, several important issues communicated at intake were never addressed. There was no coordination of care between the various doctors, which made it difficult to get consistent information or a clear plan. Communication was challenging throughout — phone calls and emails often went unanswered.

The staff consistently appeared spread thin, leaving too much work for too few people, and it showed in the quality of care. Most concerning, the patient left the facility with a wound that occurred under their care and also developed a UTI during their stay. These are preventable issues that should not happen with proper attention and staffing.

Additionally, the rehab services were billed as one hour per session, five days a week, but actual therapy time was closer to 30 minutes per session. This discrepancy added to our frustration and concern about the level of care being provided.

Based on our experience, I cannot recommend this facility and hope they make serious improvements for future patients.

name: Vintage Health Care Center
address: 205 N Bonnie Brae St, Denton, TX 76201, USA

reviews.author: Chasity Pollina
reviews.text: Let me start by saying that I’m an RN that worked in the operating room. I have not worked in a facility such as Vintage but the care here is subpar. I would never recommend this facility to anyone. My father was placed here for rehab post surgery. He was dealing with dementia and Parkinson’s prior to the surgery. We were concerned for his post op care and made the educated decision to place him in rehab. This was the worst mistake. He had trouble feeding himself, wore diapers, and couldn’t walk post surgery. Vintage did not help offer him food or fluids. I know a patient can refuse things but we have it on camera that it was not offered. He lost over 20lbs in two weeks and became severely dehydrated with acute kidney injury from the dehydration. This reduced his kidney function by 70%. After that we moved him and placed him on hospice. Let me make it clear that his quality of life prior to surgery was declining however he was still able to walk, eat slowly, enjoy some of his favorite drinks, and enjoy time with family. He has since passed and I feel Vintage accelerated his medical decline. I know it was coming naturally but they are to blame for the accelerated timeline of his death. Please protect your loved ones from this facility.

reviews.author: Hudson
reviews.text: Independently dependent. Being paralyzed from the chest down I am dependent upon others to get out of bed, in the shower, dressed and in my wheelchair every morning. Skilled nursing is also needed daily. Well this morning.. it was a great team effort timed perfectly. Starting with CeeCee. She was a hard drivin', bed makin', hard workin', happy smilin', shower slingin' and hoyer haulin'machine!! She also had Angela, the wound care nurse lined up, immediately after my shower (which is the key to me getting up before lunchtime). The "calm as a cucumber" Angela had me patched up with pride w 40 minutes to spare. Within 15 minutes, in comes the one and only positive and powerful heartbreaker "cor-yVETTE"who handled another necessity and finallyl CeeCee,(Jessica's lil sis - obviously beauty and smiles run in the family) showed right back up and finished the job of readying me for my day by lifting me into my motorized wheelchair just in time to enjoy some meatloaf and Texas longhorn softball. Credit where credit's DUE, TO all of YOU, Thank YOU, DREW and YOU TOO Miss Shenise. 🌄🧡✝️🤠😃🤣😂

reviews.author: Deanie Martino
reviews.text:
When my husband became very ill, we hired Heaven at Home — and I truly don’t know how we would have managed without them.

They have supported us in so many meaningful ways, especially with the daily challenges that come with caring for someone who is incapacitated. The practical help alone has been a tremendous relief, but what has impressed me even more is their thoughtfulness and professionalism.

Collette and Sarah take the time to meet with me regularly to assess our changing needs. When Collette came to check on us, she had clearly done her homework. She understood David’s specific challenges and arrived prepared with ideas and suggestions for how her staff could better

support his therapy goals. That level of preparation and care meant so much to me.

I have also been deeply grateful for their excellent communication. I never have to worry about who will be in our home or whether everyone is on the same page. That peace of mind is priceless.

I truly cannot say enough good about this group. They have made these past three months not only manageable, but far more doable than I ever imagined during such a difficult season.

We are so thankful for Heaven at Home and the compassionate, capable people who serve there.

reviews.author: Crystal Ashcraft
reviews.text:
I highly recommend Heaven at Home for anyone seeking compassionate, dependable home care services. Their team is dedicated to providing exceptional support & truly puts the needs of their clients & families first.

I would especially like to recognize Collette, who recently went above & beyond for one of our mutual patients. Her compassion, professionalism & attention to detail are truly remarkable. She took the time to ensure every need was met & every concern was addressed, providing comfort & peace of mind during an important time.

I am confident referring patients to this team because I know they will receive outstanding care. It is a pleasure to partner with an organization that shares the same commitment to serving others with dignity, respect & excellence.

I hate to leave a negative review, but I feel management needs to be aware of a concerning experience I recently had with Cottonwood Transportation.

Unfortunately, I did not catch the female driver’s name, but the experience was concerning enough that I felt it needed to be reported. The driver was highly unprofessional, and more importantly, I felt unsafe during the trip. The driving was erratic enough that I found myself holding on to my seat and belongings throughout the ride. What should have been a routine transportation service became a very uncomfortable and stressful experience.

I had heard that improvements were being made to the transportation program, which gave me hope. Unfortunately, this experience has had the opposite effect and has made me hesitant to use the service again.

I am sharing this feedback because I believe management should be aware of the situation and take the necessary steps to ensure the safety and comfort of residents and passengers. Safety should always be the top priority.

reviews.text: Their drivers need to be more aware of their surroundings. They shouldn’t have pulled out in front of me. There wasn’t time for them to do so and I almost rear ended them. reviews.author: Shelley Payton
reviews.text: Sodalis / Flower Mound was the first assisted living facility my husband and I toured when searching for a home for his stepmother. We were immediately impressed with the cozy, homey atmosphere, the cleanliness, and various staff we interacted with. Every other facility we toured did not come close to comparing with Sodalis, and we moved my mother-in-law in three weeks ago. I have had a lot of exposure to these types of facilities: my stepfather lived in several over the years. In my mind, the key piece of the puzzle in this kind of environment is the Executive Director. Ms Darla at Sodalis is just the sort of person and professional one wants when making such a major life decision. She is warm, responsive, fun, and most importantly, she is "hands-on." She's not sitting in an office doing paperwork. It is clear she cares about her residents as people. When you have good management at the top, the team beneath is stronger, happier, more efficient, and more effective. And such is the case at Sodalis. Yes, the rooms are nice. Yes, the food is tasty. Yes, the activities are varied and fun. And yes, the pricing is very reasonable. All of that is important. However, if the top management is lacking, all of those selling points, in my opinion, become moot. Ms Darla's heart and soul are invested daily, and it shows. We are happy that my mother-in-law is happy; it is such a relief. But most of all, we are thankful and grateful for Ms Darla, Tim, Tabitha, and the rest of the staff, for their dedication and attention---and we rest easy knowing our family member is in excellent hands while under their care.

reviews.author: Phyllis Lund
reviews.text:
Update January 2026: Sodalis has installed a new Executive Director and after a month, changes have been overwhelmingly positive. Staff has now changed over nearly 100%, but the new employees are courteous, caring and attentive. They actually come check on me regularly and respond to call button requests. Chef is excellent as well. The new management team is clearly putting in lots of effort and it shows.

I have been a resident here for 3 months. This is my first experience with assisted living.

Understand that these places start with a basic rent (room, food, utilities, housekeeping, laundry). Beyond that, there are a number of “levels of care,” each one adding an additional monthly cost in tiers.

I was specifically told that without tiers of service, they would still “assist” me with small tasks. In fact, I was even given a push/call button that I can wear around my neck.

Since being there, I have required various minor assistance with things (cpap machine comes unplugged, minor cut/ help with bandaid, broken chair- all things that would take not more than 5 minutes). With the exception of some wonderful employees, often the staff doesn’t respond to the call button at all, or when they do, they are rude or angry that I have bothered them. Even the director was now saying that “you aren’t supposed to get any assistance since you aren’t paying for a tier of service.”

So my family then moved me onto the first tier of service which included them managing my meds, and was supposed to guarantee assistance as mentioned above. The very first day (hours after we went over the meds schedule), all of my meds were withheld (employee said that “no instructions had been left so no meds for you”). The following day they tried to give me someone else’s meds. I also noticed that the staff still doesn’t come when I press the button- even when I had cut my leg and was bleeding. The director says that they are under staffed and they are “too busy with other residents to help you.” We have since removed me from the level one tier of service.

Speaking of staff- I want to emphasize that there are some truly wonderful people here, but also some that are rude and uncaring. Also, there is tremendous turnover. Within 2 months, they have lost the activities person, head medical person, head cook, maintenance person and more. Perhaps this is indicative of this industry?

Residents here are fantastic. Their friendship and the caring employees make the difference. I just wish management hadn’t promised more than they planned to deliver. Lower expectations would have made this transition easier.

For those looking to put your parents into assisted living for the first time, I hope this review will give you questions to ask. “Assisted” at least with respect to Sodalis is more of a marketing promise and certainly not a practice- even when on a paid “tier of service.” Proceed with caution and ask lots of questions.

reviews.author: Mandy Collura
reviews.text:
I DO NOT recommend Longmeadow Healthcare Center to anyone considering care for a loved one.

When my grandfather was first admitted for skilled nursing rehab, the staff initially appeared attentive, kind, and welcoming. Unfortunately, that level of care did not last beyond the first night. Call lights routinely went unanswered for over an hour, with little awareness or communication about patient needs.

My grandfather arrived with a catheter and consistently complained of pain. Each time, he was dismissed and told it was “normal.” After a later hospital visit, we learned he had not been properly cleaned and had developed an open, bleeding sore. There were no doctors on staff, and the physician assistant spent only a few minutes with him during visits, often seeming unfamiliar with his chart and unable to answer basic questions. Some staff spoke to residents in a way that felt demeaning and lacking in respect.

The facility appeared severely understaffed. The employees present seemed overworked, and despite being there almost daily advocating for my grandfather, I was repeatedly told, “I’ll let the Director of Nursing know,” with no meaningful follow-up or improvement.

What ultimately led us to remove him was the lack of urgency when his condition declined. On March 23rd, I noticed extreme fatigue and dark urine and raised concerns about a possible infection. I was told a UTI test would be done. By March 25th, his condition had worsened significantly. He was confused, hallucinating, and not making sense. At that point, I was told no sample had even been taken.

On March 26th, I arrived to find his catheter filled with blood. I demanded immediate action. While staff acknowledged it could be a serious infection, they were unable to start an IV and instead called an external team located over an hour away. We waited eight hours while his condition continued to deteriorate, and no one arrived. I ultimately insisted they call 911.

When emergency responders arrived, the sudden shift in staff behavior felt more like a performance than genuine concern. Since leaving in the ambulance, no one from the facility has reached out.

My grandfather passed away three weeks later from complications related to that infection.

We have filed a report with Adult Protective Services. In my opinion, this facility needs a full investigation. Please think very carefully before trusting this place with someone you love.

The recent change in ownership and front office personnel has certainly had a negative impact on its residents. I once enjoyed the lively and welcoming atmosphere felt as a volunteer since its initial opening as the Mariposa at Westchester 55+ Apartment Homes.

For the past three years , I served as a volunteer teacher for weekly line dancing and water aerobics classes. These classes encouraged memory training , mobility , balance, and flexibility for the body , and served as an enjoyable experience for residents. Most importantly, it gave residents a sense of overall wellness and community belonging. My recent decision to discontinue (as of June 2025) my volunteer services under the current management stems from what has become a common practice:

1. No one in the front office (routinely closed during business hours) to answer questions when potential residents dropped in to make inquiries. I or participants in my classes would have to stop to answer questions about the whereabouts of the front office employees.
2. I’ve listened to shared complaints by both current and past residents about ongoing issues and concerns
(delayed apartment repairs , car thefts due to the ever broken security gates, no or excessively late access to the community pool during the summer months , unfair community gardening restrictions, parking issues, and the loss of social activities once enjoyed by residents) with the new management . The common feelings by residents are that their concerns were met with unprofessional and uncaring attitudes.

The once lively and positive atmosphere within this residential environment has certainly changed for the worse as reflected by the high turnover of long term residents leaving in droves keeps increasing. Unfortunately, this has led to my no longer wanting to volunteer my services in this type of community environment.

reviews.text: I am very disappointed with the fact you would have an emergency call line for maintenance when your A/C goes out and not one person take the time out to call . I looked up at the thermostat and it read 80 degrees so I made a call for someone to come check it and that was before 6pm , never received a call or text , time went on and it was 11:07 pm and 83 degrees in here . I called again. I don’t know what they considered a emergency with the A/C , however some people suffer with nose bleed when overheated , asthma and headache and what may not be a emergency or problem for maintenance is a concern for me. Here it’s 2:05 am and I’m awake while my fan is tossing around heat . This is a major problem and concern for me and I’m not at all happy with this. No one wants to sit up in restless and tired because of a lack of air conditioning. We are still in some of the hottest days . I don’t call or bother maintenance for anything I stay to myself. If the after hour service isn’t going to work to take care of your needs what’s the sense of having to call for broken A/C units. Now I have to wait and lay awake until the office opens . Get more maintenance men. It’s not fair to me as a tenant to lay here in the heat .

reviews.author: Megan Furay
reviews.text: I had the privilege of touring this community for my dad today. Transitions at this age aren't easy and my dad doesn't like change. But after walking through with Michael, meeting Liz, the director and Brittany the activities director, there was no doubt that my dad would be genuinely cared for here. I appreciated that they have all levels of care to meet my dad's needs wherever he is. The community was breathtaking. They even had a swimming pool! But what stands apart, aside from the warmth of those in leadership roles, was witnessing the smiles of the residents, hearing the laughter in the community areas and having a newly moved in resident stop me and say that he is so grateful and happy they found this place for his dad. And then I got to see his dad- 80 something years old in the exercise room, grinning from ear to ear. Seeing and feeling the joy and warmth here brings peace to my heart when I consider the future care of my dad. Thank yall for taking the time to show me around, I wish I was old enough to come live with all the cool kids!

reviews.author: Scott Williams
reviews.text:
Legacy Oaks has been a Godsend for my family! I moved my parents from out of state over two years ago and over that time we've seen a few different iterations of the facility and staff. From both parent living in independent together to having to separate them due to the health of one parent and have one parent in independent and one parent in assisted living, the Legacy Oaks team was with our family each step of the way! The attention, support, care, guidance and partnership from every person at the campus from Justin all the way down to the housekeepers, I couldn't ask for a better group of people to watch over, love and care for my parents! The nursing staff and caregivers are the best in the business hands down! I've told them a million times they are "Angels on Earth" and have a special gift from God! The food services group led by a wonderful human named John always add a little spice of love to each meal they serve! The special care they gave to my dad and his special diet will never be forgotten. John always turned a puree diet into a Michelin 5 star meal each day!

Even though its beautiful living center from inside and out with many great amenities, its the people that make it a special place! After the passing of my dad to see the love, support and compassion the others who live at Legacy have shown my mom I couldn't say "Thank You" enough! They adopted her into their games, puzzles, meals and activities, they have made the transition to being a widow after 63 years of marriage doable and given her a new outlook on life! Love is felt from the second you walk in the doors of the facility! As someone who has managed Corporate facilities for over 30 years you can't just create that kind of magic!

In closing, if your looking at Legacy Oaks as a home for yourself or someone you love you can't and will not go wrong with that decision! I would make that decision again 10 out of 10 times! If I could give more than 5 stars I would have without any hesitation!

reviews.text: I have taken care of my disabled sister for over 20 years. Through those years we have been through many trials and the latest is her inability to walk after a knee replacement. She has been there almost a year now and I have nothing but good things to say about the standard of care and service she has received. The staff is extremely accommodating and the Executive Director, Landon and Nursing Director, DJ, have always made sure that she had everything she needed. I cannot thank this facility enough for making my life so much easier and giving me the assurance and comfort of knowing that my sister is in good hands. My last comment is that you need to notice the negative reviews are from years ago! Do not hold the current management responsible for what happened 4 - 6 years ago. You will not be disappointed with choosing Cedar Hill Senior Living as a place of residency for your loved one! Bravo Mr. Landon and staff!

The new executive director came in and told us that my mom should have never been moved here as they’re not staffed to provide the care that my mom needs. The assistant request pull string in my moms room has not been working since mid Jan but the faculty refuses to fix the pull string. They have asked my mom to call the main number when she needs assistance. My mom usually has to call several times as the staff rarely answer the phone. The vmail still has the name of the former executive director, even though the new director has been here for 2 weeks, and is full so messages cannot be left. There are too many violations to list. I would highly recommend skipping this facility if your looking for a place to care for your love one.

reviews.author: Leta Albrecht
reviews.text: I contacted Griswold in need of care for my father. I related how very important it was for me to have professional, reliable aids to help us care for my father who lives in our home. I was greatly distressed when in one week, not one, not two, but three no shows. No communication was given to us to inform us of the aids not coming as scheduled. This was greatly distressing to us as a family who very much need assistance. I contacted Mike the owner, who he himself was a no show on our first appointment, and related our dissatisfaction. His initial no show should have been an indicator but I gave grace knowing things happen. To sum up our experience in one week I had a 75% no show rate which is unacceptable. reviews.author: Doug and Be Anderson
reviews.text:
Assisted living was new for me to research for my wife to enter into hospice AND assisted living at the same time. I visited a larger facility and realized I wanted a more private setting. I visited 3 facilities and there was absolutely only one choice for me, Hillside! It is a privately owned facility in a quiet neighborhood.

The staff make it what it is. A home, a family, home-cooked (really good) meals. The kindness and care there was like nothing I have ever seen. My wife required a lot of specialized attention with her condition and I would go home at night and just be amazed at how comfortable she was, knowing she was being taken care of fully.

Durenda, Heather and Rose run the home very well. They will not tolerate staff that do not bring the best of care. I could visit anytime, eat with them, sit at the table, etc. They became my family too!

While my wife was not there very long, every day and hour counted. I can say that Hillside made her feel her very best, and now that she is home in heaven, I am sure she is looking out for Hillside staff every day as well!

reviews.author: Janet Okamura
reviews.text:
Mom was at Hillside for almost 2 years. The atmosphere was completely different ( in a good way) than the other larger places she had been in over the years. It was like she was at home again where she could sit at the kitchen table, pretty much have whatever she wanted, and visit with the caretakers while they were preparing the meals. She improved physically, emotionally and spiritually in this peaceful setting.
The staff was incredible, especially toward the end. They loved on her, doted on her, prayed with her and even ate late night snacks with her, sometimes with a movie! They developed a very close relationship with her and our family. We learned a lot from them on how to love the elderly and also developed a bond with the families of the other residents. Even when mom went through spells of not being able to communicate they were able to get her to joke around with them, bringing out her old self that we missed. We have seen a lot of caregivers through the years but this crew is the best!
The director, Durenda, is amazing! Seriously, she gives her everything to the residents and the staff. She is a national treasure! If the caregivers do not take their job seriously she will let them go. (Which is why you might see a disgruntled employee review).
We honestly could not of asked for a better place for mom. God blessed us with peace of mind knowing mom was safe and well cared for at Hillside until He called her home.

reviews.author: Karen Kiechler
reviews.text: Elba yanez is the most special person and CNA, she shows sincerity in her work, is gentle and patient, gives thorough care, looks out for everyone’s safety, and is very kind. She transported me from my home to Heritage House of Keller and was so good at getting me on the van and off the van and to my room. I can not say enough wonderful and good things about her and her exceptional work. I am an RN and have been a DON at several SNF and rehab facilities and I would hire many aides and caregivers that had her personality work ethics . She is the BEST PERSON AND CNA. I want to make sure that her bosses know what a special person she is. !!!!!!!! Sincerely, Karen Kiechler, RN

reviews.author: Pat Fincher
reviews.text: Father in law spent 3 weeks at HH of Keller. He said the aides/ nurses were real nice and the therapist was nice. Being a diabetic was challenging here. Inconsistent blood sugar checks and inconsistent medication administration times. Would receive insulin after he ate instead of before. Thankfully he wore a glucose monitor and would call us when his sugar was close to 400 and we would run up there to see that it was addressed. Getting a call light answered took an act of congress. Maybe short staffed? No diabetic diet offered and he rarely received what he actually ordered to eat. On 2 separate nights, his protein was one small chicken wing. He got breathing treatments but never would come back to remove nebulizer mask. There was no communication with the family in the form of a care conference, etc. the only time we received a call was when I requested to speak to someone and they did respond and they were nice. The best thing was that it was close to our house so we could run over easily to see him.
